A collector must also declare when it reads a root-only file of /proc (proc_files), needs a capability (capabilities), or connects to a socket of another service's group (groups). Every collector of the exporter's packages does this. To check a collector of another package, run prometheus-exporter collector check (from ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli). See Collector interface. - The collector API is prometheus.exporter, and collectors are in /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/collectors/. The exporter's modules moved from /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/ to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/: - The collector API, prometheus_exporter.api, is now prometheus.exporter, with the same names. - The exporter's own modules and the devkit's are prometheus.exporter.<module>. - The collectors are prometheus.collectors.<module>.

    The upgrade removes every file the exporter's packages installed under the old directory. The exporter reads its collectors from the new directory alone. A collector of another package stays where its package installed it, in /usr/share/ucode/prometheus_exporter/collectors/. The exporter does not load or list it until you rebuild its package for 0.3.0 and install it again.

    In the collector's source, rename the module, its tests, its utest config and its Makefile, and move the module to src/prometheus/collectors/:

    grep -rlZ --exclude-dir=.git prometheus_exporter . | xargs -0 sed -i -e 's/prometheus_exporter\.api/prometheus.exporter/g' -e 's#prometheus_exporter\([./]\)collectors#prometheus\1collectors#g' -e 's#prometheus_exporter\([./]\)#prometheus\1exporter\1#g' --
mkdir -p src/prometheus && git mv src/prometheus_exporter/collectors src/prometheus/

    The metric names, ucode_prometheus_exporter_*, do not change. See How to write a collector in your own package. - A collector's top level may only declare. The top level runs again in uhttpd's own process each time the service starts, and nothing can stop it there. So, both there and in the child process that first loads the collector, the exporter refuses a top level that calls any of these, before the call runs: - sleep, exit, print, printf, warn, trace, require, include, loadfile, loadstring, render or signal - the collector API's exposition functions

    The exporter then leaves the collector out and logs COLLECTOR_IMPURE at err. Every collector of the exporter's packages only declares. For a collector of another package, move the work its top level does into collect(). Check it with prometheus-exporter collector check (from ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli), which now also looks for statements and calls past the declarations. See Collector interface.

These changes differ from 0.2.1 without breaking a query or a configuration:

  • ethtool runs ethtool three times per device: -S, -i and with no option. It ran it once before. The two new runs feed node_exporter's node_ethtool_info and link families. The three runs share the seconds of the collector's timeout, which defaults to the main section's exec_timeout, 5. On a slow router with many ports, if ethtool fails with COMMAND_TIMEOUT, give it more time. See How to give programs more time.
  • The filesystem package installs an rpcd plugin, the ubus object prometheus-exporter.filesystem. The plugin answers each mount's type, read-only flag, sizes and inodes. The package reloads rpcd when you install or remove it. Only the collector calls the plugin. The service's user may no longer call rpcd's file read or luci's getMountPoints. Where rpcd has not loaded the plugin, the collector fails and says so, until you run /etc/init.d/rpcd reload.

  • wifi, hostapd_stations, timesync and wireguard's peer_names ask the service's own ubus object, prometheus-exporter. They ask it for:

    • the radios, without their keys (wireless)
    • whether ntpd and chronyd run (time_daemons)
    • the peers' descriptions (wireguard_peers)

    The service's user may no longer call netifd's network.wireless status, procd's service list or rpcd's uci get. Those answer every Wi-Fi key, every service's command line and any config. A collector of another package may still call one of them, by declaring it, while that collector is enabled. See About the security model. - OpenWrtWifiRadioDown fires for a radio that is enabled and not up. It uses wifi's new node_wifi_radio_up and node_wifi_radio_disabled. Before, it fired for any radio without a network, including one disabled on purpose. If you copied the old rule, copy the new one from monitoring/prometheus/router.rules.yml. - Two new collectors, each in its own package, which no group installs: pressure (pressure stall information) and interrupts. pressure needs a kernel with CONFIG_PSI, which OpenWrt's kernels leave off. To use one, install its package: apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-pressure. See How to choose collectors. - LuCI changes basic auth's password with its own button, Change password…, on the HTTPS & login tab. 0.2.1 had a field that Save handed on. The password still applies at once, separately from Save & Apply, and the dialog asks for it twice. Once you empty the user, Remove password removes the saved password. The app's ACL is unchanged. See How to use the LuCI app. - A collector that is refused something it needs fails with PERMISSION_DENIED, and says what grants it. Before, it would have reported nothing to observe. A reload grants again what the service granted at start and has since been taken away. - The exporter refuses, where it is written, text that would make Prometheus refuse a whole scrape: - a label named __name__, or any other label name that starts with __ - a NUL byte in a label value, a HELP text or a family's name

    textfile leaves out a *.prom file that has one and logs EXPOSITION_INVALID. A collector that writes one fails with that code. 0.2.1 served such text, and Prometheus then refused every collector's samples. - dhcp_leases and thermal each write one more family: - node_openwrt_dhcp_pool_size{interface}, the size of each interface's DHCPv4 pool - node_thermal_zone_critical_celsius{zone,type}, each zone's critical trip point, which the bundled alerts use

    See Metrics. - check shows the jail's user, its capabilities and its ubus ACL. The jail of the ubus object's describe lists each collector's calls, capabilities, groups and proc files.

docs.title: From 0.2.0 to 0.2.1
docs.text:
The changes below break something that worked in 0.2.0. The CHANGELOG marks each one BREAKING.

  • Basic auth's hash has its own config. The exporter reads auth_password from /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth, which the package installs with mode 0600. It no longer reads it from the main section of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, which LuCI's ACL lets a login read.

    • The upgrade moves a hash it finds in the main section, and logs auth_password moved from /etc/config/prometheus-exporter to /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth.
    • A script that sets the hash sets prometheus-exporter-auth.main.auth_password, or calls the ubus object's set_password.
    • check warns about a hash left in the main section. The exporter ignores it.
    • A hash without a user now means no basic auth, rather than an invalid configuration. validate no longer answers AUTH_NEEDS_USER.
    • LuCI's ACL grants password and set_password, and no longer hash_password.

    See How to serve HTTPS with basic auth. - textfile's directory must be under /var, /tmp or /etc/prometheus-exporter. The service creates and mounts no other directory. If yours is elsewhere, such as under /srv, move it before upgrading, or the service refuses the configuration (OWNED_DIRECTORY). - memory_limit takes 0, or 8 MB and more. Values 1 to 7 passed check, and uhttpd then crash-looped. The service now refuses them (ZERO_OR_MIN). - hostapd_stations labels each station's series by vif and station alone. ssid, bssid, encryption, frequency and channel are now only on the new hostapd_station_info, one series per station. A query that selected by them now joins it: hostapd_station_signal_dbm * on (vif, station) group_left (ssid) hostapd_station_info. - netstat exports only node_exporter's default fields, some 40 series where it wrote about 400. To export others, set its new option fields, a regular expression of <Section>_<Field>. .* exports every field, as 0.2.0 did:

    uci set prometheus-exporter.netstat=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.netstat.fields='.*'
uci commit prometheus-exporter

  • nat_traffic writes IPv6 addresses compressed: 2001:db8:0:1::e157, where it wrote 2001:0db8:0000:0001:0000:0000:0000:e157. Every other collector already labels them this way. A query or recording rule that matched the long form must match the short one now. The series start anew at the upgrade.

  • A collector passes its labels as an object, null, or what out.labels() made. A string of labels spliced by hand was written as it was. Now it fails the collector with EXPOSITION_INVALID. So does a label value that is not UTF-8, and two label names that become the same once sanitized. Every collector of the exporter's packages already complies. To check a collector of another package, run prometheus-exporter collector check.
  • The loader refuses a collector that calls system() or include(), as it already refused require. Run programs through deps.exec. See Collector contract.

These changes differ from 0.2.0 without breaking a configuration:

  • The jail has the ubus socket only while an enabled collector needs ubus. Take a collector of another package whose programs call ubus but whose meta.needs lacks ubus. When every collector that needs ubus is disabled, it finds no ubus. Declare ubus in its meta.needs.
  • uhttpd runs at most 3 requests at once, over at most 10 connections. Before, it used its defaults of 3 and 100. A client beyond those limits waits. One or two Prometheus servers need no more. See HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: From 0.1 to 0.2
docs.text:
0.2.0 changes what 0.1 did in these ways:

  • The command line takes subcommands. prometheus-exporter [COLLECTOR...] is now prometheus-exporter scrape [COLLECTOR...], and prometheus-exporter -l is now prometheus-exporter collector list. A script or cron job that runs the command needs the new form: see The prometheus-exporter command.
  • wifi_stations is gone. It wrote the same families as wifi's option stations, so each station was exported twice. Before the upgrade, remove it with apk del ucode-prometheus-exporter-wifi_stations. Then install ucode-prometheus-exporter-wifi if it is not there: its stations option is on by default.
  • A collector's package no longer installs what it watches. The packages of the mwan3, chrony, modemmanager, ubnt-manager and wireguard collectors depended on mwan3, chrony, modemmanager, ubnt-manager and rpcd-mod-wireguard. So installing the mwan3 collector installed and started mwan3, which changes the routing, and the chrony collector installed a second NTP daemon. Now they depend on none of these. Where the watched program is absent, the collector has nothing to observe. The upgrade removes nothing, because apk keeps what was installed. If you installed one only for its collector, remove it (apk del mwan3, for example).
  • A collector imports the collector API alone. A collector module imports prometheus_exporter.api, which exports Result, errors, services, proc and exposition, and no other module. The exporter leaves out a collector that imports prometheus_exporter.result, fs or any other module, and logs it at err. Every collector of the exporter's packages already complies. If a collector of another package was written for 0.1, change it to take the same names from the API: import { Result, errors, proc } from 'prometheus_exporter.api';, and proc.first_line(...) for first_line(...). Check it with prometheus-exporter collector check. See Collector contract.
  • A collector's options need a title. Each option of meta.options declares title, the short, sentence-case label that LuCI's Edit dialog shows: device_exclude: { default: '...', title: 'Excluded devices', help: '...' }. The exporter leaves out a collector with an option that has no title, and logs it at err. Every collector of the exporter's packages has titles. See Collector interface.
  • The ubus object's validate answers codes. Each refused value used to be an English sentence. Now it is an object, { code, ...arguments, message }, whose message is the sentence, as { "code": "RANGE", "min": 1, "max": 65535, "value": 0, "message": "expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0" }. A script that reads the reply reads message, or the code: see ubus object. check, the log and the command line say what they said before.
  • A collector that breaks the collector contract fails alone. The exporter stops it at its budget, at its max_samples, or when it writes another collector's family. See Collector contract.

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep build_info
service prometheus-exporter check

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="..."} shows the new version. The upgrade restarts a running service and leaves /etc/config/prometheus-exporter as you had it. If you changed that file, apk may put the new version's file beside it, as /etc/config/prometheus-exporter.apk-new. Compare the two, take what you want, then remove the .apk-new file.

docs.title: How to Run the Benchmark
docs.text: The benchmark times each collector, and whole scrapes, on generated worlds. A world is what a router's /proc, /sys, ubus, netlink and programs would give. Run the benchmark to see what a change costs. You can run it here, in a container limited like a slower router, on a device, or in QEMU as a MIPS router.

docs.title: In the development environment
docs.text:
make bench

It prints a table, writes bin/bench/devenv.json, and checks the budgets in test/bench/budgets.uc. It always checks the scaling and memory budgets, and also the time budgets when the container is unconstrained. CI runs the same.

The cases, by prefix. A "budget" is a limit in test/bench/budgets.uc that fails the run when exceeded.

  • scrape: runs each collector in a child process, as the service does. Its inline: twin runs them all in the scrape's own process. The difference is what that containment costs, and a budget holds it.

  • handler: is the scrape as Prometheus gets it. The benchmark starts uhttpd with the service's handler (test/bench/handler.uc, which makes the collectors read the world) and asks it with wget. So the case also counts the request's process, the ledger, the progress file and the deadline. Its note gives:

    • what the scrape takes besides its collectors (outside, leaving out wget's own time), which a budget holds
    • the descriptors and memory of the uhttpd process

    It runs where uhttpd and its ucode plugin are installed and can find this exporter. In the container, make bench links the source tree into /usr/share/ucode. QEMU's guest has the packages installed. - load: and probe:full load the collectors as uhttpd does. probe: first loads each in a child process. Their note gives the descriptors that loading left open, which a budget also holds. - rest:base and rest:full measure what the handler's process holds once it has loaded a set, as uhttpd holds it for as long as it runs. That is its private memory (RssAnon), minus what it held before it compiled the handler's program. A budget holds it. - lazy: cases time what a process pays the first time it needs a module: - the exposition parser, which a scrape loads where a collector parses - zlib, ubus, rtnl and nl80211, which uhttpd loads when it starts, so a scrape no longer pays for them - floor:base and floor:full find the smallest memory_limit, in whole MB, under which uhttpd loads the handler with the set and a typical scrape has every collector succeed. Each of the processes is limited as procd limits the service's. A budget holds the result to memory_limit's minimum, 8 MB. On a device whose installed exporter is not the source tree's, uhttpd cannot run this one. There, these cases limit the benchmark's scrape process instead, and say so (by scrape). - progress:full is a scrape's progress file. - record: cases time the recorder alone, with a sample of each shape collectors write. noop:1 and noop:41 scrape collectors that write nothing. The note of noop:41 gives what a scrape costs per collector, apart from the collector itself. Budgets hold both. The noop:41 budget is in turns of calibrate:vm's loop, so it holds on any machine. - rpcd: cases run in their own process (test/bench/rpcd.uc), which holds what rpcd's plugin holds for the ubus object. - rpcd:rest measures what the process holds, which a budget holds, and how long collecting it takes, as rpcd collects after every call. - rpcd:wireless, rpcd:wireguard_peers and rpcd:time_daemons each time a call of a method the collectors call at every scrape, on the world's configs, sysfs and procd, plus the collection after it.

    Budgets in turns of calibrate:vm's loop hold these cases, and timesync, wifi, agh and nat_traffic on 1,000 connections. So if a change runs a program for each call, or makes rpcd collect all of the object's modules, the benchmark catches it. A budget also holds rpcd:wireless to not reading the configs again while they and the phys are unchanged. - collector: cases count what the collector asked of the world (asked): rtnl and nl80211 requests, the watchdog's runs and the programs in them, and TCP connections. Budgets hold wifi, ethtool and agh to their counts. A count is the same on any machine, and a request, a run or a connection is what costs a router most. AdGuard Home's API is a stand-in on 127.0.0.1:8080 that answers with the world's replies, as the router's API answered.

For a scrape, the table's note gives the child's peak memory, to size memory_limit by.

The worlds have the config the package installs, with every option of its main section set, as on a router. A scrape reads each option. So a change that made each collector read them would cost here what it costs on a router.

Narrow it to some cases, or run each more:

make bench FILTER='typical/scrape'
make bench FILTER='nat_traffic' BENCH_ARGS='-r 20'

-r N runs each case at least N times, -t S for at least S seconds.

docs.title: Before and after a change
docs.text:
Bench another revision's src/ with this checkout's benchmark:

make bench BENCH_REV=main
make bench

The results are bin/bench/devenv-main.json and bin/bench/devenv.json.

docs.title: As a slower router
docs.text:
Limit the container to a share of one CPU:

make bench FILTER='calibrate' BENCH_CPUS=0.35 BENCH_CPUSET=0

Pick BENCH_CPUS by calibrate:vm's loop turn, in the same session: choose the share that makes the turn match the router's. A container's programs still cost what the host's do, so its whole scrapes are faster than the router's. QEMU is the closer model of a MIPS router. Performance on small routers has the calibration.

BENCH_MEMORY=64m also limits the container's memory.

docs.title: On a device
docs.text:
make bench-device HOST=root@router.lan

The target copies the sources, the benchmark and the worlds to the device's /tmp. It runs them there with the device's own ucode, beside whatever else the device runs, and removes them afterwards. It installs nothing.

The device needs ucode, ucode-mod-fs, -ubus, -uci, -rtnl and -log. Its rest: and floor: cases measure the benchmark's process, since uhttpd cannot run the source tree there. The result is bin/bench/<HOST>.json, or the name BENCH_DEVICE_LABEL= gives.

docs.title: In QEMU, as a MIPS router
docs.text:
make bench-qemu
make bench-qemu QEMU_SHIFT=2
make bench-qemu QEMU_ENDIAN=be

This runs OpenWrt's malta target in qemu-system-mipsel: a MIPS 24Kc, with the mipsel_24kc packages that MT7621-class routers use. It installs the built packages, and their dependencies from the release's feed.

  • QEMU_ENDIAN=be runs malta's big-endian image in qemu-system-mips instead, with the mips_24kc packages of ath79-class routers, the most common small ones. Its result is bin/bench/qemu-malta-be-shift<N>.json.
  • QEMU_SHIFT=1 runs the guest at 500 MIPS, and 2 at 250.
  • QEMU_MEMORY=64 runs it in a guest of 64 MB.

Before the benchmark, the guest reports:

  • what the install added to its flash, and each package's installed size (size: lines)
  • while the service runs as installed: what its uhttpd holds, what the guest has left, and how many collectors it serves (service: lines)

Then, on the installed exporter, it checks the code that reads data in the CPU's own byte order: the auxiliary vector's page size and clock tick, sockstat's bytes against its pages, and basic auth's hashes. Each check is a check: line of the output. If one fails, the target fails.

The first time, the target downloads the release's images and packages into bin/qemu/. It is slow: narrow it with FILTER=.

test/bench/gen.uc generates the worlds from a seed, with the fixtures as templates, so every machine reads the same worlds. make bench-worlds writes them to bin/bench/worlds/. Performance on small routers explains the cases and what the results mean.

docs.title: How to Write Documentation
docs.text: The documentation is built with MkDocs Material, inside Docker. You need Docker and make.

docs.title: Preview while you write
docs.text:
make docs-serve

Open http://localhost:8000. The page reloads when you save a file under docs/ or change mkdocs.yml. If port 8000 is taken, choose another: make docs-serve DOCS_PORT=8001.

docs.title: Build the site
docs.text:
make docs

The site goes to bin/site/, and make -C docs clean removes it. The build runs mkdocs build --strict, so a broken link or any other warning fails it. On pushes and pull requests to main that touch the docs, CI runs the same strict build. It also runs a second one with the versioned config, mkdocs.mike.yml (make docs-mike locally).

Merging to main publishes nothing: the docs go online with the next release. To correct the docs already online, see How to fix the docs of the released version. Documentation publishing says what publishes when.

docs.title: Where a page goes
docs.text:
Pick the folder by what the reader is doing, following Diátaxis:

Folder The reader is... Example tutorials/ learning by doing, guided step by step Monitor a router with Prometheus how-to/ working toward a goal they already have Serve HTTPS with basic auth reference/ looking up a fact Every option of the configuration explanation/ trying to understand why Nothing to observe

Keep one type per page, and link to pages of the other types instead of mixing them. Add every new page to nav in mkdocs.yml and to the index.md of its folder. Link between pages with relative paths, never with the site's URL, so each published version links to itself.

The reasoning a reader needs lives in the explanation pages. When a change rests on a new reason, write the reason there, in the same change.

docs.title: Comments in the code
docs.text:
The code under src/, files/ and luci/ carries no explanatory comments: its explanation is here, in the docs. A reason that shapes the design goes in the explanation page it belongs to; a quirk of ucode, of a module or of the kernel that the code works round, or why a piece of code is shaped as it is, goes in About the implementation. Tests may keep their comments: they do not ship.

An exported symbol of a module has a JSDoc block for the language server, which shows it on hover, and nothing more: a one-line summary, its types, and a line on each parameter and on what a function returns.

/**
 * The scrapes left before the trial, seen from scrape `m`; null for a closed breaker.
 *
 * @param {?LedgerEntry} entry the collector's entry; null for none.
 * @param {int} m the scrape's number.
 * @returns {?int} the scrapes.
 */
export function left(entry, m) {

/**
 * The scrapes after which the deadline leaving a collector out is old news.
 *
 * @type {int}
 */
export const RECENT = 10;

The tags are @module, @typedef (record types too, where the type is defined), @template, @param {T} name description, @returns {T} description and, on an exported constant, @type {T}; and {@link} in a summary. Each description is one line: what the value is, not why. A function or a constant that is not exported has no comment.

The package build strips every comment that is left, JSDoc too, from the ucode and JavaScript files it installs, and keeps a newline for each line it empties, so a device gets no comments and the line of an error on it is the line here. To check that a change to comments changed nothing else:

make same-code REV=main

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
Six reference pages are written from the code by make docs-gen, and never by hand:

Page From docs/reference/collectors.md Each collector's meta, the package Makefile, and the code's reasons for nothing to observe. docs/reference/metrics.md What each collector writes when it runs on the fixture sets of test/fixtures/. docs/reference/uci-config.md config.uc's option specs, and config/types.uc's datatypes. docs/reference/error-codes.md errors.uc, and where each code is raised; its sections are the notes'. docs/reference/command.md The command's usage, cli.uc's USAGE, which docopt parses its arguments by. docs/reference/migration.md docs/gen/migration.md, its text, with the tables of the feed exporters' packages and families and this exporter's for each: from docs/gen/feed-exporters.json, what make feed-inventory read of their sources, docs/gen/migration.uc, the mapping, and what the collectors write, as for metrics.md.

docs/gen/notes.uc holds what the code does not say:

  • when each collector has nothing to observe
  • what a computed jail path is
  • the patterns that fold a driver's statistics into one row
  • the families no fixture shows
  • the meaning of each error code, and the section of the page it is in
  • what each command of the command line does
  • a name for each fixture set

The generator checks the notes against the code. If the code contradicts an entry, the generator refuses and writes nothing.

  1. Change the code, or the notes.

  2. Regenerate:

    make docs-gen

  3. If it refuses, its message says which note to change:

    • A new collector that can have nothing to observe needs an entry in nothing_to_observe.
    • A family the collector declares, but that no fixture makes it write, needs a fixture or an entry in unharvested.
    • A new fixture set needs a name in capture_sets, which keeps the device's own name out of the docs.
  4. Commit the pages with the change. make lint fails while a page differs from what make docs-gen would write.

docs.title: Keep it true
docs.text:
Reference pages describe the code as it is. When you change one of these, update its page in the same change:

Code Reference page A collector, config.uc and config/, errors.uc, the package Makefile, test/fixtures/ The generated pages: make docs-gen. files/etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter, check.uc, status.uc Service commands cli.uc, files/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter The prometheus-exporter command, generated from cli.uc's usage and docs/gen/notes.uc: make docs-gen runner.uc, probe.uc, jailed.uc, conform.uc, the guards of scrape.uc, ownership.uc, progress.uc, exposition.uc, loader.uc Collector contract http.uc, app.uc, auth.uc, query.uc, scrape.uc HTTP endpoint rpc.uc and rpc/, the rpcd plugin ubus object luci/ LuCI app, How to use the LuCI app, the Browser (LuCI) tabs, and the screenshots: make luci-screenshots jail.uc, state.uc, the init script's mounts The jail loader.uc, deps.uc and deps/, result.uc, services.uc, exposition.uc's recorder Collector interface A log line Log messages files/, the package Makefile Files and packages The root Makefile, docs/Makefile Make targets docs/Makefile, devenv/scripts/docs-*.sh, .github/workflows/docs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml, docs/overrides/, devenv/gh-pages/, devenv/services/docs/ Documentation publishing migrate.uc How to move from the feed's exporters, and Migrate from prometheus-node-exporter-lua/-ucode: its text is docs/gen/migration.md A collector's families, or the feed's exporters (make feed-inventory) Migrate from prometheus-node-exporter-lua/-ucode: make docs-gen refuses a family of the feed's that docs/gen/migration.uc does not map, and a mapping to a family no collector writes monitoring/: a rule, a threshold, a panel How to monitor a router with the bundled dashboards and alerts, and its screenshots: make monitoring-lab A renamed metric Renamed metrics

docs.title: Steps in LuCI and over SSH
docs.text:
An operator step that LuCI can do gets two content tabs, LuCI first, with exactly these labels:

=== "Browser (LuCI)"

    On **Services → Prometheus exporter**, tab **General**, untick **Compress**, and press **Save & Apply**.

=== "Terminal (SSH)"

    ```sh
    uci set prometheus-exporter.main.compress=0
    uci commit prometheus-exporter
    service prometheus-exporter reload
    ```

Picking a tab picks it on every page (content.tabs.link). Name menus, tabs, fields and buttons by the app's English source strings, in luci/. A step LuCI cannot do, such as adding the feed's signing key, stays SSH only.

The LuCI screenshots, docs/how-to/img/luci-*.png, come from the lab: make luci-screenshots takes them again after a change to the app. Add one only where a picture makes a LuCI step clearer, with alt text that says what it shows.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Use generic names (router, ap) and documentation addresses: 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 for IPv4, 2001:db8::/32 for IPv6. Never paste a real device's name, MAC address, SSID, key or public address.
  • Output captured from the lab is the exception: paste it as it is. Its addresses are docker's, and disposable.
  • Use Mermaid in a fenced block with the mermaid language, only where a picture explains more than a paragraph.

docs.title: How to Fix the Docs of the Released Version
docs.text: A docs fix reaches the published site through the newest minor's docs branch, docs/X.Y. Pushing the branch republishes /X.Y/. Only the newest minor gets fixes, and older versions stay as they are. The examples fix 0.2.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The fix is merged into main. Fixes always land on main first.
  • The fix changes only files under docs/, mkdocs.yml or mkdocs.mike.yml. A code fix needs a release instead: How to publish the docs of a patch release.

docs.title: 1. Cherry-pick the fix onto the docs branch
docs.text:
git fetch origin --tags
git switch docs/0.2
git cherry-pick <sha>

Cherry-pick each commit you need. Never merge or rebase main into docs/0.2: it would publish the docs of unreleased work (why).

If a commit also changes files outside the docs, take only its docs part:

git cherry-pick -n <sha>
git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- . ':!docs/' ':!mkdocs.yml' ':!mkdocs.mike.yml'
git commit -C <sha>

docs.title: 2. Check the branch
docs.text:
devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh docs/0.2

It prints the release tag when the branch may publish. If it refuses, see below.

docs.title: 3. Push
docs.text:
git push origin docs/0.2

The docs workflow republishes /0.2/. Check that its publish job succeeded.

docs.title: If the guard refuses
docs.text:
The message tells you which case you are in. Docs-only guard lists every message.

  • docs/0.2 changes files outside docs/: <files>; code fixes need a release: a commit on the branch changes code. If you have not pushed yet, drop the commit with git reset --hard origin/docs/0.2, and cherry-pick again as in step 1. If you already pushed it, revert it and push the revert:

    git revert <sha>
git push origin docs/0.2

    The code fix ships with the next release.

  • v0.2.1 is not an ancestor of docs/0.2: someone tagged a patch release, and the branch has not moved to it. Move it as in How to publish the docs of a patch release, then push again.

  • docs/0.2 has no v0.2.* release tag: locally, the tags are missing: run git fetch origin --tags. In CI, it means the minor has not been released yet, and the branch should not exist.

docs.title: How to Capture Fixtures from a Device
docs.text: The tests, the benchmark's worlds and the metrics reference read what real devices answered, from test/fixtures/<set>/. When you write a collector for something the sets do not cover yet, capture a device's answers.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ssh access to the device, as root, with ucode on it (OpenWrt 25.12 has it).
  • The device runs what the collector reads.

docs.title: 1. Say what to read
docs.text:
Add the sources to test/fixtures/SOURCES, one per line:

Line Captures file PATH The file, or every file the glob matches, at its own path. ubus OBJECT METHOD [ARGS] The reply, as ubus/OBJECT.METHOD.json. link GLOB Where each symlink the glob matches leads, into links.json. uci CONFIG The config's sections, as uci/CONFIG.json, without secret options (keys, passwords).

docs.title: 2. Capture
docs.text:
make fixtures HOST=root@router.lan NAME=my-router

Everything is read-only on the device. The target adds only files that are not in test/fixtures/my-router/ yet, so the values the tests assert on do not change under them. FORCE=1 replaces them all.

Capture by hand, into the same set, what make fixtures cannot read, and say how in comments in SOURCES:

  • a program's output, as commands/<program>_<arguments>.txt (commands/ethtool_S_lan.txt for ethtool -S lan)
  • an rtnetlink or nl80211 reply, as rtnl/<CMD>.json or nl80211/<CMD>.<device>.json

docs.title: 3. Redact
docs.text:
Before you commit, replace in every file of the set:

  • MAC addresses, with locally administered ones, 02:00:00:…
  • public IP addresses, with 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32
  • SSIDs, hostnames, domain names, user names and keys

uci captures leave out secret options, but they keep names and addresses.

docs.title: 4. Name the set in the docs
docs.text:
The metrics reference runs every collector on every set, and names each set without the device's name. Add the new set to capture_sets in docs/gen/notes.uc, then run:

make docs-gen

What no captured device has is written by hand in test/fixtures/synthetic/. test/fixtures/synthetic/SOURCES gives the format each file follows.

docs.title: How to Use the Lab
docs.text: The lab is a device to try things on. It is OpenWrt under procd in a privileged container, left running, with the built packages installed: every collector and the LuCI app.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
make lab

It builds the packages, boots OpenWrt and installs them. When it is up:

The lab runs, as container ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab:
  LuCI      http://127.0.0.1:8080/  (root, no password)
  /metrics  http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics
  a shell   docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash
  stop it   make lab-down

If a port is taken, or another checkout runs a lab, give yours its own name and ports:

make lab LAB_NAME=my-lab LAB_LUCI_PORT=18080 LAB_METRICS_PORT=19100

docs.title: Try a change
docs.text: Edit the code, then run make lab again. It rebuilds the packages and starts the lab afresh, so anything you changed by hand in the lab is lost.

docs.title: Look inside
docs.text:
docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash

service prometheus-exporter check
logread -e prometheus-exporter
ubus call prometheus-exporter status

docs.title: Watch it with Prometheus, Grafana and Perses
docs.text:
make monitoring-lab

It starts, each from its official image and unprivileged:

  • a Prometheus that scrapes the lab every 5 seconds, with the rules of monitoring/prometheus/
  • a Grafana with the dashboards of monitoring/grafana/
  • a Perses with the dashboards of monitoring/perses/

After MONITORING_WAIT seconds of scrapes (3 minutes), it runs every panel's queries through Grafana and through Perses. It fails on a query that errs, or that has no data where the lab has some. Then it screenshots each dashboard:

Monitoring the lab ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab:
  Prometheus  http://127.0.0.1:9090/alerts
  Grafana     http://127.0.0.1:3000/dashboards  (no login)
  Perses      http://127.0.0.1:8081/projects/openwrt
  results     bin/monitoring/report.txt, bin/monitoring/screenshots/
  stop it     make monitoring-lab-down

The screenshots in How to monitor a router with the bundled dashboards and alerts are these, taken with MONITORING_WAIT=960, so that the last 15 minutes they show all hold lab data. Give the same LAB_NAME as the lab's, and other ports if those are taken: make monitoring-lab LAB_NAME=my-lab GRAFANA_PORT=13000.

docs.title: Stop it
docs.text:
make monitoring-lab-down
make lab-down

With LAB_NAME too, if you gave one.

docs.title: What is different from a device
docs.text:
• lan is the container's eth0, with the address docker gave it, and no bridge.
  • The firewall, mwan3 and chronyd do not start:
    • fw4 would reject what docker forwards.
    • mwan3 would rewrite the routing.
    • chronyd would steer the clock, which a privileged container shares with its host. Do not start chronyd there.
  • The exporter listens on every address (listen_interface '*'), which docker's published port needs.
  • Unbound listens on port 5353, with its control socket where the unbound collector looks.
  • textfile has a file to read, /var/prometheus/lab.prom.
  • ubnt-manager's sample radio is removed. Otherwise, ssh to it would cost each scrape 5 seconds.

The boot is in devenv/services/lab/boot.sh, and the setup in devenv/services/lab/setup.sh.

docs.title: How to Package a Collector
docs.text: Every collector is in the base package or in its own package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>. openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile declares both.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • The collector, src/prometheus/collectors/<module>.uc, and its unit test. See Collector interface.

docs.title: 1. Choose its package
docs.text:
• The base package, only for what every device has, and only when the collector needs nothing beyond what the base package brings. Add its module to BASE_COLLECTORS:

    BASE_COLLECTORS:=conntrack cpu ... uname vmstat <module>

  • A package of its own, for anything else. Add a Collector line, in alphabetical order of the module names:

    $(eval $(call Collector,<module>,<name>,<what it collects>,<dependencies>))
    Argument Content <module> The module's file name, without .uc: ltq_dsl. <name> meta.name, the package's suffix: ltq-dsl. <what it collects> A few words, added to the package's title: Lantiq DSL line. No commas. <dependencies> +package for what the collector reads with, space-separated: +ucode-mod-nl80211 for nl80211, +ucode-mod-socket for socket, the package of a program it runs on any device (+tc, +ethtool). Never what it watches: installing a collector must not install and start mwan3 or chrony. A program that comes with what it watches (chronyc, mmcli) goes in meta.optional_commands instead, and where it is missing the collector has nothing to observe. Empty for none; make test checks it.

    The macro makes a package that installs the module and depends on the base package of the same version. The package reloads an enabled service when it is installed or removed.

docs.title: 2. Add it to a group
docs.text:
If every router or access point should have it, add its name to a group's list:

NETWORK_GROUP:=ethtool nat_traffic netstat nft-counters qdisc snmp6 sockstat <name>

FULL_GROUP holds the other three groups and more. Leave out a collector for particular hardware or for an optional service.

docs.title: 3. Check
docs.text:
make test
make docs-gen
make lint
make package-check
  • test/integration/collectors_test.uc checks that every collector is in exactly one package, named after it, whose dependencies cover the collector's needs and commands. A new program needs an entry in the test's COMMAND_PACKAGES.
  • make docs-gen adds the collector to the reference: its package and groups to Collectors, its families to Metrics. If the collector can have nothing to observe, or declares a family no fixture makes it write, the generator says what to add to docs/gen/notes.uc.
  • make package-check builds and installs every package, including the new one.
  • Add the collector to NOTICE when it ports an upstream collector.

docs.title: How to Publish the Docs of a New Minor Release
docs.text: A new minor release, such as 0.2.0, publishes its docs as /0.2/ and moves /latest/ to them. It also starts a new docs branch and freezes the previous one. The examples release 0.2.0 after 0.1.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Publishing is set up: How to set up documentation publishing.
  • The release is ready on main, with PKG_VERSION:=0.2.0 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile.
  • Every pinned docs link in the shipped files points to /0.2/, including URL:= in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile. If the project keeps a CHANGELOG.md, the release's entries are under ## [0.2.0]. make lint passes.

docs.title: 1. Tag the release
docs.text:
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin v0.2.0

The docs workflow publishes /0.2/, titled 0.2.0, and moves latest to it. Check that its publish job succeeded and that /latest/ shows 0.2.0 in the version selector.

docs.title: 2. Create the docs branch
docs.text:
git branch docs/0.2 v0.2.0
git push origin docs/0.2

docs.title: 3. Freeze the previous branch
docs.text:
Stop pushing to docs/0.1. /0.1/ stays online as it was last published. From now on, doc fixes go to docs/0.2: see How to fix the docs of the released version.

What each push publishes, and when latest moves, is in Documentation publishing. Why only the newest minor gets fixes: About versioned documentation.

docs.title: How to Publish the Docs of a Patch Release
docs.text: A patch release, such as 0.2.1, republishes its minor, /0.2/, from the new tag. Afterwards the docs branch has to move onto the tag, or it cannot publish again. The examples release 0.2.1.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The minor's docs branch exists: How to publish the docs of a new minor release.
  • The release is ready, with PKG_VERSION:=0.2.1 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, and make lint passes.

docs.title: 1. Tag the release
docs.text:
git tag v0.2.1
git push origin v0.2.1

The docs workflow republishes /0.2/, now titled 0.2.1. latest follows if 0.2 is the newest minor.

docs.title: 2. Move the docs branch to the tag
docs.text:
git fetch origin
git switch docs/0.2
git merge --ff-only v0.2.1

If the fast-forward fails because the branch has fix commits of its own, merge the tag instead:

git merge v0.2.1

If the merge conflicts, keep the tag's side for every file outside docs/, mkdocs.yml and mkdocs.mike.yml: the branch may only differ from the tag in the docs.

Then push:

git push origin docs/0.2

Until the branch contains v0.2.1, every publish from it is refused with v0.2.1 is not an ancestor of docs/0.2. See Docs-only guard.

docs.title: How to Publish a Release to the Package Feed
docs.text: Routers install the exporter, its collector packages, its groups and luci-app-prometheus-exporter from the packages.ucode.dev feed. The feed builds them from the release tarball GitHub serves for a tag, with a Makefile generated from openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile. The examples publish 0.2.0.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The release is tagged and pushed: v0.2.0, with PKG_VERSION:=0.2.0 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, and CHANGELOG.md's ## [0.2.0] section dated.
  • A checkout of packages.ucode.dev next to this one.
  • The feed has ucode-docopt, which the command line's package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli, depends on. The feed already publishes it for 25.12.

The feed fetches the tarball of v<PKG_VERSION>. So a release that only raises PKG_RELEASE cannot reach the feed: publish a new version instead.

docs.title: 1. Generate the feed Makefile
docs.text:
make feed-makefile VERSION=0.2.0 OUT=../packages.ucode.dev/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile

This downloads the v0.2.0 tarball, hashes it, and writes the Makefile. If it refuses, it names one of these:

  • the line of openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile it does not know how to transform
  • the paths the Makefile copies that the tarball lacks: every collector that the Collector calls and BASE_COLLECTORS name, each directory of MODULE_SUBDIRS, the programs of libexec/, and the license files

TARBALL=<path> uses a tarball already on disk instead of downloading it. HASH=<sha256> transforms this tree's Makefile with that hash, offline, and checks nothing against a tag.

docs.title: 2. Commit it to the feed
docs.text:
In packages.ucode.dev, commit ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile and push it to main. Do not edit the file there: the feed's workflow regenerates it from the tag, and fails if the two differ.

The workflow then builds every package with the OpenWrt 25.12 SDK, signs them into 25.12/noarch/, and adds them to every architecture's index.

The first release to reach the feed needs that workflow, a copy of the feed's wgpathd workflow. It runs this repository's devenv/scripts/gen-feed-makefile.sh from the tag. It expects the 35 packages of 0.2.0: the base package, 29 collectors, 4 groups and the LuCI app.

docs.title: 3. Check the feed
docs.text:
On a router with the feed configured:

apk update
apk info -a ucode-prometheus-exporter | head -3

The version shown is 0.2.0-r<PKG_RELEASE>. To upgrade a router to it, see Upgrading the exporter.

docs.title: How to Republish a Version
docs.text: Republish a version when its publish failed or was cancelled, or when gh-pages lost it. You can run the docs workflow by hand for any release tag or docs branch. The examples republish 0.2.

docs.title: 1. Choose the ref
docs.text:
• If the minor has a docs branch, use it: docs/0.2. It holds the release plus its doc fixes.
  • Otherwise use the minor's newest release tag, for example v0.2.1.

If you republish a tag older than the newest, or a tag instead of the branch, /0.2/ gets older docs.

docs.title: 2. Run the workflow
docs.text:
In the repository, open Actions → docs → Run workflow, enter the ref, and run it. With the GitHub CLI:

gh workflow run docs.yml -f ref=docs/0.2

Republishing an older minor leaves latest on the newest one. A docs branch still has to pass the docs-only guard. If the guard refuses, see How to fix the docs of the released version.

docs.title: How to Set Up Documentation Publishing
docs.text: Nothing is published until the repository is on GitHub, the site's URL is known, and the first release is tagged. Do these steps once, in this order. The examples use the repository m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter, the site https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/, and 0.1.0 as the first release.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A GitHub repository for the exporter, with admin rights to change its Pages settings.
  • The first release, 0.1.0, is ready on main: PKG_VERSION:=0.1.0 in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile.

docs.title: 1. Push main
docs.text:
git remote add origin git@github.com:m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter.git
git push -u origin main

docs.title: 2. Set the site's URL and pin the links
docs.text:
1. In mkdocs.yml, check that site_url is the site's base URL, without a version, and repo_url the repository's. Change both if the repository has another owner or name:

    site_url: https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/
repo_url: https://github.com/m00qek/ucode-prometheus-exporter

  2. To give the packages a link to their docs, add URL:= to Package/$(PKG_NAME)/Default in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, pointing to the docs of the package's minor:

    URL:=https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.1/

  3. Link the README to https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/latest/.

  4. Check the pinned links:

    make lint

Commit the change and push it to main. Links to the documentation says which link goes where.

docs.title: 3. Tag the first release
docs.text:
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

The docs workflow creates gh-pages and publishes /0.1/ and /latest/. Wait for its publish job to succeed.

docs.title: 4. Turn on GitHub Pages
docs.text: In the repository's Settings → Pages, set the source to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The site then answers at https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/, which redirects to /latest/.

docs.title: 5. Create the docs branch
docs.text:
git branch docs/0.1 v0.1.0
git push origin docs/0.1

Doc fixes for 0.1 go through this branch: see How to fix the docs of the released version.

docs.title: Clear an unversioned deploy from gh-pages
docs.text:
If gh-pages carries files from an earlier unversioned deploy, for example from mkdocs gh-deploy, remove them once. They shadow the 404 redirect and keep serving stale pages. Do this while no docs workflow is running.

  1. Check out gh-pages and list its root:

    git fetch origin gh-pages
git switch gh-pages
git ls-tree --name-only HEAD

  2. Remove everything that is not part of the versioned layout. Keep the version folders, latest, versions.json, index.html, 404.html and .nojekyll.

    git ls-tree --name-only HEAD |
    grep -vxE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+|latest|versions\.json|index\.html|404\.html|\.nojekyll' |
    xargs git rm -r -q
git commit -m 'Remove the unversioned site'
git push origin gh-pages
git switch main

If nothing has been published to gh-pages with mike yet, publish first (step 3), so that index.html is mike's redirect and not the old site's home page.

docs.title: How to Run the Tests
docs.text: Everything runs in Docker, on OpenWrt's own images of the release in OPENWRT_VERSION (25.12.5 by default). You need Docker and make.

docs.title: Unit and integration tests
docs.text:
make test

The tests of the template collector package, devkit/template/test/, run with the unit tests, on the tree's devkit. make unit and make integration each run one suite. To narrow a run:

make unit MODULES=test/unit/prometheus/collectors/wifi_test.uc
make test FILTER='collectors.wifi' VERBOSE=1
make watch

A full run first checks the comment stripper that the package build runs. It runs the stripper's own tests, test/strip/, and strips every ucode and JavaScript file the packages install. Each ucode file must compile to the same stripped bytecode as its source, which proves the stripper removed comments and nothing else. A narrowed run skips this check.

watch runs the tests again whenever a file under src/, test/, files/, devenv/scripts/, docs/gen/ or devkit/ changes. To run them on the API floor, the first 25.12 release, as CI also does: make test OPENWRT_VERSION=25.12.0.

docs.title: Lint
docs.text:
make lint

It loads every module on the release's ucode, so a call to a function that ucode lacks fails here, not on a router. It also fails when the translation template or a generated reference page is out of date. Run make pot or make docs-gen, and commit the result.

docs.title: The packages
docs.text:
make package-check

This builds the apks with the SDK and installs them offline in an OpenWrt image. It scrapes a real uhttpd and calls the ubus object in a real rpcd, first with the base package alone, then with the LuCI app. It checks that each installed ucode file, which the build stripped of comments, compiles to the same code as its source. Then it installs the devkit and runs the template collector's tests on it, as a collector package's own CI would.

docs.title: The service under procd
docs.text:
make e2e

This boots OpenWrt in a privileged container, without network. It checks the service in its jail while packages are installed and removed and the configuration changes. It needs Docker to allow privileged containers.

A check the host cannot run prints skip, with why, and is not counted: on a kernel without /proc/net/nf_conntrack (Ubuntu's, as GitHub's runners have), on a machine without a hwmon chip, where chronyd cannot start, and, on 25.12.0's rpcd, every check of the ubus object's status. make package-check skips its status checks there too.

docs.title: The LuCI app
docs.text:
make browser
make browser FILTER='settings'

This runs the Playwright tests of test/browser/ against LuCI with the built packages. It also compares the app's JavaScript as LuCI serves it, stripped of comments, with its sources, token by token. Screenshots go to bin/browser/, and on a failure so do the error context and LuCI's log.

docs.title: The documentation tooling
docs.text:
make docs-test
make docs

docs-test runs the publishing scripts' tests. docs builds the site, strictly. See How to write documentation.

CI runs lint, test, package-check and e2e on 25.12.0 and 25.12.5, and bench and browser once. A failed e2e on 25.12.0 does not fail the run: on GitHub's runners, about a third of its runs lose rpcd partway through, for a cause not yet found. Its first failure prints what rpcd and ubusd were doing. The docs workflow builds the site. Make targets lists every target.

docs.title: How to Update the Translation Template
docs.text: The translation template luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot holds the LuCI app's strings: every _('...') in luci/. make lint fails while the template is out of date.

docs.title: Update it
docs.text:
After you add, change or move a string in the LuCI app:

make pot

It runs openwrt/luci's own scanner, build/i18n-scan.pl, over luci/, laid out as applications/luci-app-prometheus-exporter in the luci tree. So the template's location comments are the ones upstream would write. Commit the template with the change.

docs.title: If it fails
docs.text:
pot: the scanner warned, so a string may be missing from the template means the scanner lost its way in a file. The lines above name the file. Fix the string it stumbled on, often a quote inside _(), and run it again. It writes nothing while it warns.

The scanner runs in its own image, ucode-prometheus-exporter-i18n, from devenv/services/i18n/Dockerfile, without network.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Technical descriptions of the exporter, to consult while you work. Six pages are generated from the code by make docs-gen: Collectors, Metrics, UCI configuration, Error codes, The prometheus-exporter command and Migrate from prometheus-node-exporter-lua/-ucode. The pages are grouped by reader: who these docs are for.

docs.title: What it collects
docs.text:
For operators.

Page Content Collectors Every collector: its package and groups, options, configs, programs, jail paths, and when it has nothing to observe. Metrics Every metric family, by collector: type, labels and help. Renamed metrics The names that changed from the feed's exporters, and why. Migrate from prometheus-node-exporter-lua/-ucode Every package and metric family of the feed's exporters, and this exporter's for each; PromQL rewrites, a relabeling for a transition, and what the configuration import takes over.

docs.title: Configuring and running it
docs.text:
For operators.

Page Content UCI configuration Every option of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, and what values it takes. Service commands The init script's actions, status and check, procd's instances and triggers. The prometheus-exporter command A scrape on the command line. HTTP endpoint /metrics: the query string, the reply, compression, basic auth. ubus object prometheus-exporter's methods, arguments and replies. LuCI app Its pages, fields and ACL. The jail What procd's jail mounts, and the state the exporter keeps. Log messages Every line the exporter logs, and its priority. Error codes The codes of a failure, and where each is raised. Files and packages What each package installs and depends on.

docs.title: Developing it
docs.text:
For collector authors and maintainers.

Page For Content Collector interface Collector authors meta, collect(deps, out, options), the capabilities and Results. Collector contract Collector authors What a collector may do, what the exporter enforces, what breaking a rule costs, and collector check. The devkit Collector authors What a collector's tests run on, in the exporter's tree or a package of its own: with_collector, the mocks and fixtures. Make targets Maintainers The targets of the root Makefile and docs/Makefile, and their variables. Documentation publishing Maintainers How the versioned site is published.

docs.title: Collector Contract
docs.text:
This page lists what a collector may do, what the exporter enforces, and what breaking each rule costs. The exporter holds every collector to the same contract, its own and those of other packages. It does so wherever collectors run: in the service's scrapes, in check, in the ubus object's status, and in the prometheus-exporter command.

The contract guards against collectors with bugs, not against hostile ones: see About the security model.

docs.title: What a collector may import
docs.text:
A collector module imports prometheus.exporter, the collector API, and nothing else:

import { Result, errors, services, proc, exposition } from 'prometheus.exporter';
Export Names Result ok, err, none, is, is_none, describe errors SOURCE_UNREADABLE, SOURCE_INVALID, CONFIG_INVALID, the codes it fails with; UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED, UBUS_CALL_FAILED, UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED, NL80211_FAILED, RTNL_FAILED, SOCKET_FAILED, COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED, COMMAND_FAILED, COMMAND_TIMEOUT, PERMISSION_DENIED, SCRAPE_DEADLINE, EXPOSITION_INVALID, those its capabilities return services state, idle, unless_disabled, object_missing; ENABLED, DISABLED, NOT_INSTALLED, NOT_FOUND proc first_line, lines, each_line, fields, rows, auxv; AT_PAGESZ, AT_CLKTCK exposition parse, format_value, sanitize u16, u32 functions

Collector interface describes each one. These exports are the collector's semantic-versioning surface: they change incompatibly only in a major version. The modules behind them belong to the core, and may change in any release. See About versions.

The loader refuses these before it loads the module:

  • Any other module.
    • fs, ubus, uci, socket, rtnl, nl80211, uloop: the capabilities of meta.needs do their work, under the exporter's guards.
    • The core's modules, prometheus.exporter.<module>: the API is exactly prometheus.exporter, not what is under it.
    • Another collector's module, prometheus.collectors.<module>.
    • Pure modules too, such as math, struct or digest. Each would be a dependency the collector's package does not declare, and one more exception to judge. What collectors need of them belongs in the API, in a minor version.
  • Code loaded past the imports. A call to require, loadfile, loadstring or include: require('fs') reaches fs as surely as an import does.
  • A program started past exec. A call to system. What it starts outlives the child process that the scrape kills under the collector, and keeps running. deps.exec, instead, kills a program still running at its timeout, with everything it started.

The loader reads the module's text for its imports without compiling it, and skips comments, strings, templates and regular expressions. A collector is a single module. It cannot keep code of its own in another module, because the loader loads every module of the collectors' directory as a collector.

Where Broken: The loader, wherever collectors are loaded: the service, check, the ubus object, the command line Not loaded; logged at err: skipping collector: COLLECTOR_INVALID (<module>: imports fs (line 3): a collector reads files through deps.fs, with 'fs' in meta.needs) prometheus-exporter collector check A FAIL line, with the same text: FAIL imports fs (line 3): a collector reads files through deps.fs, with 'fs' in meta.needs The repository's tests test/unit/prometheus/imports_test.uc holds every collector of src/ to it.

The message for each refused module names what to use instead:

  • for a module of the system, the capability;
  • for the core's result, errors, services, proc and exposition, the API (take Result from prometheus.exporter);
  • for any other, a collector imports prometheus.exporter alone.

docs.title: What a collector may touch
docs.text:
Of the system Only Files and directories Procfs, sysfs, and what meta.configs and meta.paths declare. The jail has nothing else a collector would read: see The jail. Unix sockets Those in a directory of meta.paths. TCP ports The device's own, through deps.socket.tcp_request. The jail shares the host's network, so they need no declaration. Programs Those of meta.commands. ubus, uci, netlink Through deps.ubus (the calls of meta.ubus), deps.uci (the configs of meta.configs), deps.rtnl, deps.nl80211. Privileges As the service's user: the capabilities of meta.capabilities, the groups of meta.groups, the root-only files of /proc in meta.proc_files. See The jail.

Nothing a collector may read is writable.

docs.title: In the tests
docs.text:
The devkit's with_collector (prometheus.exporter.devkit.collector, see The devkit) runs a collector's test in the filesystem that the service's jail would give the collector. That filesystem holds the jail's mounts for the collector's meta, and what every jail has (jail.COMMON): procfs, sysfs, the log's and ubus's sockets, ujail's devices and /etc/resolv.conf, the exporter's code, ucode's modules and libraries, the shell, and the exporter's own config and state. Whatever the fs and socket mocks hold, an access outside that filesystem answers as it would in the jail:

Access Answers readfile, open null lsdir null; for a directory above a mount, such as /etc, the names of what is mounted under it stat, realpath null; for a directory above a mount, a directory glob What the pattern matches of the mounts only open to write, of any path null: the mounts are read-only deps.socket.unix_request SOCKET_FAILED, connect(): No such file or directory deps.socket.tcp_request What the mock answers: the jail has the host's network, and the capability itself refuses an address that is not the device's deps.exec.run of a program not in meta.commands COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED, as everywhere deps.ubus.call of a method meta.ubus does not list UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED, as everywhere, as the service's ubus ACL would refuse it

with_collector records each such access. Once the collector has run, it fails the test with assert.fail(): a failure, which a property test shrinks. It does not fail from inside the run, where the collector's error boundary would take the failure for a crash, and a collector that falls back on a default would pass.

collector 'foo' read /etc/foo/state, which its meta does not declare.
In the service's jail that path does not exist: the read returns null, as it did here.
Declare it in meta.paths (or its directory: '/etc/foo'), or stop reading it.
Declared: /proc, /sys, /etc/config/foo

collector 'foo' connected to the socket /var/run/foo/foo.sock, which its meta does not declare.
In the service's jail that socket is not there: connect fails with 'No such file or directory', as it did here.
Declare its directory in meta.paths ('/var/run/foo'): the jail cannot mount a socket itself. Or stop connecting to it.
Declared: /proc, /sys

collector 'foo' ran 'false', which its meta.commands does not list.
The exporter refuses it, in the jail or not: run() returns COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED without running it, as it did here. A test that expects the collector to fail may pass by accident.
List it in meta.commands, with 'exec' in meta.needs, or stop running it.
Declared commands: true

A meta the loader refuses, and text that is not valid exposition, fail the test the same way. with_collector asserts nothing about the collector's Result: the test does that.

A test's outside_jail names paths that a collector looks for even though the jail never has them; the mocks then answer them. An example is chrony's command socket: the chrony collector reads server statistics from it when it runs outside the jail.

docs.title: What a collector may do
docs.text: A collector may Through Read files, sockets, ubus objects, uci configs and netlink The capabilities of meta.needs, in collect's deps: see Collector interface. Run programs deps.exec, the programs of meta.commands only. Write samples out, the recorder: see Collector interface. Log what it could not read deps.log, at warning. Take its time Up to its budget, and within the scrape's deadline. Fail Result.err(code, details): what it wrote is served, and the scrape answers without the rest. Have nothing to observe Result.none(reason): a success without samples. See About nothing to observe.

docs.title: What the exporter enforces
docs.text:
The last column says what a broken rule does to the collector's circuit breaker: it counts as a failure, it trips the breaker at once, or it leaves the breaker unchanged.

Rule Limit, by default Set by Broken: the error Its breaker The module is in strict mode: its first statement is 'use strict'. — — Not loaded; logged at err, COLLECTOR_INVALID. — It imports only the collector API, and calls no require, loadfile, loadstring, include or system. — — Not loaded; logged at err, COLLECTOR_INVALID. See What a collector may import. — Its top level only declares. At any load, it calls nothing that blocks, ends or writes to the process, loads code, or changes its signals. See Collector interface. — — Not loaded; logged at err, COLLECTOR_IMPURE. — Its top level loads in time. 5 s — Not loaded; logged at err, collector '<module>' hung at load. — meta and collect are valid. — — Not loaded; logged at err, COLLECTOR_INVALID. — It returns a Result, without throwing. — — COLLECTOR_NO_RESULT, COLLECTOR_CRASHED. A failure It returns within its budget. At the budget, the exporter kills its child process, with every process under it. A loop, a system call that never returns, a FIFO opened with no writer: all stop there. 5 s, or its timeout and a second more collector_budget, its section's budget COLLECTOR_CANCELLED; none of its samples served. Trips It is done by the scrape's deadline: the scraper's timeout, less half a second and the time writing the reply takes. 9.5 s of Prometheus's 10 the scraper, scrape_timeout SCRAPE_DEADLINE: not run, or stopped; none of its samples served. Unchanged Its programs end in time. The exporter kills one still running, with every process it started. 5 s, in all, per scrape exec_timeout, meta.timeout, its section's timeout COMMAND_TIMEOUT Trips Its ubus calls are answered within its own limit (its budget, or the deadline). as its budget — UBUS_CALL_FAILED A failure It calls over ubus only what meta.ubus lists. — — UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED, without calling. A failure The service's user has what the collector declares: its capabilities, read access to its configs and proc files, its socket's group, its ubus calls. — the service, when it starts PERMISSION_DENIED, saying what grants it. A failure It writes at most its samples. The recorder stops it at the next one. 20,000 max_samples, meta.max_samples, its section's max_samples SAMPLE_LIMIT, saying how far it got; none of its samples served. A failure The collectors of a reply write at most its samples in all. The recorder stops the collector that would go past them, and no collector starts once they are written. 200,000 max_scrape_samples SAMPLE_LIMIT, saying how many were left; none of its samples served. Unchanged What it writes is what Prometheus accepts: label values and HELP text in UTF-8 and without a NUL byte, family names without one, label names that do not start with __ and stay distinct once sanitized, and labels that are an object or what out.labels() made. The recorder stops it at the first sample that breaks this. — — EXPOSITION_INVALID, naming the family and the label; none of its samples served. A failure A family belongs to one collector: the first, in the reply's order, that writes it. The exporter's own collectors come before those of other packages. — — FAMILY_CONFLICT, naming the family's collector; none of its samples served. A failure It writes none of the exporter's own families, node_scrape_collector_* and ucode_prometheus_exporter_*, which the scrape writes. — — FAMILY_CONFLICT A failure It takes no more memory than each of the service's processes may. Past that, its own process ends. A quarter of the RAM, at most 64 MB memory_limit, 0 or 8 MB and more COLLECTOR_KILLED; none of its samples served. Trips It leaves its process to the exporter: it never ends it, by exit() or by a crash of a native module. — — COLLECTOR_KILLED Trips It is not running when its scrape process dies (killed at uhttpd's timeout, or by the kernel out of memory). — — The next scrape reads the dead one's progress file: COLLECTOR_KILLED, logged collector '<name>' was running when a scrape process died. The child left running is killed. Trips It reads only what the jail gives it, and runs at the service's priority. nice 10 — What is not mounted is not there: SOURCE_UNREADABLE, COMMAND_FAILED. See The jail. A failure

The collectors run one after the other in a child process forked from the scrape's process, never in the scrape's own. Whatever the child does, the scrape goes on with the next collector, in a new child if the last one was stopped or ended. See About the architecture.

flowchart TD
    S["The service starts"] --> P["Probe: the module loads in a child process<br/>its text, imports and top level checked, 5 s at most"]
    P -- "refused" --> X["Left out, logged at err"]
    P -- "passed" --> U["uhttpd loads the module<br/>its top level guarded again"]
    U --> R["A request to /metrics:<br/>a scrape process forked from uhttpd"]
    R --> C["A child forked from the scrape<br/>runs the collectors one after the other"]
    C --> K["collect(deps, out, options)<br/>stopped at its budget or the deadline"]
    K -- "returns" --> Res["Its Result: ok, err or none"]
    K -- "stopped or ended" --> N["A new child, for the next collector"]
    N --> C

docs.title: What breaking a rule costs
docs.text:
• The collector, and nothing else. The scrape answers on time with every other collector: their samples, and node_scrape_collector_success 1. The broken one has node_scrape_collector_success 0.
  • Its samples. A collector that was stopped, killed, went over its max_samples or wrote another collector's family has none of its samples served. A collector that fails by its own Result keeps what it wrote.
  • A line in the log, at warning: collector '<name>': <CODE> (<detail>). See Log messages.
  • A count, ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_failures_total{collector,reason}, from the exporter collector, since the service started.
  • Its breaker. The exporter quarantines a collector at once when it was stopped at its budget, was killed, or had a program killed at its timeout. A collector that fails in any other way is quarantined after three failed scrapes in a row. A quarantined collector is left out for 1 scrape, then 2, 4 and up to 32: each failed trial doubles the wait, until a trial succeeds. See About deadlines and circuit breakers.

When the deadline leaves a collector out, or stops it, the scrape ran out of time; the collector is not at fault. Its breaker stays as it was.

docs.title: What a collector may declare
docs.text:
meta Effect timeout The seconds its programs get, 1 to 30, unless its section says otherwise. Its budget is at least that and a second more. max_samples The samples it may write, 1 to 100,000, unless its section says otherwise. For a collector whose samples grow with what it reads, as nat_traffic's grow with the connection table (65,536). cost: 'heavy' Until the ledger has timed it, it runs after the other collectors not yet timed, so the first scrape after a restart does not spend their time on it. It changes only the order.

Until the ledger has timed them, as on the first scrape after a restart, the exporter's own collectors run before those of other packages.

docs.title: Check a module before installing it
docs.text:
prometheus-exporter collector check /tmp/my_collector.uc

The command:

  1. reads the module's text for strict mode, its imports and its top level;
  2. loads the module under the load timer and the top level's guard, and validates its meta;
  3. runs it on the device under the rules above;
  4. says how long it took to load and to run, the samples it wrote and its families;
  5. checks that its text is valid exposition with each series once, and whether an installed collector or the exporter already writes one of its families.

Each broken rule is a FAIL line, and the exit status is 1. See The prometheus-exporter command.

docs.text:
• Collector interface: meta, deps and out.
  • Tutorial: write your first collector
