docs.title: Collector Interface
docs.text:
A collector is a ucode module. Its source is src/prometheus/collectors/<module>.uc, and it is installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/collectors/. It imports only the collector API, and exports meta and collect:

'use strict';

import { Result, errors, proc } from 'prometheus.exporter';

export const meta = {
    name: 'loadavg',
    title: 'Load average',
    help: 'Load averages from /proc/loadavg.',
    needs: [ 'fs' ],
};

export function collect(deps, out) {
    let line = proc.first_line(deps.fs, '/proc/loadavg');

    if (line == null)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_UNREADABLE, '/proc/loadavg');

    let x = proc.fields(line);
    if (length(x) < 3)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_INVALID, `/proc/loadavg: ${sprintf('%J', line)}`);

    out.gauge('node_load1', '1m load average.')(null, x[0]);
    out.gauge('node_load5', '5m load average.')(null, x[1]);
    out.gauge('node_load15', '15m load average.')(null, x[2]);

    return Result.ok();
};

This is the loadavg collector, as the base package installs it.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
The loader (src/prometheus/exporter/loader.uc) imports every file of the collectors' directory whose name matches [a-z0-9_]+.uc, and validates its exports. A module must:

  • be in strict mode: its first statement is 'use strict', with only comments before it;
  • import prometheus.exporter, and no other module;
  • only declare at its top level, and finish loading within 5 seconds (the loader first loads it in a process of its own);
  • export a valid meta and collect.

The loader leaves out a module that breaks one of these rules, and loads the rest. The handler logs the module at err, and check and the ubus object's collectors list it. The loader sorts the collectors by name.

Collector contract lists what the exporter enforces on a collector, and what breaking each rule costs.

uhttpd loads the collectors once, when it starts. A scrape runs the collectors loaded then. Installing or removing a collector package reloads the service, which restarts uhttpd.

Each collector gets its own capabilities, copies included. A collector that overwrites one of their functions changes nothing for the collectors after it. uci cursors read only the committed configuration, never changes that are staged and not yet committed.

docs.title: The top level
docs.text:
A module's top level runs twice each time the service starts:

  1. in a child process, where the probe stops it at 5 seconds;
  2. in uhttpd's own process, which every scrape is forked from, and where nothing guards it.

So the top level only declares, and leaves the work to collect(). It may hold:

  • 'use strict', and its import of prometheus.exporter;
  • constants and variables (const, let) and functions, and their exports, meta and collect among them;
  • values built from literals, regular expressions, templates, objects and arrays, functions (not called), operators, and names it declared earlier;
  • calls to the ucode functions that compute only from their arguments: arrtoip, assert, b64dec, b64enc, chr, exists, filter, hex, hexdec, hexenc, index, int, iptoarr, join, json, keys, lc, length, ltrim, map, match, max, min, ord, pop, push, regexp, replace, reverse, rindex, rtrim, shift, slice, sort, splice, split, sprintf, substr, trim, type, uc, uchr, uniq, unshift, values, wildcard; and to the collector API functions that do the same: Result's, proc.fields, proc.auxv, u16, u32.
const FIELDS = [ 'rx_bytes', 'tx_bytes' ];
const LINE = regexp('^(' + join('|', FIELDS) + ') ([0-9]+)$');  // ok: pure calls
const UPPER = map(FIELDS, (f) => uc(f));                         // ok

const HOME = getenv('HOME');                 // not ok: reads the process's environment
const ONE = proc.first_line(fs, '/proc/x');  // not ok: no fs here; read it in collect()
for (let f in FIELDS) TABLE[f] = true;       // not ok: a statement; declare TABLE whole
Where Holds it to Broken Every load: the probe's child, uhttpd, rpcd's helpers, the command line While the top level runs, sleep, system, exit, print, printf, warn, trace, require, include, loadfile, loadstring, render and signal refuse to run. They block, end or write to the process, load code (and through require, read files, run programs and open sockets), or change its signals. The collector API's exposition functions load the format with loadstring, so they are refused too. In the child, the probe stops a loop that never ends at 5 s. Once the top level has run, the loader puts the global scope back as it was. It refuses a top level that changed it, with global.sort = ... or a name of its own in global. Left out, logged at err: skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (<module>: its top level called sleep(), which blocks the process: ...), or ... its top level changed the global scope, sort: ...; a loop, collector '<module>' hung at load. Always: the top level and collect() The collector API's exports (Result, errors, services, proc and exposition) and a Result's prototype are constant. Every collector loaded with the API shares them, so writing over one, Result.ok = ..., fails with object value is immutable. At the top level, the module is left out: skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (<module>: its top level wrote over what the collector API exports, which no collector may change: ...). In collect(), the run fails with COLLECTOR_CRASHED. prometheus-exporter collector check, the repository's tests, and a collector package's tests with the devkit The module's text, outside the bodies of its functions: no statement but declarations, and no call but to the functions above. FAIL its top level calls getenv() (line 4): ..., FAIL its top level runs 'for' (line 6): ....

push, pop, shift, unshift, splice and sort change the array they are given. At the top level they can only reach the module's own arrays, because the API's values are constant, so the top level may call them. It may not call proto: every collector shares a Result's prototype.

The loader does not read the module's text. Reading a module a character at a time would cost a router's uhttpd seconds when it starts. Instead, the guard around each load refuses each forbidden call as the module makes it. The text check does not read a function that the top level calls through map() or sort(), but the guard holds that function to the rules as it runs. See Error codes.

docs.title: meta
docs.text:
Field Required Type Rules name yes string [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*. The module's file name is the name with _ for -: ltq-dsl in ltq_dsl.uc. collect[] takes this name, and it is the suffix of the collector's package. title yes string 1 to 40 characters, no control characters: a label for lists and forms. help yes string A sentence: what it collects, and from where. needs yes array Capabilities from needs, each once. deps gets only these. configs with uci array The uci configs it reads, [a-z0-9_-]+. Not prometheus-exporter: the collector gets its own settings as options. Not allowed without uci. commands with exec array The programs it runs. Not allowed without exec. optional_commands no array The commands it runs only where they are installed. No package it depends on provides them, and the jail works without them. timeout no integer With exec: the seconds its programs get in total per scrape, 1 to 30. Its section's timeout overrides it. Without either, the main section's exec_timeout applies. max_samples no integer The samples it may write per scrape, 1 to 100,000. Its section's max_samples overrides it. Without either, the main section's max_samples (20,000) applies. cost no string light (the default) or heavy. Until the ledger has timed it, a heavy collector runs after the other collectors not yet timed. options no object Its own options, { <name>: { default, title, help, datatype } }. See Options. paths no array What it reads outside procfs and sysfs, with fs, socket or exec in needs. See The jail. ubus with ubus object The ubus objects and methods it calls, { <object>: [ <method> ] }, each object once. <name>.* stands for every object whose name starts with <name>. (hostapd's hostapd.*). Where an option decides the methods, a function of the options can replace the list and return one ([] for none). A call it does not list fails with UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED. The service's ubus ACL allows what the enabled collectors list. Not allowed without ubus. capabilities no array The capabilities its reads or programs need: CAP_NET_ADMIN (nftables, ctnetlink), CAP_NET_RAW. groups no array The groups whose sockets it connects to, such as unbound for unbound's control socket, which is srw-rw----. proc_files with fs array The files of /proc that only root can read and that it reads, such as /proc/net/nf_conntrack.

The jail says what ubus, capabilities, groups and proc_files grant, and when.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Key Required Rules (the name) [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. Not enabled, timeout, budget or max_samples: those belong to the core. default yes A boolean, an integer or a string. It sets the option's type. title yes 1 to 40 characters, no control characters. The label a form shows for the option: short and in sentence case, such as Excluded devices. LuCI shows it as the collector gives it, untranslated. help yes A sentence: what the option does. datatype no One of the datatypes the core checks: uinteger, range(min,max), directory, file, regex, ipaddr (an IPv4 or IPv6 address, without a prefix), or owned_directory (a directory under /var, /tmp or /etc/prometheus-exporter, for an option that names an owned path). The default must pass it. See UCI configuration.

collect gets the options typed, with the default for each option left unset. A value that does not fit its option fails the collector with CONFIG_INVALID in every scrape.

docs.title: collect(deps, out, options)
docs.text:
Argument Content deps One capability per entry of meta.needs, by name. out The recorder the collector writes its families to. options Its own options, typed.

collect returns a Result. If it returns anything else, it fails with COLLECTOR_NO_RESULT. If it throws, it fails with COLLECTOR_CRASHED. The exporter keeps what the collector recorded when it fails. It drops it when the collector has nothing to observe, or when the exporter stopped it (see Collector contract).

The collectors run one after the other in a child process forked from the scrape's process. A collector shares nothing with the collectors before and after it but that process's ubus connection and uci cursor. It must not end the process (exit()).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The collector API's Result:

Call Means node_scrape_collector_success node_scrape_collector_observing Logged Result.ok() It observed what it reads. 1 1 No Result.err(code, details, data) It failed: code from the API's errors, details a string for the log. 0 1 At warning: collector '<name>': CODE (details) Result.none(reason) Nothing to observe: its hardware, kernel feature or service is not there. Its samples are dropped. 1 0 No

Result.is(r) tells whether r is a Result, and Result.is_none(r) whether it is one of nothing to observe. Result.describe(r) gives CODE (details).

docs.title: services
docs.text:
The collector API's services helps a collector tell nothing to observe from a failure. Its functions work over deps.ubus:

Function Returns unless_disabled(ubus, name, failure) Result.none('<name> is disabled') or Result.none('<name> is not installed') when rpcd's rc says the init script name is not enabled or not there. failure otherwise, or when rc cannot say. idle(ubus, name) That reason, or null. state(ubus, name) A Result of enabled, disabled or not installed. object_missing(res) Whether a ubus call failed because its object is not there (Not found).

docs.title: The collector API
docs.text:
prometheus.exporter is the only module a collector imports. It exports five objects, each with exactly the names below, and two functions. These exports are what a major version protects; see Collector contract.

Export Name Is Result ok, err, none, is, is_none, describe See Results. errors SOURCE_UNREADABLE, SOURCE_INVALID, CONFIG_INVALID The codes a collector fails with on its own. UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED, UBUS_CALL_FAILED, UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED, NL80211_FAILED, RTNL_FAILED, SOCKET_FAILED, COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED, COMMAND_FAILED, COMMAND_TIMEOUT, PERMISSION_DENIED, SCRAPE_DEADLINE, EXPOSITION_INVALID The codes its capabilities and out.parse fail with. See Error codes. services state, idle, unless_disabled, object_missing, ENABLED, DISABLED, NOT_INSTALLED, NOT_FOUND See services. proc first_line(fs, path) The first line of a file, without its newline; null when it cannot be read. lines(fs, path) Every line, without newlines; null when it cannot be read. each_line(fs, path, cb) cb(line) for each line, read one at a time; false when it cannot be read. fields(line) The whitespace-separated fields of a line; [] for none or for null. rows(fs, path) The fields of every line, as fields() gives them, with [] for a blank line; null when it cannot be read. For a file of single spaces, it is cheaper than fields() on each line. auxv(text), AT_PAGESZ, AT_CLKTCK An auxiliary vector as /proc/self/auxv gives it, as { type: value }, or null. AT_PAGESZ and AT_CLKTCK are two of its types. exposition parse(text) Exposition text read strictly, as a Result of its families (EXPOSITION_INVALID). format_value(v) A value as the format spells it, or null for one that is not a number. sanitize(name) A metric name made valid: each character the format does not allow becomes an underscore. u32 u32(v) Makes a ubus integer unsigned again when a daemon sent it as unsigned 32 bits (blobmsg_add_u32). ucode's ubus gives it signed, so 4294967295 arrives as -1. Anything but a negative 32-bit integer comes back unchanged. u16 u16(v) The same, for 16 bits (blobmsg_add_u16): a port of 51820 arrives as -13716.

fs is the collector's deps.fs.

Each exported object lists exactly the names a collector may use, rather than re-exporting a whole core module. That list is what a major version protects. Every collector compiles its own copy of each module it imports. So the API imports only small modules, and loads the exposition format only the first time one of the exposition functions is called.

docs.title: needs
docs.text:
Only prometheus.exporter.deps touches the system, through its module for each capability (prometheus.exporter.deps.ubus, .exec, ...). A collector gets the capabilities it names. A scrape's collectors share one ubus connection and one uci cursor.

Need deps.<need> fs readfile, open, lsdir, glob, stat, realpath of the fs module. Nothing that writes. ubus call(object, method, args) and list(), as Results. A call that meta.ubus does not list is UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED, and is not made. A failed call is UBUS_CALL_FAILED, with libubus's text in data.status, such as Not found. A call the service's ubus ACL refuses is PERMISSION_DENIED. So is an object not found while ubusd has not loaded the ACL. list() names the objects the ACL lets the service call. uci deps.uci.<config> for each of meta.configs, read-only, the committed configuration only: loaded(), get(section, option), get_all(section), sections(type), foreach(type, cb). rtnl request(cmd, flags, attrs) as a Result (RTNL_FAILED), and const. nl80211 The same, for nl80211 (NL80211_FAILED). Needs ucode-mod-nl80211. socket unix_request(path, message, timeout_ms): the whole reply of a Unix stream socket's server, as a Result (SOCKET_FAILED). tcp_request(address, port, message, timeout_ms): the same, for a TCP port of the device itself. The address must be one of the device's own IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, and the socket binds to it before it connects. Any other address fails with SOCKET_FAILED, without connecting. timeout_ms bounds every wait: to connect, to send and to read. The reply is what the server sent until it closed. Needs ucode-mod-socket. exec run(argv) runs a program of meta.commands, with no shell interpreting its arguments, and gives its standard output as a Result. run_all(argvs) runs several, one after the other under one watchdog, and gives a Result for each, as run does. See Programs. time now(): the system time, in seconds. log log(msg) logs a line at warning, collector '<name>': <msg>, for what a collector that succeeds still has to say. At most 10 lines a run, each cut at 512 bytes. Past them, one line after the run says how many more were left out. exporter The exporter itself, read-only, for the exporter collector. process(file) reads the serving uhttpd's /proc/<pid>/stat, status or limits. fds() counts the descriptors it has open. system(file) reads /proc/stat or /proc/self/auxv. The instance's ledger counts, and each collector's samples, are written by the scrape itself while the exporter collector is selected (see Metrics).

The collector fails with NEED_MISSING, without running, when the system lacks one of its needs (nl80211, socket). It fails with PERMISSION_DENIED, also without running, when the process:

  • lacks a capability of meta.capabilities;
  • may not read a config of meta.configs;
  • may not read a file of meta.proc_files that is there. Read as anyone else, the file would look missing, and the collector would report nothing to observe.

A Unix socket it may not connect to (EACCES) is PERMISSION_DENIED too.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
• A program not in meta.commands is COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED, and does not run.
  • Its standard error is discarded. An exit status other than 0 is COMMAND_FAILED, with data.status. A program that cannot start is COMMAND_FAILED with data.status null.
  • A collector's programs share a number of seconds per scrape: its section's timeout, else meta.timeout, else the main section's exec_timeout (5), at most 30. The shell counts whole seconds, so the programs take at most one second more.
  • When the seconds are spent, the watchdog kills the program still running, with every process it started. That program is COMMAND_TIMEOUT, with data.timed_out. Any later run is COMMAND_TIMEOUT too, and does not run.
  • run_all runs its programs one after another in one shell. Each costs a fork and an exec, where each run also costs a shell and a watchdog: a few milliseconds a program on a router. The programs share the seconds as run's do. When the seconds are spent, the watchdog kills the program still running, as with run. The programs before it keep their Results, and those after it are COMMAND_TIMEOUT without running. A batch that cannot start is COMMAND_FAILED for each program.

docs.title: out
docs.text:
out is the recorder of prometheus.exporter.exposition:

Call Does out.gauge(name, help), out.counter(name, help), out.untyped(name, help) Declares a family, and returns (labels, value), which records a sample and returns itself, so calls chain. out.batch(type, rows) Records families of one sample each. For each row [ name, help, value, labels ], in order, it records what out[type](name, help)(labels, value) would, with less work. labels is optional, as for a writer: null, an object, or what out.labels() made. type is 'gauge', 'counter' or 'untyped'. out.labels(labels) Makes a label set once, for several samples to share. Pass it in place of the object. out.parse(text) Adds exposition text, which must be valid as a whole: a Result, EXPOSITION_INVALID otherwise.
  • labels is an object, null for none, or what out.labels() made. A label whose value is null is left out.
  • A value that is not a number (null, an empty string, a word) is skipped. A string of digits, or of hex as in sysfs flags, is read as a number. true and false are 1 and 0.
  • Names are made valid: each character the format does not allow becomes an underscore.
  • A family declared twice with two types keeps the first type, and a warning is logged.
  • A collector writes at most max_samples samples in all. The next one stops the collector: out throws, and throws again at each later sample. The collector fails with SAMPLE_LIMIT.

  • out refuses anything that would make Prometheus refuse the whole scrape:

    • a label value or HELP text that is not valid UTF-8, or holds a NUL byte;
    • a family name that holds a NUL byte;
    • a label name Prometheus reserves: __name__, or any that starts with __, as written or once sanitized;
    • two label names that become one once sanitized (if-name and if_name);
    • labels given as a string of the collector's own.

    Such a sample stops the collector, as the one past max_samples does. The collector fails with EXPOSITION_INVALID, naming the family and the label. - A family belongs to the first collector that writes it. A collector that writes another collector's family, or one of the exporter's own (node_scrape_collector_*, ucode_prometheus_exporter_*), fails with FAMILY_CONFLICT.

docs.title: Tests and packaging
docs.text:
Every collector has a unit test, test/unit/prometheus/collectors/<module>_test.uc, and a package. The package is either the base package, through BASE_COLLECTORS, or a Collector line of the package Makefile, which depends on what the collector's needs and commands call for. test/integration/collectors_test.uc checks both for every collector. See How to package a collector.

A unit test runs the collector with the devkit's with_collector (prometheus.exporter.devkit.collector). It fails the test when the collector touches a path, a socket or a program that its meta does not declare: see Collector contract and The devkit. A collector of another package is tested the same way, with ucode-prometheus-exporter-devkit: see How to write a collector in your own package.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
The base package, ucode-prometheus-exporter, installs conntrack, cpu, entropy, exporter, filefd, loadavg, meminfo, netclass, netdev, openwrt_interfaces, selinux, softnet, time, timesync, uname, vmstat. Every other collector is a package of its own, ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>, which depends on the base package of the same release. A group package installs no files, only its collectors.

Group package For Collectors ucode-prometheus-exporter-network network statistics ethtool, nat_traffic, netstat, nft-counters, qdisc, snmp6, sockstat ucode-prometheus-exporter-wireless Wi-Fi hostapd_stations, hostapd_ubus_stations, wifi ucode-prometheus-exporter-hardware hardware and filesystems diskstats, filesystem, hwmon, thermal ucode-prometheus-exporter-full a router or access point ethtool, nat_traffic, netstat, nft-counters, qdisc, snmp6, sockstat, hostapd_stations, hostapd_ubus_stations, wifi, diskstats, filesystem, hwmon, thermal, dhcp_leases, dnsmasq, openwrt, textfile, uci_dhcp_host, wireguard

In no group: agh, bmx7, chrony, dawn, interrupts, ltq-dsl, mmc, modemmanager, mwan3, pressure, realtek-poe, ubnt-manager, unbound.

docs.title: Nothing to observe
docs.text:
These collectors can have nothing to observe: they succeed without samples, and their node_scrape_collector_observing is 0. Every other collector fails when it cannot read what it reads. The reasons are what check, the ubus object's status and LuCI's status page show.

Collector Nothing to observe when Reasons it gives Still a failure agh AdGuard Home disabled, or not installed, and nothing answers at the collector's address and port. adguardhome is disabled, adguardhome is not installed AdGuard Home enabled, and nothing answering there; a reply that is not its API's; or one that asks for a login, which the collector does not send. bmx7 bmx7 disabled, or not installed. bmx7 is disabled, bmx7 is not installed bmx7 enabled, and its status files unreadable. chrony chronyd disabled, or not installed. chronyd is disabled, chronyd is not installed chronyd enabled, and chronyc failing (chronyd stopped). conntrack nf_conntrack not loaded: none of its files in /proc/sys/net/netfilter. no connection tracking (nf_conntrack is not loaded) Its files there, but unreadable. dawn DAWN disabled, or not installed. dawn is disabled, dawn is not installed DAWN enabled, and its dawn object missing or failing. dhcp_leases dnsmasq disabled, not installed, or without an instance in /etc/config/dhcp; and odhcpd disabled or not installed. When one of them is enabled, the collector observes that one. dnsmasq is disabled, dnsmasq is not installed, odhcpd is disabled, odhcpd is not installed An enabled server that is not there: no dnsmasq lease file, odhcpd not on ubus. diskstats device_exclude leaves out every block device in /proc/diskstats (by default: flash, loop devices, zram and partitions), as on a router without a disk. Or there is no block device at all. device_exclude leaves out every block device, no block devices /proc/diskstats missing or unreadable, or a malformed line for a device it exports. dnsmasq dnsmasq disabled, or not installed. dnsmasq is disabled, dnsmasq is not installed dnsmasq enabled, and its dnsmasq object missing or failing. hostapd_stations As wifi, or no hostapd.<ifname> object for any interface. no wireless radios, no hostapd access points A hostapd object that does not answer. hostapd_ubus_stations No hostapd.* object. no hostapd access points A hostapd object that does not answer. ltq-dsl No dsl object. no DSL modem (no dsl on ubus) A dsl object that does not answer. mmc No eMMC that reports its health: no MMC host; only SD or SDIO cards, which have no life_time or pre_eol_info; or an eMMC older than 5.0, whose fields are 0 (not defined). no eMMC reports its health A life_time or pre_eol_info there, but not as the kernel writes it. modemmanager ModemManager disabled or not installed, or it lists no modem. ModemManager lists no modems, modemmanager is disabled, modemmanager is not installed ModemManager enabled, and mmcli failing or running out of time. mwan3 mwan3 disabled, or not installed. mwan3 is disabled, mwan3 is not installed Its mwan3 object failing. mwan3 enabled but stopped is a reading, not a failure: mwan3_interface_running 0. nat_traffic nf_conntrack not loaded: no /proc/net/nf_conntrack. no connection tracking (nf_conntrack is not loaded) The file there, but unreadable. pressure No /proc/pressure: a kernel without CONFIG_PSI, or booted with psi=0. no PSI (no /proc/pressure: a kernel without CONFIG_PSI, or booted with psi=0) /proc/pressure there, but its cpu, io or memory unreadable or not as the kernel writes it. realtek-poe No poe object. no PoE switch (no poe on ubus) A poe object that does not answer. snmp6 No /proc/net/dev_snmp6 (IPv6 disabled). no IPv6 (no /proc/net/dev_snmp6) The directory there, but unreadable. timesync Neither busybox ntpd nor chronyd runs, by procd's instances (the service's ubus object's time_daemons). sysntpd runs ntpd only while /etc/config/system turns NTP on. When one of them runs, the collector observes that one. neither ntpd nor chronyd runs chronyd enabled and not running, or chronyc failing; busybox ntpd's event file unreadable. ubnt-manager ubnt-manager not installed, or ubnt-manager -l lists no radio. ubnt-manager is not installed, ubnt-manager lists no radios A radio that fails or does not answer. unbound unbound disabled, or not installed. unbound is disabled, unbound is not installed unbound enabled, and its control socket not answering. wifi The wireless config has no radio: the service's ubus object's wireless gives none. no wireless radios Another failed call, or an interface that is there but that nl80211 cannot answer for. An interface that is not there, because its network is not set up, is left out. wireguard rpcd has no wireguard object: rpcd-mod-wireguard not installed. rpcd has no wireguard object: rpcd-mod-wireguard is not installed Any other failure of wireguard status.

docs.title: The prometheus-exporter Command
docs.text:
/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter, installed by the package ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli. It prints a scrape on standard output, checks the service and a collector module, and hashes a password for basic auth. It parses its arguments with docopt (the ucode-docopt package, which only this package depends on) by the usage below, which -h also prints. The service needs none of it. Its init script checks the configuration with the base package's own /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc, which check also runs. The ubus object sets basic auth's password (set_password, LuCI's **Change password**). apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli installs it.

prometheus-exporter: metrics of OpenWrt for Prometheus.

Usage:
  prometheus-exporter scrape [--dir=<dir>] [<collector>...]
  prometheus-exporter check [--config]
  prometheus-exporter collector list [--dir=<dir>]
  prometheus-exporter collector check <path>
  prometheus-exporter hash-password
  prometheus-exporter -h | --help
  prometheus-exporter --version

Commands:
  scrape            Print a scrape, as /metrics answers it: of every enabled
                    collector, or of those named, in that order. Each runs as
                    the service runs it, in a child process of the scrape,
                    stopped at its budget, within scrape_timeout.
  check             Check the configuration, describe the installed
                    collectors and run a scrape of them, as the init script's
                    check does.
  collector list    List the installed collectors: name, whether enabled, and
                    what each collects.
  collector check   Check a collector module before it is installed: load it,
                    run it on this device as the service would, and say what
                    it wrote and which rule of the collector contract it
                    broke, if any.
  hash-password     Read a password, without echoing it on a terminal, and
                    print the hash auth_password takes.

Options:
  -d <dir>, --dir=<dir>  Load the collectors from <dir>, a directory on
                         ucode's module path, not the installed ones.
  --config               Check the configuration alone, as start and reload do.
  -h, --help             Show this help.
  --version              Show the version.

Up to 0.1, the command took only collectors, prometheus-exporter [COLLECTOR...], and -l listed them. They are now prometheus-exporter scrape [<collector>...] and prometheus-exporter collector list. Given arguments the usage does not take, the command prints the usage on standard error, and exits with status 1.

docs.title: prometheus-exporter scrape
docs.text:
Prints a scrape on standard output, as /metrics answers it: of every enabled collector, or of the collectors named, in that order, by name (ltq-dsl) or module (ltq_dsl). For cron and push (see How to push metrics), and for debugging.

  • Each collector runs as the service runs it: in a child process of the scrape, one after the other, stopped at its budget, with at most its max_samples, and with families of its own. The scrape has the main section's scrape_timeout (see Collector contract).
  • It has no ledger: nothing is quarantined, and the collectors run in their order, slow ones too, within the scrape's time.
  • --dir loads the collectors of a directory on ucode's module path, such as a source tree's with ucode -L src, instead of the installed ones.
  • It never compresses and never asks for basic auth: those are the HTTP endpoint's.
Exit status When 0 The scrape was printed, whatever its collectors did. 1 The scrape was refused, for a collector that is not installed or that is disabled. It says why on standard error, such as COLLECTOR_INVALID (unknown collector 'nope'). 
$ prometheus-exporter scrape loadavg
# HELP node_load1 1m load average.
# TYPE node_load1 gauge
node_load1 0.72
...
ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="0.2.0-r1"} 1

docs.title: prometheus-exporter check
docs.text:
Checks the configuration as the exporter and the init script read it, and describes every installed collector: its section, options, needs, and what the jail gives it. Then it runs a scrape of the enabled collectors, each as the service runs it, in the service's jail where ujail can run. Last, it shows what the service's own scrapes found: each collector quarantined, and each the deadline left out lately. service prometheus-exporter check runs the same, the base package's /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc, without the command line. With --config, it checks only the configuration, as start and reload do. See Service commands.

Exit status When 0 The configuration is valid, whatever the collectors did. 1 It is not: a line starts FAIL.

docs.title: prometheus-exporter collector list
docs.text:
Prints a line per installed collector: its name, enabled or disabled, and what it collects.

  • --dir lists a directory's, as scrape loads them.
Exit status When 0 Always. 
$ prometheus-exporter collector list
conntrack                enabled  Connection tracking table usage, from /proc/sys/net/netfilter.
cpu                      enabled  CPU time per mode, from /proc/stat.
...

docs.title: prometheus-exporter collector check
docs.text:
Checks a collector module before it is installed, on the device it is meant for: whether it keeps the collector contract. It reads <path>, which must be <module>.uc, and checks its text for strict mode and its imports. It loads the module under the load timer (5 s), validates its meta, and runs it as the service would: in a child process, with at most its budget and its max_samples. It says how long the module took to load and to run, the samples it wrote, and its families. Then it checks that its text is valid exposition with each series once, and whether an installed collector or the exporter already writes one of its families.

  • A line starts ok, warn or FAIL. Each broken rule is a FAIL: not in strict mode; importing a module other than prometheus.exporter, or calling require, loadfile, loadstring, include or system, with the text the loader logs (FAIL imports fs (line 3): a collector reads files through deps.fs, with 'fs' in meta.needs); not loading, or not in time; a meta that is not valid; stopped at its budget or at the deadline, killed, over its max_samples, crashing, or not returning a Result; text that is not valid; a family another collector writes.
  • A failure that comes from the device (SOURCE_*, UBUS_*, COMMAND_FAILED, NEED_MISSING) is a warn, and so is nothing to observe: the collector may do its job on another device.
  • An installed module of the same name is left out of the families the module is compared with, so a new version of a collector can be checked beside the old one.
Exit status When 0 No rule is broken. 1 One is: a line starts FAIL. 
$ prometheus-exporter collector check /tmp/apk_updates.uc
ok   strict mode: 'use strict' first
ok   imports: prometheus.exporter alone
ok   top level: declarations alone
ok   load: 0.004 s, of at most 5 s
ok   meta: apk_updates (APK updates), needs exec, budget 6 s, max_samples 20000
ok   run: 0.412 s, 3 samples in 2 families
ok   families: apk_upgradable_packages apk_installed_packages
ok   exposition: valid text, each series once

docs.title: prometheus-exporter hash-password
docs.text:
Reads a password and prints its hash: SHA-512-crypt of 1000 rounds, freshly salted, the value auth_password takes. From a terminal, it asks for the password without echoing it. Otherwise it reads the first line of standard input. It never prints the password, and never takes it as an argument, where ps would show it.

Exit status When 0 The hash was printed. 1 No password, or one it does not accept. It says why on standard error. 
$ prometheus-exporter hash-password
Password:
$6$rounds=1000$...

docs.title: Everywhere
docs.text:
• It reads the committed configuration, as the service does: it leaves out a collector disabled in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, and refuses a query that names one.
  • scrape and check run the collectors in the service's jail where ujail can run. scrape --dir and collector check run them outside the jail, as the user who runs the command. A collector that works there and fails under the service lacks something in the jail; see The jail.
  • The exporter's log goes to standard error, whatever its level.
  • The version (--version, and the build info's version) is the package's, <version>-r<release>, or dev from a source tree.

docs.title: The Devkit
docs.text:
ucode-prometheus-exporter-devkit tests collectors under utest: the exporter's own collectors, and those of any other package. It installs its modules to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/. It depends on the exporter of the same release, ucode-utest, ucode-mod-nl80211 and ucode-mod-socket. It is for a development machine or a CI image, not for a router.

A major version of the exporter protects the devkit as it protects the collector API: what its modules export, and what their configs and callbacks hold. See About versions. How to write a collector in your own package shows how to use it.

docs.title: The utest config
docs.text:
A collector package's test/utest.config.uc, like the template's, puts the package's module on the path, and names the mocks that with_collector builds a collector's capabilities from.

return {
    pattern: '*_test.uc',
    lib_paths: [ '../src' ],
    mocks: {
        fs:      null,
        uci:     null,
        ubus:    { proxy: '/usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/proxies/ubus.uc' },
        rtnl:    { proxy: '/usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/proxies/rtnl.uc' },
        nl80211: { proxy: '/usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/proxies/nl80211.uc' },
        socket:  { proxy: '/usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/proxies/socket.uc' },
    },
};

All six mocks are needed, whatever the collector needs, because with_collector builds the session of every capability. fs and uci use utest's own proxies.

docs.title: prometheus.exporter.devkit.collector
docs.text: Export Is with_collector(mod, cfg, cb) Runs the collector module mod (its exports) as a scrape does, with only its needs, over the mocks of cfg. Then it calls cb(r) with the run. Before cb runs, it holds the collector to its contract, and fails the test with assert.fail() on a breach: see Collector contract. It asserts nothing about the Result: the test does. outcome(r) { ok, none, error, lines, logs } of a run: what a test checks of a run that fails or has nothing to observe. jail_of(mod, cfg) What the service's jail gives the collector: its mounts, configs, commands, ubus calls and grants, as prometheus.exporter.jail works them out. with_mods(cfg, cb, id) Injects utest's mocks, and calls cb with module-shaped objects for a session, shaped like the exporter's real modules. id puts cfg.options in that collector's section. module_problems(text) What the loader and collector check refuse in a module's text, before loading it, each with its line: not in strict mode, an import other than the collector API, a top level that does more than declare. [] for none. assert_module(path) Fails the test when module_problems() finds any problem in the file at path. MOCKED [ 'fs', 'ubus', 'uci', 'rtnl', 'nl80211', 'socket' ], the mocks the utest config names.

docs.title: cfg
docs.text:
Every key is optional.

Key Is fs, ubus, uci, rtnl, nl80211, socket Each mock's config, as utest and the proxies below take it: { data, errors, behavior, strict }. A mock is strict unless its config says strict: false: a call it holds no data for fails the test. options The collector's own options, its config collector section, as uci holds them: strings, '0' and '1' for a boolean. main The exporter's main section. no_nl80211, no_rtnl, no_socket As if that module were not installed: the collector fails with NEED_MISSING. time What deps.time.now() returns. self_status The text of /proc/self/status that the session checks meta.capabilities against. unreadable The paths the service's user may not read (a config, a proc file). Without it, nothing is checked. outside_jail Paths that a collector looks for even though the jail never has them, for when it runs outside the jail. The mocks answer them, and the contract check lets them be. files, absent For jail_of() only: the regular files that commands are found among, and the paths that are not there. Any other path exists, as a directory.

docs.title: The run, r
docs.text:
Field Is result The collector's Result. text, lines What it wrote, as the exposition format, and its lines. logs, levels What the scrape and the collector logged, and the level of each. families Its families as the format reads them back: { name, type, help, samples }.

The devkit records a breach of the contract during the run, and fails the test after it, never from inside. Inside, the collector's error boundary would take the failure for a crash, and a collector that falls back on a default (readfile(p) ?? '') would pass.

docs.title: prometheus.exporter.devkit.fixtures
docs.text: Export Is reader(dir) A reader of the fixtures under dir, relative to where utest runs, or absolute (sourcepath(0, true) gives a test's own directory). It has:- file(path): a file's text, by the path it has on the device (<dir>/proc/loadavg for /proc/loadavg);- files(paths): several files, as an fs mock's data;- ubus(object, method): the JSON of <dir>/ubus/<object>.<method>.json.A fixture that is not there fails the test, naming it.

docs.title: prometheus.exporter.devkit.commands
docs.text:
For a collector that needs exec: an fs mock whose popen answers each program as the exec capability runs it, under its watchdog.

Export Is fs(outputs, extra) An fs mock config whose popen answers outputs[line(argv)]. Each value is one of:- { out, status };- { hangs: true }: a program its watchdog killed (COMMAND_TIMEOUT);- { run: argv, seconds }: argv runs for real, under the real watchdog.A command line that outputs does not hold cannot start (COMMAND_FAILED). It answers the batch of a run_all() too, each program as if alone; a program that hangs stops the batch there. A batch with a command line outputs does not hold cannot start. extra is merged into the config: its data, for example. line(argv) A command line as the capability runs it, each argument single-quoted: the key of outputs. parse(script) { seconds, line } of a script the capability gives popen, or null. parse_batch(script) { seconds, mark, lines } of the script of a run_all(), or null: its seconds, the mark of the line after each program's output, and each program's command line. running(text) The command lines of the processes whose command line holds text, looked for again for up to a second. A test uses it to check that no process a program started outlives it. 
with_collector(mine, { fs: commands.fs({ [commands.line([ 'tc', '-s', '-j', 'qdisc', 'show' ])]: { out: '[]', status: 0 } }) }, (r) => ...);

docs.title: prometheus.exporter.devkit.rc
docs.text:
For a collector that tells a disabled service from a failure, with the API's services.

Export Is rc(scripts) A ubus mock's data of rpcd's rc list, as 25.12's rpcd answers it: { 'rc:list': ... }. It answers { <name>: { start, enabled } } for an init script that scripts names, and {}, not installed, for any other. Merge it: { ...rc({ dnsmasq: true }), 'dnsmasq:metrics': ... }. list(scripts) Its method, a function of the call's arguments.

docs.title: The proxies
docs.text:
proxies/<name>.uc are utest proxies, which the utest config names. Each takes data, keyed as below, and the channels below. Each records every call, as utest's proxies do.

Proxy Keys Channels ubus object:method, or object for every method of it. A value is a reply, or a function of the call's arguments that returns one. errors: the message error() reports after the call, which then returns null (Not found, Permission denied). list() names every object data names. list(path) answers [ {} ] for one of them and for system, or [] for list:<path> in errors. rtnl The command as rtnl's constants name it, with the device where the request has one: RTM_GETLINK:eth0, else RTM_GETLINK. A value is a reply, or a function of (flags, attrs). errors: the message after that request fails. nl80211 As rtnl's: NL80211_CMD_GET_STATION:phy0-ap0. errors. socket A Unix socket's path; a TCP port's address:port, [address]:port for IPv6 (127.0.0.1:8080, [::1]:3000). A value is the server's whole reply, or a function of the request. errors: the message after connect() fails there (connect(): Connection refused).hangs: the server replies and never closes, so the next read times out.addresses: the device's own addresses, besides loopback and the unspecified ones, that a TCP socket may bind() to ({ '192.168.1.1': true }). Any other fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL.Any other path is missing (ENOENT); any other port refuses (ECONNREFUSED).

The devkit ships its own proxies because utest 1.5 has none for rtnl, nl80211 or socket, and its ubus proxy lacks list() and error(). commands.fs() replaces utest's popen mock, whose handle closes without the exit status that 25.12's ucode gives. The proxies are programs, hence their top-level return.

  • Collector interface and Collector contract

docs.title: Documentation Publishing
docs.text: The docs workflow, .github/workflows/docs.yml, publishes the documentation to the gh-pages branch with mike, one version per minor release. Make targets lists the targets that build and test it locally. For the reasons behind this design, see About versioned documentation.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Event Ref Job Publishes Version title Push of a tag v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example v0.2.1 publish version X.Y X.Y.Z, the tag without its v Push to a branch docs/[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example docs/0.2 publish version X.Y, if the docs-only guard passes the newest vX.Y.* tag without its v Push to a branch main build nothing — Pull request into main build nothing — Manual run (workflow_dispatch) the input ref: a release tag vX.Y.Z or a branch docs/X.Y publish as for a push of that ref as for a push of that ref

Branch pushes and pull requests start the workflow only when they change at least one of these paths. Tag pushes and manual runs always start it.

  • docs/**
  • mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml
  • devenv/gh-pages/**
  • devenv/scripts/docs-*.sh
  • devenv/services/docs/**
  • test/docs/**
  • .github/workflows/docs.yml

Nothing else publishes: main, pull requests and pre-release tags such as v0.3.0-rc1 never reach gh-pages.

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Runs on pull requests and on pushes to main.

  1. make -C docs build: strict build with mkdocs.yml.
  2. make -C docs build-mike: strict build with mkdocs.mike.yml.
  3. make -C docs test: the shell and Node tests in test/docs/. The generator's tests in test/docs/gen/ run with make test.

docs.title: publish
docs.text:
Runs on release tags, docs/* branches and manual runs. REF is the manual run's ref input, or else the pushed ref.

  1. Checks out REF with its full history and tags.
  2. Takes docs/Makefile from the commit the workflow runs from, which is REF on a push, because releases before 0.2.1 have no publish target. That Makefile runs on REF's checkout, with PROJECT_ROOT set to it.
  3. Sets the git committer to github-actions[bot], in the repository's config.
  4. build-mike: strict build with mkdocs.mike.yml, in the docs tools image built from REF's devenv/services/docs.
  5. publish: devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh "$REF" in the same image, with the network, and the checkout's credentials and committer from its .git/config.

docs.title: Permissions and concurrency
docs.text:
Setting Value Workflow permissions contents: read publish permissions contents: write publish concurrency group gh-pages, with cancel-in-progress: false

One publish job runs at a time; a later one waits. GitHub keeps at most one waiting job per concurrency group: a newer one cancels the one already waiting.

docs.title: The latest rule
docs.text:
A publish of version X.Y moves latest only when X.Y is the newest version. It compares X.Y with the version folders already on gh-pages, with sort -V: 0.10 is newer than 0.9.

  • If X.Y is the newest, the publish points latest to X.Y, and makes latest the default version.
  • Otherwise, latest stays where it is.

The first publish always takes latest.

The script prints which case applied:

publishing 0.10 (0.10.0) as latest
publishing 0.9 (0.9.1); latest stays on 0.10

docs.title: Site layout
docs.text:
The published site on gh-pages:

Path Written by Content /X.Y/ mike One folder per minor, without a v: 0.9, 0.10. /latest/ mike A full copy of the newest minor's folder (alias_type: copy), not a symlink or a redirect. /versions.json mike The versions, their titles and aliases, for the version selector. /index.html mike Redirects to /latest/ (mike set-default latest). /404.html docs-publish.sh Copy of devenv/gh-pages/404.html. See below. /.nojekyll docs-publish.sh Empty. Tells GitHub Pages to serve the files as they are.

Every page carries a version selector. With site_url set, its canonical URL is the same page under /latest/ (canonical_version: latest). Pages of a version that is not latest show a banner, docs/overrides/main.html:

You are reading the documentation of an older release. Go to the latest.

The link goes to the site's root, which redirects to /latest/.

docs.title: 404 redirect
docs.text:
GitHub Pages serves /404.html for every missing path. Its script redirects /<site>/<path> to /<site>/latest/<path>, keeping the query string and the #anchor. /<site> and /<site>/ go to /<site>/latest/.

It does not redirect, and shows "Page not found", when the first segment after /<site>/ is latest, dev or a version X.Y, or when the path is /. The first path segment is always taken as the site, so the redirect works only on a project site, https://<user>.github.io/<site>/.

docs.title: Docs-only guard
docs.text:
devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh runs before every publish of a docs/X.Y branch, whether pushed or run manually. It does not run for release tags. It checks the checked-out commit, HEAD, against the release tag of its minor:

  1. The tag is the newest tag of the form vX.Y.Z with the branch's X.Y, by sort -V: v0.9.10 is newer than v0.9.9. Other tags, such as v0.9.11-rc1, are ignored.
  2. The tag must be an ancestor of HEAD.
  3. HEAD may differ from the tag only in these files: anything under the top-level docs/, mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml. A docs/ folder anywhere else, such as src/docs/, does not count.

On success the guard prints the tag, which becomes the version's title. On failure it prints one of these messages on stderr, exits 1, and nothing is published:

Message Cause not a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The first argument is not a docs/ branch. not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The branch is docs/ but not docs/X.Y. docs/X.Y has no vX.Y.* release tag No release tag of that minor exists. <tag> is not a X.Y release The tag given as the second argument is of another minor. not a release tag: <tag> The second argument does not start with v. <tag> is not an ancestor of docs/X.Y The branch does not contain its newest release tag, for example after a patch release it has not moved to. docs/X.Y changes files outside docs/: <files>; code fixes need a release The branch changes other files than the docs. The files are listed, space-separated.

For example:

docs/0.2 changes files outside docs/: src/prometheus/exporter/app.uc; code fixes need a release

To run it locally, check out the branch, make sure the release tags are fetched, and pass the branch name:

devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh docs/0.2

docs.title: Links to the documentation
docs.text:
Where the link is It points to Always-current places: the README, the repository's homepage, forum posts <site_url>latest/... CHANGELOG.md <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the section the link is in Release notes <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the release Shipped files: everything under files/, src/ and luci/, and openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile (including URL:=) <site_url>X.Y/..., the package's current minor Pages of the documentation Relative paths, never the site's URL

site_url is the site's base URL without a version, set in mkdocs.yml, here https://m00qek.github.io/ucode-prometheus-exporter/.

docs.title: Link check
docs.text:
make lint runs devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh, which checks every pinned link, <site_url><X.Y>/, in the shipped files and in CHANGELOG.md:

  • site_url is read from mkdocs.yml, with or without quotes; a missing trailing / is added. While site_url is unset, nothing is checked and the check passes.
  • In shipped files the minor must be the one of PKG_VERSION in openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile: PKG_VERSION:=0.1.0 requires 0.1.
  • In CHANGELOG.md the minor must be the one of the enclosing ## [X.Y.Z] heading. Any other ## heading, such as ## [Unreleased], and the text before the first ## heading allow no pinned link at all. ### headings do not change the section.
  • Links to latest/ and links under other URLs are not checked.

CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog: ## [Unreleased] on top, then one ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section per release, newest first. Only the ## [X.Y.Z] part of the heading is read.

A failure prints every wrong link and exits 1:

pinned docs links to the wrong version:
files/etc/config/prometheus-exporter:1: https://example.org/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.9/ (expected 0.10)
CHANGELOG.md:5: https://example.org/ucode-prometheus-exporter/0.10/ (outside a release section)

docs.title: Files and scripts
docs.text: File Role .github/workflows/docs.yml The docs workflow: triggers, jobs. mkdocs.yml The site. Has no mike settings; make -C docs build and serve use it. mkdocs.mike.yml The versioned site: inherits mkdocs.yml and adds the search and mike plugins (canonical_version: latest, alias_type: copy), the version selector (extra.version.provider: mike) and the theme overrides in docs/overrides/. Used by build-mike and by the publish job. docs/overrides/main.html The outdated-version banner. devenv/gh-pages/404.html The 404 redirect, copied to the root of gh-pages on every publish. devenv/services/docs/Dockerfile The docs tools image, ucode-prometheus-exporter-docs: the mkdocs-material image plus requirements.txt, git, coreutils and Node. devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt Pinned mkdocs-material, mike, and mike's dependencies the mkdocs-material image lacks, for the tools image. devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh Maps a ref to its docs version. devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh The docs-only guard. devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh Publishes one version. devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh The link check. test/docs/*_test.sh, test/docs/404_test.js Tests of the four scripts and of the 404 redirect, run by make -C docs test.

docs.title: docs-version.sh REF
docs.text:
Prints the version X.Y of a release tag vX.Y.Z or of a branch docs/X.Y. REF may carry a refs/tags/ or refs/heads/ prefix. Anything else prints not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: REF on stderr and exits 1.

$ devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh refs/tags/v0.10.2
0.10

docs.title: docs-guard.sh BRANCH [TAG]
docs.text: Checks HEAD as the tip of BRANCH, docs/X.Y with an optional refs/heads/ prefix, against TAG, by default the newest vX.Y.Z tag of that minor. See Docs-only guard. Prints the tag and exits 0, or prints a message on stderr and exits 1.

docs.title: docs-publish.sh REF
docs.text:
Publishes the current checkout as version X.Y of REF, a release tag or a docs/X.Y branch, with an optional refs/ prefix, to origin's gh-pages. Run from the repository root, with mike installed and a git committer configured.

  1. Maps REF to its version with docs-version.sh. For a docs/ branch, it runs docs-guard.sh and takes the title from the tag the guard prints. For a tag, the title is the tag. Either way, the leading v is dropped.
  2. Fetches gh-pages from origin into the local gh-pages branch, if it exists there.
  3. Applies the latest rule: mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> --update-aliases X.Y latest and mike set-default -F mkdocs.mike.yml latest, or only mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> X.Y.
  4. Writes 404.html and .nojekyll to the root of gh-pages, in a separate commit, Root files: 404 redirect to latest, .nojekyll, only if they changed.
  5. Pushes gh-pages to origin.

It exits non-zero, before anything is pushed, if REF is not a release tag or a docs branch, or if the guard refuses.

docs.title: docs-links.sh [ROOT]
docs.text: Runs the link check on the repository at ROOT, by default the one the script is in. Exits 0 when every pinned link is right or site_url is unset, 1 otherwise.

docs.title: Pinned versions
docs.text:
Tool Version Pinned in mkdocs-material image squidfunk/mkdocs-material:9.5.17 MKDOCS_IMAGE in docs/Makefile mkdocs-material 9.5.17 devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt mike 2.1.3 devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt Docs tools image ucode-prometheus-exporter-docs:9.5.17, tag taken from MKDOCS_IMAGE docs/Makefile actions/checkout v4.4.0, by its commit .github/workflows/docs.yml

The publish job runs in the docs tools image, as build-mike and test do in the build job. The image pins each Python package it adds to the mkdocs-material image.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: A failure carries an uppercase code, from src/prometheus/exporter/errors.uc, and a detail. It is written CODE (detail), or CODE alone without one: in the log (collector '<name>': CODE (detail), see Log messages), in check, in the ubus object's replies and on LuCI's status page. A collector that fails has node_scrape_collector_success 0.

docs.title: Collectors and their sources
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by SOURCE_UNREADABLE A file the collector reads is not there or cannot be read. The detail names it. the collectors agh, bmx7, conntrack, cpu, dhcp_leases, diskstats, entropy, exporter, filefd, interrupts, loadavg, meminfo, nat_traffic, netstat, pressure, selinux, snmp6, sockstat, softnet, timesync, uci_dhcp_host, uname, vmstat SOURCE_INVALID What the collector read is not what it expects: a file, a ubus reply or a program's output it cannot parse. The detail says where. services.uc; the collectors agh, bmx7, chrony, conntrack, cpu, dawn, dhcp_leases, diskstats, dnsmasq, entropy, filefd, filesystem, hostapd_stations, interrupts, loadavg, ltq-dsl, meminfo, mmc, modemmanager, mwan3, netclass, netdev, netstat, nft-counters, openwrt, openwrt_interfaces, pressure, qdisc, realtek-poe, selinux, sockstat, softnet, time, timesync, ubnt-manager, unbound, vmstat, wifi, wireguard COLLECTOR_CRASHED The collector died with an exception. The detail is the exception's first line. conform.uc, scrape.uc COLLECTOR_NO_RESULT The collector returned something other than a Result, or a failure without an error code (a code the collector API does not export is null). The detail says what. conform.uc, runner.uc, scrape.uc COLLECTOR_INVALID A collector module whose meta or collect is not valid: the exporter leaves it out. Or a query that names a collector that is not installed, or one that is disabled: the exporter answers 400. loader.uc, scrape.uc COLLECTOR_IMPURE A collector module whose top level does more than declare. The exporter leaves it out. As it loaded, the top level called a function that blocks, ends or writes to the process (sleep, exit, print), loads code (require, loadstring, and so the collector API's exposition functions), or changes its signals. The call is refused before it runs, in the process that first loads the module and in uhttpd's, and the detail names it. Or the top level changed the global scope, which is put back, or wrote over what the collector API exports, which is constant; the detail says which. Or, in collector check and the tests, its text runs a statement or calls a function that a declaration does not; the detail names it and its line. See Collector interface. collection.uc

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by CONFIG_INVALID An option has a value the exporter does not take, or options that go together are not set together. The detail is <option>: expected <what>, got <value> (never the value of auth_password), or what is missing. auth.uc, config.uc, config/types.uc, conform.uc; the collectors diskstats, netstat, snmp6, vmstat FILE_UNWRITABLE The init script could not write or remove uhttpd's basic auth file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf; or the ubus object's set_password could not write the hash's config, /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth. auth.uc, rpc.uc

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by NEED_MISSING A capability the collector needs is not installed: nl80211 without ucode-mod-nl80211, socket without ucode-mod-socket. deps.uc UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED The exporter could not connect to ubus. deps/ubus.uc, rpc/sources.uc UBUS_CALL_FAILED A ubus call failed. The detail is <object> <method>: <status>, as Not found. deps/ubus.uc, rpc/sources.uc, services.uc; the collector filesystem NL80211_FAILED An nl80211 request failed. The detail is the device and the kernel's error. deps/netlink.uc RTNL_FAILED An rtnetlink request failed. The detail is the kernel's error. deps/netlink.uc SOCKET_FAILED A Unix socket is missing; a socket refused the connection, or stopped sending its reply before the timeout; or a TCP address is not one of the device's own. The detail names the socket, or the address and port. deps/socket.uc; the collector agh COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED The collector ran a program its meta.commands does not list. conform.uc, deps/exec.uc COMMAND_FAILED A program could not start or exited with a status other than 0. The detail is <program>: exit status <n> or <program>: cannot start. deps/exec.uc COMMAND_TIMEOUT A program was still running when the collector's seconds for programs ran out, so the exporter killed it, with every process it started. Or the collector asked to run a program after the seconds ran out. deps/exec.uc, ledger.uc UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED The collector called a ubus object or method that its meta.ubus does not list. The exporter refuses the call without making it, in the jail or not, as the service's ubus ACL would. The detail is <object> <method>. deps/ubus.uc PERMISSION_DENIED The system refused the service's user something the collector declared: a capability its process lacks, a config or a file of /proc it may not read, a socket it may not connect to, or a ubus call that ubusd denies, as when the service's ubus ACL is not loaded. The detail says what, and what grants it. The service grants each one when it starts with the collector enabled (see The jail). Never nothing to observe. deps.uc, deps/socket.uc, deps/ubus.uc

docs.title: The scrape
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by SCRAPE_DEADLINE The scrape's time was nearly spent, so the collector was not run, or a program it ran was killed at the deadline. This lets the scrape answer before the scraper gives up. The scrape logs every such collector in one line. See About deadlines and circuit breakers. conform.uc, deps/exec.uc, ledger.uc, runner.uc, scrape.uc COLLECTOR_QUARANTINED The collector's circuit breaker is open, so it was not run in this scrape, even if the query named it. The detail says what tripped the breaker, and when the collector is tried again. Restarting the service tries it at once. ledger.uc COLLECTOR_OVERRUN What tripped a breaker: the collector took longer than its budget. The detail is how long it took, and its budget. The run's own result stands, and its breaker trips. ledger.uc

docs.title: What the exporter enforces of a collector
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by COLLECTOR_CANCELLED The collector was still running at the end of its budget, so the exporter stopped it, with the process it ran in: a loop that never ends, or a system call that never returns. None of its samples are served, and its breaker trips. See Collector contract. conform.uc, ledger.uc, runner.uc COLLECTOR_KILLED The process the collector ran in ended while it ran: the collector went past the memory limit, a native module crashed, or it called exit(). Or the scrape process itself died while the collector ran, which the next scrape finds. None of its samples are served, and its breaker trips. conform.uc, ledger.uc, runner.uc COLLECTOR_NOT_RUN The collector was not run, through no fault of its own, so its breaker stays as it was. Either the processes the scrape forked to run the collectors ended twice in a row before they ran one, which is logged once for all of them. Or the scrape's process was asked to stop while they ran, and ends without a reply. runner.uc, scrape.uc SAMPLE_LIMIT The collector wrote more samples than its max_samples, and was stopped there. Or it wrote more than were left of the reply's max_scrape_samples, or none were left when it would have started; in these two cases its breaker stays as it was. The detail says how many, and in which family. None of its samples are served. conform.uc, ledger.uc, scrape.uc FAMILY_CONFLICT The collector wrote a family that another collector of the reply wrote first, or one the exporter keeps for itself (node_scrape_collector_*, ucode_prometheus_exporter_*). The detail names it. None of its samples are served. conform.uc, ownership.uc

docs.title: Exposition text
docs.text: Code Meaning Raised by EXPOSITION_INVALID Text that is not valid Prometheus exposition format. Either a *.prom file of textfile, which the collector then leaves out; the detail names the line. Or something a collector wrote that would make Prometheus refuse the whole scrape: a label value or HELP text that is not valid UTF-8 or holds a NUL byte; a family name that holds one; a label name Prometheus reserves (__name__, or any that starts with __, as written or once sanitized); two label names that become one once sanitized (if-name and if_name); or labels that are neither an object nor what out.labels() made. The recorder stops the collector there, and the detail names the family and the label. None of its samples are served. exposition/parse.uc, scrape.uc

docs.title: Files and Packages
docs.text:
Every package is built from openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, is architecture-independent (PKGARCH:=all), and has the version <PKG_VERSION>-r<PKG_RELEASE>. Each collector package, each group package, the command line's package and the LuCI app depend on the base package of the very same version.

The ucode and JavaScript files they install carry no comments. The build strips them (devenv/scripts/strip-comments.py), and keeps a newline for each line it empties, so a line number in an error on the device is the same line in the repository.

docs.title: ucode-prometheus-exporter
docs.text: The exporter, its service, its ubus object and the base collectors.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
uhttpd, uhttpd-mod-ucode, ucode, ucode-mod-fs, ucode-mod-ubus, ucode-mod-uci, ucode-mod-rtnl, ucode-mod-log, rpcd-mod-ucode (the ubus object), ucode-mod-uloop (its status without blocking rpcd), ucode-mod-zlib (gzip), ucode-mod-digest (basic auth's hashes).

It conflicts with prometheus-node-exporter-ucode and prometheus-node-exporter-lua: apk will not install it and either of them side by side.

It makes the user and group prometheus-exporter, which uhttpd runs as in the service's jail. See The jail.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Path Content /etc/config/prometheus-exporter The configuration. A conffile: an upgrade keeps it when it was changed. See UCI configuration. /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth The hash of basic auth's password, mode 0600, kept apart from the configuration that LuCI may read. A conffile too. See UCI configuration. /etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter The service. See Service commands. /etc/uci-defaults/prometheus-exporter-import Takes over a feed exporter's settings, once. See How to move from the feed's exporters. /etc/hotplug.d/ntp/90-prometheus-exporter Keeps busybox ntpd's last event for timesync. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc uhttpd's handler for /metrics. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc The check. service prometheus-exporter check runs it, and start and reload run check.uc --config. The command line's check runs the same. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/status.uc What status prints of a running service. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/jail.uc Prints the jail's mounts. --missing prints the paths not there yet. --make makes the directories the service makes, and grants its user what the collectors declare. --clean takes away what it granted, when the service stops. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/auth.uc Writes or removes basic auth's file. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/watch.uc The watch instance. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/import.uc The import the uci-defaults script runs. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc The scrape of the ubus object's status. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/trial.uc What runs in the service's jail for check, status and the command line's scrape. /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/probe.uc Loads collector modules in a process of its own, for rpcd: rpcd loads no module it has not seen load there first. /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter.uc rpcd's plugin: the ubus object. /usr/share/acl.d/prometheus-exporter.json A link to /var/run/prometheus-exporter.acl.json, the service's ubus ACL, which ubusd reads. See The jail. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter.uc The collector API, prometheus.exporter: the only module a collector imports. See Collector interface. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/*.uc The exporter's modules, prometheus.exporter.<module>, except the command line's (cli.uc, conform.uc). version.uc holds the package's version. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/config/*.uc The modules split out of config.uc: the options' types and datatypes. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/exposition/*.uc The modules split out of exposition.uc. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/deps/*.uc The capabilities of deps.uc, a module each. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/rpc/*.uc The modules split out of rpc.uc: what collectors describes, and validate. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/collectors/<module>.uc The base collectors, prometheus.collectors.<module>.

docs.title: At run time
docs.text:
Path Content /var/run/prometheus-exporter/ Mode 0700, root's. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf Basic auth's file, mode 0640, root's and the service's group's, while basic auth is on. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/tls.crt, tls.key Copies of cert and key, mode 0640, root's and the service's group's, while the service runs over HTTPS. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/capabilities.json The capabilities of the jail, while the service runs. /var/run/prometheus-exporter.acl.json The service's ubus ACL, while the service runs. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state/ The handler's state, each scrape's progress file, and the file that carries its collectors' runs back to it. See The jail. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ntpd busybox ntpd's last event.

All are on tmpfs: none survives a reboot.

busybox ntpd runs /usr/sbin/ntpd-hotplug on a step, a new stratum, a loss of sync, and periodically. procd hands each hotplug.d/ntp script ntpd's environment: ACTION, stratum, offset, freq_drift_ppm and poll_interval. chrony's own hotplug call has no stratum, so the script keeps nothing of it. The script writes the file whole and renames it into place, so timesync never reads half a file.

docs.title: ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli
docs.text:
The command line, prometheus-exporter. It prints a scrape on standard output, runs the check, lists the installed collectors, checks a collector module before it is installed, and hashes a password. The service, its check, its ubus object and LuCI need none of it.

It depends on the base package of the very same version, and on ucode-docopt, which parses the command's arguments. ucode-docopt comes from the same feed as the exporter, and nothing else depends on it. The package takes 16 KiB installed, and ucode-docopt 43 KiB.

Path Content /usr/bin/prometheus-exporter The command. See The prometheus-exporter command. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/cli.uc Its commands, and the usage docopt parses its arguments by. /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/conform.uc collector check: a collector module checked against the collector contract.

docs.title: Collector packages
docs.text:
ucode-prometheus-exporter-<name>, one per collector not in the base package. Each installs /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/collectors/<module>.uc, and depends on the base package and on what its collector needs: see Collectors.

Installing or removing one reloads the service if it is enabled or running, which grants or takes back what the collector declares. If the service is neither, removing one takes back all the service granted (jail.uc --clean). Removing the base package does that too, before its files go.

ucode-prometheus-exporter-filesystem also installs an rpcd plugin, /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter-filesystem.uc. It serves the ubus object prometheus-exporter.filesystem. Its mounts method answers each of the host's mounts with its type, read-only flag, sizes and inodes: { result: [ { device, mount, fstype, ro, size, free, avail, files, ffree } ] }. It reads the host's /proc/mounts and calls statvfs() on its mounts, which the collector cannot do from the jail. Installing or removing the package also reloads rpcd. See ubus object.

docs.title: Group packages
docs.text: ucode-prometheus-exporter-network, -wireless, -hardware and -full install no files: each depends on its collectors' packages. Removing a group from a device's world lets apk remove its collectors too. Collectors lists the collectors in each group.

docs.title: ucode-prometheus-exporter-devkit
docs.text: Tests collectors under utest. It installs its modules to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/devkit/, and the mocks' proxies to devkit/proxies/. It depends on the base package of the same release, ucode-utest, ucode-mod-nl80211 and ucode-mod-socket. It is for a development machine or a CI image, not a router: see The devkit.

docs.title: luci-app-prometheus-exporter
docs.text: LuCI's pages for the exporter. It depends on luci-base and the base package. LuCI app lists its files. Installing or removing it clears LuCI's caches and reloads rpcd.

docs.title: Source tree
docs.text: Path Content src/prometheus/exporter.uc The collector API, installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter.uc. src/prometheus/exporter/ The modules, installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/exporter/. src/prometheus/collectors/ The collectors, installed to /usr/share/ucode/prometheus/collectors/. src/prometheus/exporter/devkit/ The devkit, installed by its own package: what the tests of every collector run on. devkit/template/ The template of a collector in a package of its own: its Makefile, module, test and fixtures. files/ What the base package installs besides the modules. luci/ The LuCI app. openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile The package Makefile. test/unit/ Unit tests; test/unit/prometheus/ mirrors src/prometheus/. test/integration/ Integration tests. test/fixtures/ What devices answered, for the tests. test/bench/ The benchmark. test/browser/ The LuCI app's Playwright tests. test/docs/ The documentation tooling's tests. devenv/ The development environment: Docker images and scripts. docs/ This documentation.

docs.title: HTTP Endpoint
docs.text: uhttpd serves the exporter's handler, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc, under the prefix /metrics. It listens on port listen_port (9100), on the addresses of listen_interface (loopback), or on every address for *. It serves HTTPS when cert and key are both set and both files are there, and HTTP otherwise. See UCI configuration.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text: Request Answer /metrics, any method A scrape. A path under /metrics, such as /metrics/x The same scrape: uhttpd hands the handler every path with that prefix. Any other path 404, from uhttpd: its document root is /dev/null.

docs.title: Query string
docs.text:
Parameter Meaning collect[]=<name> Scrape this collector. Repeat it for several; they are scraped in the order given, once each. collect=<name> The same, as the feed's ucode exporter spelled it. exclude[]=<name> Leave this collector out.

A name is a collector's name (ltq-dsl) or its module (ltq_dsl), URL-encoded or not. Without collect[], a scrape selects every enabled collector except those excluded, sorted by name, and the reply follows that order. Other parameters are ignored.

docs.title: Request headers
docs.text: Header Meaning X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds The seconds the scraper waits, as Prometheus and vmagent send it: a positive number, such as 10 or 9.5. Without it, or with a value that is not a positive number, the main section's scrape_timeout (10) applies. Never more than 60, uhttpd's -t. Accept-Encoding Whether the scraper takes gzip: Compression. Authorization Basic auth: Basic auth.

docs.title: Deadline
docs.text:
A scrape's collectors get the timeout less 0.5 seconds, or half the timeout if that is less. The time counts from when the request reaches the handler.

The collectors run fastest first, by how long each took before; a collector never timed runs after the others. The scrape starts a collector only if the time it took before, and the time to write the reply, still fit before the deadline:

  • A collector left out fails with SCRAPE_DEADLINE, and so does one whose program was killed at the deadline. A program gets the whole seconds left, and is not started with less than one.
  • A collector that its circuit breaker quarantined does not run, even when collect[] names it. It fails with COLLECTOR_QUARANTINED, and its ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_quarantined is 1.
  • The scrape logs those the deadline left out in one line: see Log messages.

See About deadlines and circuit breakers.

Query Status Body Names only installed, enabled collectors 200 OK The scrape. Names a collector that is not installed, in collect[] or exclude[] 400 Bad Request COLLECTOR_INVALID (unknown collector '<name>') Names a disabled collector in collect[] 400 Bad Request COLLECTOR_INVALID (collector '<name>' is disabled)

docs.title: The scrape
docs.text:
Content-Type: text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8: the Prometheus text exposition format, version 0.0.4.

  • Each collector's families. A family belongs to the first collector in the reply that writes it, with the exporter's own collectors before those of other packages. Another collector that writes it fails with FAMILY_CONFLICT, and none of its samples are served (see Collector contract). Within a collector, a family declared with two types keeps the first type, drops the later samples, and logs a warning.
  • Then, for every collector selected: node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds (0 for one not run), node_scrape_collector_success, node_scrape_collector_observing and ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_quarantined, labeled collector. Then ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version}. See Metrics.
  • A collector that fails keeps the samples it wrote before it failed. One with nothing to observe writes none.
  • With option omit_zero_values '1', samples of counters whose value is 0 are left out.

A collector's failure does not fail the scrape: the answer is still 200 OK.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
While option compress is 1 (the default):

  • Every reply has Vary: Accept-Encoding.
  • A 200 reply is gzip-compressed, with Content-Encoding: gzip, when the request's Accept-Encoding accepts gzip. It does with gzip or x-gzip with a q other than 0, or, when it names neither, with * with a q other than 0. gzip;q=0 refuses it.
  • zlib's level is 1, the fastest.

With option compress '0', no reply is compressed and none has Vary.

docs.title: Basic auth
docs.text:
