With auth_user and auth_password set, the handler checks every request before it scrapes. It checks against uhttpd's config file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf:

Request Status Headers Body Over HTTP 403 Forbidden Basic auth takes HTTPS only. Without an Authorization: Basic header, or with a user or password that does not match 401 Unauthorized WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="prometheus-exporter" Unauthorized. With the user and password As without basic auth Any, when the file is there but is not one line of a user and a hash for /metrics, or is not there while auth_user is set 500 Internal Server Error Basic auth is not configured as it should be; see the log.

These replies are Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8. The init script never serves basic auth over HTTP. The 403 is for a request that reaches the handler without TLS anyway.

The handler reads the file, compress and scrape_timeout once, when uhttpd starts it. A change to any of them restarts uhttpd: see Service commands.

The handler checks the password against the hash: $1$ (MD5-crypt), $5$ (SHA-256-crypt) or $6$ (SHA-512-crypt), of at most 2000 rounds. After it lets a request in, it keeps a digest of the request's Authorization header in its state. It lets in a later request with the same header on the digest alone. See The jail.

docs.title: Keep-alive
docs.text:
uhttpd keeps an idle connection open http_keepalive seconds (70), with -k: Keep-Alive: timeout=70. At 0 it answers Connection: close and closes each connection once it has answered.

70 seconds outlasts Prometheus's default scrape_interval of 60. So Prometheus's connection stays open from one scrape to the next, and each scrape reuses it. That saves a new TCP connection and, over HTTPS, a new TLS handshake, which costs a router's CPU more than a scrape's request does. A scraper that scrapes less often than every 70 seconds connects again each time. To spare it that, set http_keepalive above its interval.

The init script always passes -k. Without it, uhttpd would use its own 20 seconds.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
The init script has uhttpd run at most 3 requests at once (-n 3), over at most 10 connections (-N 10), rather than leave it to uhttpd's defaults, 3 and 100.

  • One or two Prometheus servers scrape the service, each over a connection of its own that keep-alive keeps open. LuCI reaches the exporter through rpcd, not over this port.
  • Each request is a full scrape, or, with basic auth, a check of the hash first. 3 at once allow two scrapers' scrapes that overlap, and one more, such as a curl's.
  • A request past them waits until one ends, and the connections limit how many can wait.

uhttpd gives each request 60 seconds (-t 60), which scrape_timeout takes into account.

Only the scrapers should reach the port: whoever reaches it can make the router scrape, and hash, again and again. See How to listen on the LAN.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• How to serve HTTPS with basic auth
  • How to compress scrapes
  • About the security model

docs.title: The Jail
docs.text:
uhttpd, and the exporter with it, runs in procd's jail (ujail), named prometheus-exporter. It runs with no_new_privs, as the user and group prometheus-exporter, never as root.

The jail holds only what the exporter needs and what its installed and enabled collectors declare. The user may do only what they declare: see The service's user.

  • src/prometheus/exporter/jail.uc works out the mounts.
  • src/prometheus/exporter/privileges.uc works out what the user is granted.
  • /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/jail.uc prints the mounts for the init script, and grants the rest.

docs.title: What every jail has
docs.text:
From What The jail's options procfs, sysfs, /dev/log. The exporter (jail.uc, before the collectors' mounts) /usr/lib/uhttpd_ucode.so, /lib/libubus.so*, /lib/libuci.so*, /usr/lib/libnl*.so*, /usr/lib/libz.so*, /usr/lib/ucode, /usr/share/ucode/prometheus, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc; /bin/sh, whose kill a scrape uses to end a collector's process that a dead scrape left running. The configuration /etc/config/prometheus-exporter. HTTPS, when cert and key are set and copied Their copies, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/tls.crt and tls.key; /lib/libustream-*.so*, /usr/lib/libustream-*.so*. Basic auth Its file, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf. The state /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state, read-write.

Every mount is read-only, except the state. The ubus socket is not among them: see What a collector gets.

flowchart LR
    procd -- "ujail: user prometheus-exporter,<br/>no_new_privs, its capabilities file" --> U
    subgraph J["jail prometheus-exporter"]
        U["uhttpd and handler.uc"]
    end
    U -- "read-only" --> RO["procfs, sysfs, /dev/log<br/>the exporter's code and libraries<br/>/etc/config/prometheus-exporter<br/>what the enabled collectors declare"]
    U -- "read-write" --> ST["/var/run/prometheus-exporter/state"]
    U -- "only while an enabled collector needs ubus" --> UB["the ubus socket:<br/>ubusd holds it to the ubus ACL"]
    U -- "the host's network" --> NET["deps.socket.tcp_request:<br/>the device's own addresses only"]

procd starts the instance at nice 10, with a data limit (RLIMIT_DATA) on each of its processes. The limit is memory_limit MB, or else a quarter of the RAM, at most 64 MB: see Collector contract.

check, the ubus object's status and prometheus-exporter scrape run their collectors in a jail of their own, named prometheus-exporter-trial:

  • It runs /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/trial.uc with ujail.
  • It has the same mounts, priority and data limit as the service's jail.
  • It has ubus (ujail's -u) only when the service's jail has it.
  • It gets the libraries of /usr/lib/ucode/*.so one by one, and ujail mounts what each needs.

Where ujail cannot run, they run their collectors outside a jail.

The jail mounts the libraries of ucode's modules by glob (/usr/lib/ucode/*.so, libubus, …). ujail stages the libraries that a library it is given needs, but not those of a directory's files.

docs.title: What a collector gets
docs.text:
For each installed collector that is enabled:

Declared in meta Mounted configs: [ 'dhcp' ] /etc/config/dhcp. ubus in needs The ubus socket, /var/run/ubus/ubus.sock, through the jail's ubus option: jail.uc names it, and the init script sets the option. While no enabled collector needs ubus, the jail has no ubus. exec in needs /bin/sh, which runs its programs. commands: [ 'nft' ] Each program, where PATH (/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin) finds it. ujail mounts its shared libraries with it. optional_commands The same, where the program is installed. Where it is not: nothing, and no warning. paths Each path: see below.

A disabled collector gets nothing. Of /etc/config, the jail holds only the exporter's own config and the configs the enabled collectors name. Collectors and check show the mounts each collector gets.

The jail shapes some declarations:

  • modemmanager gets the directory /var/run/dbus, not the system bus socket in it. dbus makes the socket anew each time it starts, so a bind mount of the old one would go stale.
  • chrony and timesync run chronyc -u root. OpenWrt builds chrony to drop root for the chrony user, and the jail, which has no /etc/passwd, cannot look that user up.
  • timesync gets the directory of busybox ntpd's last event, not the file: the hotplug script renames the file into it.

docs.title: The service's user
docs.text:
The package makes the user and group prometheus-exporter on install and on upgrade. Its USERID takes the first free id from 32768.

procd has ujail run uhttpd:

  • as that user and group (-U, -G);
  • with no new privileges (-c);
  • with the capabilities file /var/run/prometheus-exporter/capabilities.json (-C).

Since it is not root, the process reads only what the files' modes let it, ubusd holds it to an ACL, and it has only the capabilities it is given. The init script refuses to start without the user, and logs why at err.

When the service starts or reloads, jail.uc --make runs as root. It grants the user what the installed and enabled collectors declare. It takes back anything it granted that no collector declares now: what a disabled collector declares, and what a collector no longer installed did.

jail.uc --make records, in /var/run/prometheus-exporter/granted.json (root's alone, 0600), the group and mode each file had before it granted it, and restores them when it takes the grant back. Where it has no record, as after a reboot (tmpfs forgets), it takes back:

  • every config of /etc/config that has the service's group, giving it to root's group;
  • every group the user is a member of.

jail.uc --clean takes back all of it, and removes the ACL, the capabilities file, the TLS copies, basic auth's file and the record. It runs when:

  • the service stops;
  • the service is disabled (enabled 0);
  • its package is removed. Its prerm disables and stops the service, which would otherwise outlive its files.

Removing a collector package reloads the service, which takes back what that collector was granted. If the service is neither enabled nor running, it runs jail.uc --clean.

Declared in meta Granted ubus: { dnsmasq: [ 'metrics' ] } The call, in the service's ubus ACL. Taken back: the ACL is written anew. capabilities: [ 'CAP_NET_ADMIN' ] The capability, in every set of the capabilities file (bounding, effective, permitted, inheritable, ambient), so the programs the jail runs have it too. groups: [ 'unbound' ] The user's membership of the group, in /etc/group, under OpenWrt's lock (/var/lock/passwd), when the group is there. Taken back: the membership is removed, from any group but the user's own. proc_files: [ '/proc/net/nf_conntrack' ] Read access for the group: the file's group is prometheus-exporter, and its group bits r--. Taken back: its group and mode are what they were before. configs: [ 'dhcp' ], and the exporter's own config The same, for /etc/config/<config>.

What the enabled collectors declare now:

Collector Granted nft-counters CAP_NET_ADMIN: nftables answers a netlink dump only to a process that has it. nat_traffic Reading /proc/net/nf_conntrack, r--r----- root's. unbound The group unbound: unbound's control socket is srw-rw---- unbound:unbound. Those that read a config (chrony, dhcp_leases, uci_dhcp_host, ...) Reading it: OpenWrt's configs are mostly root's alone (0600). Those that call ubus Their calls: see Collectors (Calls over ubus).

The service itself gets CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE while listen_port is under 1024.

A collector may declare only CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW. Not CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH or CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE: the first would read past the jail's mounts (a file opened by handle), and the second would write /proc (the jail's procfs is writable).

uci commit replaces a config with a file of root's group, keeping the mode. The reload that the commit triggers grants the file again before procd restarts uhttpd; until then, uhttpd reads the file it mounted. /proc files belong to the kernel: a module loaded again gives them back to root.

check, the ubus object's status and prometheus-exporter scrape run their collectors in a jail as the same user, with no new privileges and the capabilities file the service wrote. So they get what the service granted when it started. While the service is stopped, they have no capability and no ACL.

These stay root's, unjailed:

  • the init script and jail.uc;
  • rpcd's ubus object;
  • the watch instance (see Missing paths), which sends procd the event that reloads the service. Sending an event needs procd's service event, which would let whoever calls it send any event.

docs.title: The ubus ACL
docs.text:
ubusd reads its ACLs from /usr/share/acl.d. The package installs prometheus-exporter.json there: a link to /var/run/prometheus-exporter.acl.json.

When the service starts, jail.uc --make writes that file for the user prometheus-exporter. It lists the calls the enabled collectors declare (their meta.ubus, for their options). If the file changed, jail.uc --make has ubusd read it again (SIGHUP).

The file is root's, mode 0644, and lies outside the service's run directory, which only root can enter: ubusd runs as its own user. When the service is stopped or disabled, it removes the file, and the link points nowhere.

The file is written for the enabled collectors, not installed with the packages for all of them. So a call is allowed only while a collector that declares it is enabled, with the options that call for it: wireguard's peer_names for the ubus object's wireguard_peers.

ubusd's ACL names objects and methods, never arguments. So no collector declares a call that reads whatever its caller names, or that answers a secret, as these do: rpcd's file read and uci get, netifd's network.wireless status and procd's service list. Instead, the service's own ubus object reads or asks for what they would answer, as root, and returns only the fields the collectors read (see ubus object). About the security model lists every call the ACL can allow.

ubusd refuses a call the ACL does not allow:

  • Permission denied for a method of an object the user may call other methods of;
  • Not found for an object the user may call nothing of. ubusd does not list that object either.

So the ACL always allows system board, the canary. A collector whose object is not found asks for system board. If that is not found either, ubusd has not loaded the ACL, and the call is PERMISSION_DENIED, never nothing to observe.

docs.title: What fails, and how
docs.text:
The exporter never takes a missing permission for nothing to observe. A collector fails with PERMISSION_DENIED, naming what it lacks and what grants it, when:

  • its process lacks a capability it declares;
  • it may not read a config or /proc file it declares;
  • it may not connect to a Unix socket (EACCES);
  • ubusd refuses a call.

A call its meta.ubus does not list is refused before ubusd sees it, with UBUS_NOT_ALLOWED. See Error codes. If something took a grant away under the running service, a reload grants it again.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
meta.paths lists what a collector reads outside procfs and sysfs:

Entry Mounted '/var/run/bmx7/json' That path. '{directory}' The value of the string option directory. { path: '{directory}', owned: true } That path, which is the exporter's own: the service makes it, with its parents (root's, mode 0755), when it is not there. It must be under /var, /tmp or /etc/prometheus-exporter, and not under /var/run or /tmp/run: see below. (options, uci) => [ ... ] What the function returns for the collector's options and the configs it reads.

The exporter refuses a path, with a warning, when it:

  • is not absolute;
  • holds a space, a control character or a glob character;
  • is not plain (//, ., .., or a trailing /);
  • is one of the directories every service shares:

/, /bin, /dev, /etc, /etc/config, /lib, /proc, /run, /sbin, /sys, /tmp, /tmp/run, /usr, /usr/bin, /usr/lib, /usr/sbin, /usr/share, /var, /var/run.

ujail cannot mount a socket, so a collector declares the socket's directory. A TCP port is not a path: the jail has the host's network, and deps.socket.tcp_request connects only to an address of the device itself (see About the security model).

docs.title: Owned paths
docs.text:
The service makes an owned path as root, and mounts it. So it accepts one only below these directories, and refuses any other with a warning, neither making nor mounting it:

Under Why /var, /tmp tmpfs on OpenWrt (/var is /tmp): what a script writes there often does not wear the flash. /etc/prometheus-exporter The exporter's own, on flash: for files that must outlive a reboot.

An owned path may not be under /var/run or /tmp/run, every service's run directory. The one exception is a directory of the exporter's own, /var/run/prometheus-exporter/<name>, that a collector's meta names (timesync's), and that is not its state.

An option that names an owned path, such as textfile's directory, has the datatype owned_directory. It accepts the same paths, but none under /var/run. The exporter refuses such a configuration with OWNED_DIRECTORY (see UCI configuration) before the service makes anything.

Before it makes or mounts an owned path, jail.uc walks it from /, never following a link it has not checked:

  • each directory must be root's, and writable by no one else unless it is sticky (/tmp);
  • each link must be root's (/var, a link to /tmp).

It makes each missing directory, root's and 0755, and checks it again once made. A path that fails, such as a /tmp/prometheus another user made, or a link there, is neither made nor mounted. jail.uc --make logs <path>: <why>: neither made nor mounted at err, and check warns of it. See About the security model.

docs.title: Missing paths
docs.text:
When a path is not there as the service starts, the service leaves it out of the mounts, and check warns of it. While one is missing, the service runs a second instance, watch, with the missing paths:

  1. Every 5 seconds it looks for them.
  2. Once one is there, it logs <path> is there now: reloading to mount it at info and sends procd the event prometheus-exporter.path.
  3. The event reloads the service, which mounts the path and restarts uhttpd with it. The reload ends the watch instance, or starts it again for the paths still missing.
  4. If procd does not take the event, it logs cannot send procd prometheus-exporter.path; trying again in 60s at warning.

A path the service owns is never missing: the service makes it first.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
/var/run/prometheus-exporter/state is the only path the jail mounts read-write. It is on tmpfs, mode 0700, owned by the service's user. It sits inside /var/run/prometheus-exporter, which is 0700 and root's. jail.uc --make makes both when the service starts.

Owner A uhttpd instance. The handler names it when uhttpd loads the handler, before any request, by the pid and start time of that process. Files <pid>-<start time>.<name>, mode 0600, at most 32768 bytes each, written whole: to <file>.new, then renamed. Lock <pid>-<start time>.lock: every write holds an exclusive flock() of it; a read takes none. Read by root check and the ubus object's status, and nothing else of the object, read the ledger as root. They read only a regular file of the state's owner, with one link and at most 32768 bytes, never a link, a FIFO or a device in its place, and without blocking. See About the implementation. Other instances' files Removed when the handler loads. Lifetime Until the instance stops: a restart starts without state, and a reload that keeps the instance keeps it. Used for Basic auth's cache, <instance>.auth: one digest of the last Authorization header let in.The ledger, <instance>.scrape: below.Each scrape's progress file, <instance>.p<pid>_<start time>, named by its process. The scrape appends a line start <collector> <child pid>-<start time> before each collector, and collected once they are done, and removes the file when the reply is written. A file a dead process left names the collector it was running, for the next scrape.The file that carries the collectors' runs from their process to the scrape's, made with mkstemp and removed at once.

docs.title: The ledger
docs.text:
<instance>.scrape is JSON. Every scrape of the handler reads it when it starts. When it ends, the scrape re-reads it under the lock and records itself in it.

check and the ubus object's status read the ledger of the instance that started last. check --config, which start and reload run, and the object's other methods do not read it.

Field Content v 1, the ledger's version. A ledger of another version is read as empty. scrapes The scrapes the instance answered. k Seconds per sample of writing a reply, a moving average. c.<module>.d The collector's seconds, a moving average weighing the last run by 0.25. c.<module>.n The samples it wrote last. c.<module>.late The scrape that last left it out at the deadline. c.<module>.f Its failures in a row, while its breaker is closed. c.<module>.q The last scrape of its quarantine; absent while its breaker is closed. c.<module>.cd The cool-down of that quarantine, in scrapes: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. c.<module>.why What tripped its breaker, as CODE (detail). auth_failures The requests basic auth refused (401). c.<module>.fails Its failures by error code, { CODE: n }, at most 8 codes; any other is counted as OTHER. c.<module>.to Its programs killed at their timeout. c.<module>.qn The times its breaker tripped. c.<module>.dl The times the deadline left it out, or killed its program.

A collector no longer installed is dropped from the ledger.

An instance is named by its start time as well as its pid, because in the jail's own pid namespace uhttpd has the same pid at every start. The start time is the 22nd field of /proc/<pid>/stat, counted after the ) that ends the command name, which may hold spaces.

The ledger, the largest state file, sets the 32 KiB limit. It takes some 30 bytes for a collector that never failed, and 300 for one that failed every way it can. When the ledger is longer than a state file may be, the scrape writes it again without each breaker's why and each collector's failures by code. A state that cannot be written would lose the whole scrape's durations, breakers and counts.

docs.title: Files the service writes
docs.text:
Path Mode Written by Mounted /var/run/prometheus-exporter/ 0700, root's jail.uc --make, auth.uc No /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf 0640, root's and the service's group's auth.uc, at each start: one line, /metrics:<user>:<hash>. Removed without basic auth, and when the service stops. Read-only, with basic auth /var/run/prometheus-exporter/tls.crt, tls.key 0640, root's and the service's group's jail.uc --make, at each start: copies of cert and key. It copies each only if it is a regular file of at most 64 KiB under /etc/ssl, /etc/acme or /etc/prometheus-exporter, or /etc/uhttpd.*, wherever its links lead, and reads at most that much. If either one fails, it copies neither. Removed when the service stops. Read-only, with both there: the init script serves HTTPS only from them /var/run/prometheus-exporter/granted.json 0600, root's jail.uc --make: each file it gave the service's group, with the group and mode it had. Removed with the last of them, and when the service stops. No /var/run/prometheus-exporter/capabilities.json 0644 jail.uc --make, at each start. Removed when the service stops. No: procd hands it to ujail /var/run/prometheus-exporter.acl.json 0644 jail.uc --make, at each start. Removed when the service stops. No: ubusd reads it /var/run/prometheus-exporter/state/ 0700, the service's user's jail.uc --make Read-write /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ 0755 jail.uc --make (timesync's owned path), or the hotplug script Read-only /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync/ntpd 0644 /etc/hotplug.d/ntp/90-prometheus-exporter, on each event of busybox ntpd, outside the jail With its directory /var/prometheus/ (textfile's directory) 0755 jail.uc --make Read-only

The jail reads these files as the service's user. textfile's *.prom files must be readable by that user, as a file a script writes is (0644), or by its group. textfile skips a file only root can read, and logs it.

auth.uc writes uhttpd's auth file to a temporary name and renames it into place. A running instance's jail bind-mounted the old file, so it reads the old one until it restarts.

docs.title: Restarts
docs.text:
procd binds files into the jail. When a new file replaces one, as uci commit replaces a config, the jail still sees the old one. So procd watches these files for the uhttpd instance, and restarts the instance on reload when one changed:

  • the configs the jail mounts from /etc/config;
  • every collector module;
  • basic auth's file;
  • the copies of the TLS files, which a reload makes again from the files cert and key name;
  • the capabilities file.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Collector interface: what a collector declares.
  • About the security model

docs.title: Log Messages
docs.text:
The exporter logs to syslog as prometheus-exporter, facility daemon, each line at its own priority. Read it with logread -e prometheus-exporter.

Priority For err What stops it doing its job: an invalid configuration, a collector that does not load. warning What it does without: a collector that fails, which the scrape answers without; collectors the deadline left out; a quarantine; a path the jail cannot mount. notice A quarantined collector served again. info What it says of itself: how many collectors it serves, a directory it made, the settings it took over.

A collector with nothing to observe logs nothing. Neither does a quarantined collector while it is left out. The exporter never logs basic auth's password, nor its hash.

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
uhttpd's handler logs these, with the pid of the uhttpd process.

Message Priority When serving <n> collectors[, with basic auth][, gzip when asked] info uhttpd loaded the handler. cannot load collector '<module>': <error> err A collector module does not compile or import, or loading it ended the process it was loaded in. It is left out. collector '<module>' hung at load: still loading after 5 s: stopped; it is left out err A collector module's top level did not return within 5 s, in the child process where it is first loaded. skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (<module>: its top level called <function>(), which <does>: ...) err As it loaded, a collector module's top level called a function that blocks, ends or writes to the process, loads code, or changes its signals. The call was refused before it ran, in the child process where the module is first loaded, or in uhttpd's. The module is left out. See Collector interface. skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (<module>: its top level changed the global scope, <name>, ...: ...) err A collector module's top level wrote over, added or removed these names of the global scope. The change would have stayed in uhttpd for every scrape. The names are put back as they were, and the module is left out. skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (<module>: its top level wrote over what the collector API exports, which no collector may change: object value is immutable) err A collector module's top level wrote over Result, errors, services, proc or exposition, or a Result's prototype. Every collector shares these, and ucode keeps them constant. The module is left out. skipping collector: COLLECTOR_INVALID (<module>: <why>) err A module's meta or collect is not valid; or it is not in strict mode (not in strict mode: its first statement must be 'use strict'); or it imports a module other than the collector API, or loads code past its imports (imports fs (line 3): a collector reads files through deps.fs, with 'fs' in meta.needs; see Collector contract). It is left out. checking again what changed since it was checked, as in an upgrade: <module> ... info A collector module's file changed between its check in the probe's child and its load in uhttpd. This happens when an upgrade of several packages writes the next package while the service starts. The module is checked and loaded again, alone. skipping collector: <module>: not what it was when it was checked, in a process of its own, 3 times: is it being upgraded? err The module changed at each of three checks. It is left out until the next reload. native module '<name>' did not load in a process of its own: <error>; each scrape loads it where it needs it warning uhttpd loads ubus, rtnl, nl80211 and zlib when it starts. This one failed or crashed as it loaded in the probe's child, so uhttpd does not load it. A scrape's child loads it where a collector needs it, and a crash there costs only that collector (COLLECTOR_KILLED). Without zlib, replies are sent plain. asked to stop (signal <n>) while it loaded the collectors: stopping notice procd stopped the instance while it loaded its collectors, as a reload between the packages of an upgrade does. The instance ends at once, as the signal would have ended it, and procd starts the next. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf is not one line of a user and a hash for /metrics: every request is denied err Basic auth's file is there, and wrong. /var/run/prometheus-exporter/uhttpd.conf is not there, and the config sets basic auth (auth_user): every request is denied err uhttpd started without basic auth's file, though auth_user is set: procd started it again after the file was removed. service prometheus-exporter restart writes the file. collector '<name>': <CODE (detail)> warning A collector failed in a scrape, with the code it returned, or with the code the exporter stopped it with (COLLECTOR_CANCELLED, COLLECTOR_KILLED, SAMPLE_LIMIT, EXPOSITION_INVALID, FAMILY_CONFLICT). Not for SCRAPE_DEADLINE, which the scrape's own line reports. See Error codes and Collector contract. collector '<name>' was running when a scrape process died warning A scrape found the progress file of a scrape process that died while this collector ran. The collector is quarantined, and the child process it ran in is killed. cannot fork a process to run the collectors in; running the collectors in the scrape's own process warning The system could not fork (out of processes or memory). The scrape ran its collectors in its own process, where nothing can stop them midway. cannot make the file the collectors' runs cross by, in <directory>; running the collectors in the scrape's own process warning The state's directory (/tmp outside the service) is full or not writable, so it could not take a temporary file. The scrape ran its collectors in its own process, where nothing can stop them midway. scrape deadline: <n> collector[s] not served in its <seconds> s: <name>, ... warning The scrape's deadline left these collectors out, or killed their programs. One line per scrape. See HTTP endpoint. collector '<name>' quarantined for <n> scrape[s]: <CODE (detail)> warning Its circuit breaker tripped, on a program killed at its timeout, on COLLECTOR_OVERRUN (over its budget), or on a third failure in a row. Or its trial failed. collector '<name>' served again: its trial succeeded notice Its circuit breaker closed. collector '<name>': <message> warning A collector that succeeded said something with its log capability. For example textfile's skipped <file>: <why>, as skipped /var/prometheus/x.prom: is not a regular file (fifo): not read. collector '<name>': <n> more line[s] of its log left out warning A collector's run logged more than 10 lines with its log capability. The first 10 were logged, each cut at 512 bytes, and this line once the run was over. collector '<name>': '<family>' declared with two types; later samples dropped warning A collector declared a family twice. the process running the collectors ran past the scrape's deadline, past the limits it gave: stopped there, the rest left out warning Something a collector did went wrong in the child process that runs the collectors. That process gave a collector a limit past the scrape's deadline, or none, or went on past the deadline with no collector started. The scrape stopped it at the deadline itself, served the runs it had finished, and left the rest out with SCRAPE_DEADLINE. the processes forked to run the collectors in ended twice before running one; not run: <name>, ... warning Two child processes in a row ended before they ran a collector. The collectors left fail with COLLECTOR_NOT_RUN, and their breakers stay as they were. asked to stop (signal <n>) while it ran the collectors: stopping notice The scrape's process was asked to stop (SIGTERM or SIGINT) while its collectors ran. It stopped their child process and ended at once, as the signal would have ended it, without a reply and without blaming a collector. the scrape could not be recorded in the instance's state: its ledger is as the last scrape left it warning The state's directory could not be written. The next scrape orders, times and quarantines the collectors by the ledger as it was. main: <CODE (detail)> err A scrape read a main section it does not accept, and used the defaults.

The handler logs through ucode-mod-log, at each message's own priority. It does not log to standard error, which procd would log at err whatever the message.

docs.title: The init script
docs.text: Message Priority When FAIL main: ..., FAIL collector ..., the lines of check --config err start or reload found the configuration invalid. Also on standard error. invalid configuration, not starting err start refused it. Also on standard error. invalid configuration, keeping the running instance err reload refused it. Also on standard error. deferring start until listen interface <interface> becomes ready info The listen interface has no address yet. <CODE (detail)>, then cannot set up basic auth, not starting err Basic auth's file could not be written or removed. basic auth takes HTTPS only, and <cert> or <key> is missing: not starting err Basic auth is on, and a TLS file is not there. made <path> info It made a directory a collector owns, such as /var/prometheus. cannot make <path>: <error> err It could not make one, or the state directory. <collector>: <problem> warning A path or a program the jail cannot give a collector: command <name> is not on /usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin, <path> is too broad to mount for one collector, its paths are not known: ..., a paths function failed: ....

docs.title: The watch instance
docs.text: Message Priority When <path>[, <path>] is there now: reloading to mount it info A missing path appeared. cannot send procd prometheus-exporter.path; trying again in 60s warning procd did not take the event.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
A uci-defaults script takes over a feed exporter's settings, and moves basic auth's hash out of the place 0.2.0 kept it. It logs at info, once, when the package is installed or upgraded:

Message When imported from /etc/config/<old>: <option>=<value>, ..., collector <module> It took over these settings. It says nothing it changed from the defaults when there was nothing to take over. <old>: option <option>: expected <what>, got <value>; left at the default A value this exporter does not accept. <old>: collector <module>, option <option>: expected <what>, got <value>; left at its default A value of a collector section that the collector does not accept. <old>: collector <module> has no option <option>; left out An option of a collector section that the installed collector does not have. <old>: collector <module> is not installed, and <option> is not an option it is known to have; left out An option of a collector section whose collector is not installed yet. The option is neither one the feed's ucode exporter had for that collector (wifi's stations) nor one of the core's (enabled, budget, max_samples). /etc/config/prometheus-exporter is not as the package ships it: nothing imported from /etc/config/<old> The config had been changed already. auth_password moved from /etc/config/prometheus-exporter to /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth An upgrade from 0.2.0 found the hash of basic auth's password where 0.2.0 kept it, and moved it to where the exporter reads it now. auth_password removed from /etc/config/prometheus-exporter: /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth has one already, which is kept The same, when a hash was already saved apart. /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth is not there: auth_password left in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, where it is not read; set it again The hash's config was removed: save the password again (set_password).

See How to move from the feed's exporters.

docs.title: LuCI App
docs.text: luci-app-prometheus-exporter adds two pages to LuCI. It depends on luci-base, and on the exporter's base package of the same release. It calls the ubus object that the base package serves.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Menu Path View Services → Prometheus exporter admin/services/prometheus-exporter prometheus-exporter/settings Status → Prometheus exporter admin/status/prometheus-exporter prometheus-exporter/status

Both need the ACL luci-app-prometheus-exporter and the config prometheus-exporter.

Every string from the router (collector names and help, packages, interfaces, paths, errors) reaches the page as a text node. The page puts it either in an array of children of E(), or into a translated template piece by piece. It never uses .format(), whose %s puts text where markup may go. It never uses such a string as a form's title or description, which LuCI renders as markup. make lint's luci-dom-lint.sh refuses the usual ways around this.

docs.title: Services → Prometheus exporter
docs.text: This page edits the main section and the collector sections of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, in four tabs. General, HTTPS & login and Limits hold the main section, and Collectors holds the collectors. LuCI reopens the page on the tab last shown, or on General the first time.

docs.title: General tab
docs.text: Field Option Notes Enable enabled Listen on listen_interface The interfaces of the ubus object's interfaces, and Every address (*). A saved interface that netifd does not list is kept. Port listen_port Keep-alive http_keepalive Compress compress Leave out zero values omit_zero_values

docs.title: HTTPS & login tab
docs.text:
The tab's description says that basic auth needs HTTPS, so the certificate and key come first.

Field Option Notes TLS certificate cert No placeholder. The description says where the files may be: /etc/ssl, /etc/acme or /etc/prometheus-exporter, at most 64 KiB, or uhttpd's own files, /etc/uhttpd.crt and /etc/uhttpd.key. The field marks a path elsewhere as validate refuses it (TLS_PATH). It does the same for a file there that is not a regular file of that size, or whose links lead out (TLS_FILE). TLS key key Basic auth user auth_user Basic auth password auth_password, in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth Not a field of the form: Save, Save & Apply and Revert never touch it, and the page never reads the hash. The row says Set or Not set, as the ubus object's password answers. It has two buttons, which act at once. See Basic auth password.

The basic auth fields show even without the TLS files, and the ubus object refuses them there. If the page hid them, LuCI would unset them (it unsets an option whose depends are not met), which would drop the user on Save and leave the hash unused.

docs.title: Basic auth password
docs.text:
Like LuCI's own router password, this password is changed apart from the form, and at once:

  • Change password… opens a dialog with New password and Confirmation, which must match: 1 to 256 bytes, without control characters.
    • Its Change password hands the password to the ubus object's set_password, which saves its hash and reloads the service.
    • Cancel, or Escape, changes nothing.
    • The dialog says that the password applies at once, and that every scraper must send it from then on.
    • The button needs TLS certificate and TLS key filled in, as basic auth does. Without them, the row says so.
  • Remove password shows while a hash is saved. It asks for confirmation, then hands set_password an empty password, which removes the hash and reloads the service. It needs Basic auth user to be empty, because a user without a password is refused. So the row says to empty the user and Save & Apply first.

When either is done, a notification says so. When it fails, its dialog says why. The page never stores the password, and sends it only to set_password. A login that may only read sees whether a password is saved, with the buttons disabled.

docs.title: Limits tab
docs.text:
The tab's description says that the limits keep a slow or broken collector from costing the whole scrape.

Field Option Notes Scrape timeout scrape_timeout Collector budget collector_budget Program timeout exec_timeout Sample limit max_samples Reply sample limit max_scrape_samples

docs.title: Main section
docs.text:
• The page writes every field, even at its default (option enabled '1'). The exceptions are the TLS files and basic auth, which it leaves out while they are empty. Emptying any other field is refused.
  • Emptying the user turns basic auth off, and leaves the saved hash unused.
  • Basic auth without both TLS files is refused, and so is a user without a password.

docs.title: Collectors tab
docs.text:
The tab has one row per collector that the ubus object's collectors lists, sorted by title. Each row shows:

  • its title, with its help below;
  • its package: Base, or the rest of the package's name after ucode-prometheus-exporter-, such as wifi, with the whole name on hover;
  • a switch for enabled;
  • an Edit button, for a collector with options.

Above the table, a count shows how many collectors are switched on, as the switches on the page stand: 12 of 45 collectors enabled. Collectors that are installed but do not load are listed above the form. When collectors cannot be called, the table says The collectors could not be read.

Edit opens a dialog with:

  • a field per option of the collector, by its type, labelled by the option's title, with its help and datatype;
  • for a collector that runs programs, a field for the core's timeout, labelled Program timeout. Its placeholder is the seconds the collector gets while the field is empty: its own default, or exec_timeout as the Limits tab has it;
  • read-only rows: Reads (the configs it reads), Runs (the programs it runs), Jail mounts (what the jail mounts for it) and, when there are any, Jail problems.

An option's label is the title the collector declares for it, shown as the collector gives it. Like the collector's own title and help, it comes from the router, so LuCI cannot translate it. LuCI labels the core's options in its own language: Enabled, Program timeout, Budget and Sample limit. A field's accessible name is its title and the collector's name, such as Excluded devices option of the diskstats collector.

The first field has the focus when the dialog opens. The dialog's Save stages its values in uci, where they show among the unsaved changes. Dismiss, or Escape, drops them. Either way, the focus goes back to the row's Edit. The page's Save & Apply applies the staged values with the rest.

A login with only read access can open the dialog too, with its fields and Save disabled.

A collector has a config collector section only while something differs from its defaults, its switch included. The page adds the section when a value first differs, and removes it once all values are back to their defaults. While the section is there, it holds the switch and every option the collector declares, each written out, and timeout only when it is set. A collector whose row did not change keeps its section as it was.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The page checks values with the ubus object's validate, as the exporter reads them:

  • the main section's values while they are typed, and again before Save;
  • a dialog's values while they are typed, and again before the dialog stages them.

Nothing the exporter would refuse is saved or staged.

validate answers each refusal with a code and its arguments. The page turns each into a sentence of its own, in the user's language, that names the field by its title, not its option: Port must be an integer from 1 to 65535, not 0, Basic auth user needs HTTPS: set TLS certificate and TLS key, or the password crosses the network in the clear. A collector's option is named by the title the collector gives it, untranslated. For a code the page does not know, from a newer exporter, it shows the exporter's English message after the field's title.

While another tab is shown, a tab with fields the exporter or LuCI would refuse shows how many on its title, with LuCI's own badge.

A Save that the exporter would refuse opens LuCI's Save error dialog, wherever the page is scrolled. The dialog lists each refused field and why. The same list stays above the form until the values are fixed.

  • Each field is named by its tab, such as HTTPS & login → Basic auth user.
  • A collector's option is named by the collector's title and the option's, such as Collectors → Disk I/O → Excluded devices.
  • The name is a link. It closes the dialog, shows the tab, and gives the focus to the field, or to the collector's Edit.

A refused collector dialog says why inside the dialog.

The browser checks the regex datatype as a JavaScript regular expression, which catches unbalanced brackets. The exporter compiles it as POSIX extended, so the object's validate has the last word.

The page's sentences for validate's problem codes are its own translations of the English in config/problems.uc. A test holds the two to the same codes, so a new code goes into both in the same change.

docs.title: Without the ubus object
docs.text:
The ubus object may be missing while rpcd reloads or the package is being upgraded. The page then says The exporter's ubus object is not available (rpcd may be restarting). Reload in a moment. and is read-only: no field can be changed, and Save is disabled. The page shows a failed call by its message, never with LuCI's stack trace.

The page takes the object as missing on:

  • uhttpd's JSON-RPC errors -32000 (no such object) and -32002 (access cannot be checked: rpcd, which holds the sessions, is not answering);
  • ubus's codes 3 and 4 (method or object not found).

docs.title: Status → Prometheus exporter
docs.text:
The page runs each enabled collector once, a test run, when it opens and on Refresh, never on a timer. The test run is the ubus object's status: a scrape of its own on the router, apart from the service's scrapes, which runs a quarantined collector all the same. So its results can differ from what Prometheus gets, and the page says so above the tables.

Part Content Banner What needs attention, above the tables. See Banners. Service Whether it runs, is enabled in the settings, and starts at boot; where it serves /metrics, marked (reachable from the router only) on loopback; whether a scrape logs in, over HTTPS; whether the reply is compressed. Collectors The test run's counts, as 3 failed, 20 OK, 3 with nothing to observe, 0 off., then a row per installed collector. See Collectors.

docs.title: Banners
docs.text: Banner When Content Error The service is enabled and not running. The exporter is enabled but not running: Prometheus gets nothing., with buttons to System → Startup and System log. Notice The service is switched off in its settings, and not running. That Prometheus gets nothing, with a button to Services → Prometheus exporter. Warning Collectors failed in the test run. How many, by title: 3 collectors failed in the test run: … Notice The service quarantined collectors. How many, by title, and that restarting the service tries them at once.

docs.title: Collectors
docs.text:
Column Content Collector Its title and name. Test run How it did in the test run, in words: OK; Failed, with the error's detail, then its code, which links to Error codes, and its jail mounts folded away; Nothing to observe, in italics, with why; or Not run: switched off. Duration Its time in the test run. Service's scrapes What the service's own scrapes found of it, from the running instance's ledger (the ubus object's service of each collector). Quarantined, with when the service tries it again and why. Left out at the deadline, in the service's last scrape or how many scrapes ago, within the last 10. Empty otherwise.

The rows are grouped in this order, and sorted by title within a group:

  1. Failed in the test run.
  2. Quarantined, or recently left out at the deadline, by the service.
  3. OK.
  4. Nothing to observe.
  5. Not run.

An error code the page does not know is still shown and linked. An error without a code is shown as it is. Status never rests on colour alone: each state is in words. On a narrow screen, a theme that shows each cell's column heading shows it only over a cell that has content.

Without the ubus object, the page says so, as the settings page does.

docs.title: ACL
docs.text:
/usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/luci-app-prometheus-exporter.json:

Access ubus methods of prometheus-exporter uci read collectors, interfaces, password, status, validate prometheus-exporter write set_password prometheus-exporter

It grants nothing else. In particular, it grants neither read nor write on /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth, which holds the hash. Only a login that may write gets set_password, which writes the hash.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Content /www/luci-static/resources/view/prometheus-exporter/settings.js Services → Prometheus exporter. /www/luci-static/resources/view/prometheus-exporter/status.js Status → Prometheus exporter. /www/luci-static/resources/prometheus-exporter.js What both pages share. /www/luci-static/resources/prometheus-exporter/widgets.js The settings page's widgets: the listen interface's picker, basic auth's password and its dialogs, and the Collectors tab's table and its Edit dialog. /usr/share/luci/menu.d/luci-app-prometheus-exporter.json The menu entries. /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/luci-app-prometheus-exporter.json The ACL.

The translation template is luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot in the source tree.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • How to use the LuCI app

docs.title: Make Targets
docs.text: Every target runs in Docker, except feed-makefile, a shell script that uses curl. Nothing is installed on the host. monitoring-lab waits for its servers with curl on the host. fixtures and bench-device reach a device over ssh.

docs.title: Tests and checks
docs.text: Target Description test Runs the unit, integration and docs generator tests, with utest, in the OpenWrt image of OPENWRT_VERSION. Unless FILTER or MODULES narrows the run, it first runs the strip check (devenv/scripts/strip-check.sh): the comment stripper's tests, and every file the packages install, stripped as the build strips it. Each ucode file must compile to the same stripped bytecode as its source. unit test/unit/ only, with the strip check. integration test/integration/ only. watch All tests, then again whenever a file under src/, test/, files/, devenv/scripts/ or docs/gen/ changes. lint Loads every module on the release's ucode, so a function that ucode lacks fails here. Compiles every test, program and handler, and runs sh -n on every shell script. Parses the JSON of luci/, and the LuCI views as the function bodies LuCI compiles them into, with quickjs. Fails on LuCI code that could turn data into markup (devenv/scripts/luci-dom-lint.sh). Checks the pinned documentation links (devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh, see Link check). Fails while a generated reference page is not what docs-gen would write. Runs test/feed/, the tests of feed-makefile's generator. Then checks that luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot is what pot would write. same-code Checks that the sources differ from REV's (main by default) only in comments and blank lines. Each ucode file of src/ and files/ that differs must compile to the same stripped bytecode, and each JavaScript file of luci/ must give esbuild the same tokens. FILES narrows the paths. Changes nothing (devenv/scripts/same-code.sh). shell A shell in the development image. image Rebuilds the development image, pulling its base again.

docs.title: Packages and the device
docs.text: Target Description package Builds the apks with the OpenWrt SDK of OPENWRT_ARCH and OPENWRT_VERSION, into bin/, and the devkit's into bin/devkit/. It strips every comment from the ucode and JavaScript files the packages install, keeping a newline for each line of a comment (devenv/scripts/strip-comments.py, on the SDK's Python). template-package Builds the devkit's template collector package, devkit/template, with the same SDK, into bin/template/. It builds it as a package of another tree, against this tree's release of the exporter. package-check Runs package, then installs the packages offline in an OpenWrt image that carries their dependencies. It scrapes a real uhttpd on loopback, and calls the ubus object in a real rpcd, first with the base package alone, then with the LuCI app. It checks the files, the dependencies and the ACL, and that each installed ucode file compiles to the same stripped bytecode as its source. Then it installs the devkit, runs the template collector's tests on it from the template's own utest config, and has collector check pass the template. e2e Runs package and template-package, then boots OpenWrt (procd, ubusd, netifd) in a privileged container without network. It checks the service in its jail as packages come and go and its config changes, and checks its ubus object, without LuCI. It installs, serves and removes the template collector's package beside the exporter's. lab Runs package, then OpenWrt under procd in a privileged container, left running, with every collector package and the LuCI app installed. LuCI is on http://LAB_ADDRESS:LAB_LUCI_PORT/ (root, no password), and /metrics on http://LAB_ADDRESS:LAB_METRICS_PORT/metrics. make lab again starts it afresh with new packages. See How to use the lab. lab-down Removes the lab's container. browser Runs package, then the Playwright tests of test/browser/ against LuCI in a container, with the built packages, the ubus object in a real rpcd, real collectors, and a stand-in for procd and netifd. It also checks, with esbuild, that the app's JavaScript as LuCI serves it has its sources' tokens. Results and screenshots go to bin/browser/. pot Writes luci/po/templates/prometheus-exporter.pot with openwrt/luci's scanner. Fails, and writes nothing, when the scanner warns. fixtures Reads the sources of test/fixtures/SOURCES from HOST over ssh into test/fixtures/NAME/. See How to capture fixtures.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text: Target Description bench Runs each collector, and whole scrapes, on the generated worlds, in the package-check image. Prints a table, and writes bin/bench/<label>.json. Checks the scaling, memory, turn and request budgets of test/bench/budgets.uc, and, when unconstrained, the time budgets too. bench-worlds Writes the worlds to bin/bench/worlds/. bench-device Runs the benchmark on HOST over ssh, from its /tmp, with its own ucode. It installs nothing, and removes everything it copied. bench-qemu Runs package and bench-worlds, then the benchmark on OpenWrt's malta target, a MIPS 24Kc, with the built packages installed from the release's feed. The guest is little-endian in qemu-system-mipsel, or big-endian in qemu-system-mips (QEMU_ENDIAN). Before the bench, the guest checks the code that reads data in the CPU's byte order (devenv/scripts/qemu-checks.uc), and the target fails if a check does. bench-src With BENCH_REV, extracts that revision's src/ into bin/bench/rev-<rev>. bench and bench-device run it.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Target Description monitoring-check Checks monitoring/, each tool in its official image, without the network:- every metric family and label that its rules, their tests and its dashboards name is in Metrics (devenv/scripts/monitoring-refs.py, in the docs' mkdocs image);- promtool check rules and promtool test rules;- vmalert -dryRun and vmalert-tool unittest on the same files;- percli lint of the Perses dashboards against the plugins the Perses image ships;- the Grafana dashboards take their data source from a variable;- no rule matches a job or instance by name, and no dashboard matches them except by its variables, unless the rule says monitoring-check: allow-target-matcher.The metric check and the lint are also given input they must refuse. monitoring-lab Runs Prometheus, Grafana and Perses on the running lab (LAB_NAME), with monitoring/'s rules and dashboards, and leaves them running. It applies the dashboards to Perses with percli lint --online and percli apply. After MONITORING_WAIT seconds, it runs every panel's queries through Grafana's and Perses's APIs. It writes a report to bin/monitoring/report.txt and screenshots to bin/monitoring/screenshots/. See How to use the lab. monitoring-lab-down Removes monitoring-lab's containers and network. luci-screenshots Runs lab as a lab of its own (SCREENSHOTS_LAB, on ports SCREENSHOTS_LUCI_PORT 18080 and SCREENSHOTS_METRICS_PORT 19100). Takes the LuCI app's screenshots for the docs, docs/how-to/img/luci-*.png, with Playwright in the browser tests' image, and shrinks them with pngquant. Removes the lab afterwards. See devenv/scripts/luci-screenshots.sh. failure-demo Runs package, then shows this exporter and the feed's Lua exporter when what they read breaks. A Prometheus server (the official image, prom/prometheus) scrapes them every 15 s with its 10 s timeout. The scenarios are a hung ubus daemon, a program that never exits, and a label that is not UTF-8, each exporter in an unprivileged container of its own; and a conntrack table of FD_CONNTRACK connections on QEMU's malta, each exporter booted under procd. Prints a table, and keeps it with the logs and the JSON in bin/failure-demo/. Takes some 25 minutes, with the network; not run in CI. See What happens when a collector breaks.

docs.title: Release
docs.text: Target Description feed-makefile Writes the Makefile of the packages.ucode.dev feed for release VERSION to OUT, or to standard output. The Makefile is this tree's package Makefile as the v<VERSION> tag has it, set to build from GitHub's tarball of the tag, which the target downloads and hashes. See How to publish a release to the package feed.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Target Description docs make -C docs build. docs-mike make -C docs build-mike. docs-test make -C docs test. docs-serve make -C docs serve. docs-gen Writes the generated reference pages, docs/reference/collectors.md, metrics.md, uci-config.md, error-codes.md, command.md and migration.md, in the development image. It writes them from the code, the fixtures and docs/gen/notes.uc, and migration.md also from docs/gen/migration.md, migration.uc and feed-exporters.json. It fails, writing nothing, when the notes contradict the code, or when the migration's mapping contradicts the feed's exporters or the collectors. See How to write documentation. feed-inventory Writes docs/gen/feed-exporters.json: what the feed's Lua and ucode exporters write, and how they are packaged. It reads their sources in openwrt/packages at FEED_PACKAGES_REF, which it downloads from GitHub. docs-gen writes the migration page from this file. With CHECK=1, it writes nothing, and fails when the feed is not what the file says.

test, unit, integration, watch, lint, shell and docs-gen run in the image ucode-prometheus-exporter-openwrt:<arch>-<version>-<hash>, built on first use from devenv/services/openwrt/Dockerfile. <hash> is the Dockerfile's hash, so worktrees with different Dockerfiles do not overwrite each other's image. The container has no network, and sees the checkout read-only. Only docs-gen may write, and only to docs/reference/.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Applies to Description OPENWRT_VERSION 25.12.5 all The OpenWrt release of the images and the SDK. CI also runs 25.12.0, the API floor. OPENWRT_ARCH x86_64 all The architecture of the images and the SDK. FILTER — tests, browser, bench, bench-device, bench-qemu Tests: only those whose name matches. Benchmark: a regex of world/case. VERBOSE — tests, package, template-package Tests: one line per test. package, template-package: the SDK's V=s. MODULES — tests Only these test files or directories. TEST_TIMEOUT 300 tests Seconds the whole run may take. Past them, the run is stopped, and the test file it was in is named. CI — all Runs containers without a TTY. HOST — fixtures, bench-device An ssh destination. NAME — fixtures The fixture set to write, test/fixtures/NAME/. LAB_NAME ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab lab, lab-down, monitoring-lab, monitoring-lab-down The lab's container. LAB_ADDRESS 127.0.0.1 lab The host address its ports are published on. LAB_LUCI_PORT 8080 lab LuCI's port on the host. LAB_METRICS_PORT 9100 lab /metrics' port on the host. MONITORING_ADDRESS 127.0.0.1 monitoring-lab The host address Prometheus, Grafana and Perses are published on. PROMETHEUS_PORT 9090 monitoring-lab Prometheus's port on the host. GRAFANA_PORT 3000 monitoring-lab Grafana's port on the host. PERSES_PORT 8081 monitoring-lab Perses's port on the host. MONITORING_WAIT 180 monitoring-lab Seconds of the lab's scrapes before the panels are checked. BENCH_ARGS — benchmark Options of test/bench/bench.uc: -r N runs at least, -t S seconds at least. BENCH_REV — bench, bench-device Bench another revision's src/ with this benchmark. BENCH_CPUS — bench A share of a CPU, 0.05 at least, as a CFS quota of a 20 ms period. BENCH_CPUSET — bench The CPUs the container may use. BENCH_MEMORY — bench The container's memory, without swap. BENCH_LABEL devenv and the limits bench The name of the result. BENCH_DEVICE_LABEL HOST bench-device The name of the result. QEMU_ENDIAN le bench-qemu le: malta/le, mipsel_24kc, as MT7621-class routers. be: malta/be, mips_24kc, as ath79-class ones. QEMU_SHIFT 1 bench-qemu The guest runs at 1000/2^QEMU_SHIFT MIPS: 1 is 500, 2 is 250. QEMU_MEMORY 128 bench-qemu The guest's memory, in MB. BENCH_QEMU_LABEL qemu-malta-shift<N>, qemu-malta-be-shift<N> big-endian bench-qemu The name of the result. FD_SCENARIOS all failure-demo The scenarios to run, of healthy, hung-ubus, stuck-nft, bad-utf8 and conntrack. FD_SCRAPES 8 failure-demo The scrapes Prometheus makes of each exporter in a scenario. FD_CONNTRACK 20000 failure-demo The connections of conntrack's table. FD_QEMU_CPUS 0.65 failure-demo The share of a host CPU that conntrack's QEMU gets. It runs without -icount, so that the guest's time is Prometheus's. Pick the share that makes the guest's loop turn near 9.9 µs, bench-qemu's 500-MIPS 24Kc; the guest prints its turn. FEED_PACKAGES_REF a commit of openwrt-25.12 feed-inventory The openwrt/packages commit, or branch, to read the feed's exporters from. CHECK — feed-inventory Check docs/gen/feed-exporters.json against the feed, writing nothing. VERSION — feed-makefile The release, X.Y.Z, without the v. OUT — feed-makefile Where to write the Makefile. TARBALL — feed-makefile The tag's tarball, already on disk, instead of downloading it. HASH — feed-makefile Offline: transform this tree's package Makefile, with this sha256 as PKG_HASH. 
make unit FILTER='collectors.wifi' VERBOSE=1
make unit MODULES=test/unit/prometheus/collectors/wifi_test.uc
make bench FILTER='typical/scrape' BENCH_CPUS=0.35 BENCH_CPUSET=0

docs.title: docs/Makefile
docs.text:
Target Description build Builds the site into bin/site/ with mkdocs build --strict. build-mike The same with the versioned config, mkdocs.mike.yml: the mike plugin, the version selector and the outdated-version banner. test Runs test/docs/'s shell and Node tests: the docs version, guard, publish and link-check scripts, with a full mike publish to a throwaway local repository, and the gh-pages 404 redirect. No network. publish Publishes release REF (vX.Y.Z, or a docs/X.Y branch) to gh-pages with devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh. It runs in the image build-mike builds in, with the network and the checkout's git credentials. See Docs publishing. serve Serves the site with live reload on http://localhost:8000, or the port in DOCS_PORT. dev is the same. clean Removes bin/site/. help Lists the targets. The default.

build and serve run the pinned squidfunk/mkdocs-material:9.5.17 image as the invoking user. build-mike, test and publish run ucode-prometheus-exporter-docs:9.5.17: the same image with git, Node, and the pinned mike of devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt. It is built on first use from devenv/services/docs/Dockerfile.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The metric families each collector writes, and those a scrape writes of itself. Types, labels and help texts are what the collectors write: each collector runs as a scrape runs it, on each set of captures in test/fixtures/ (an access point, a router, a second router, made-up captures), with its defaults and with each boolean option the other way. A family that only an option writes says which.

The labels are those seen on the captures; a collector leaves out a label it has no value for, so a device may show fewer. Families whose names hold what the source reports (a driver's statistics, a kernel table's fields) are one row, their name a pattern in <>. Families no capture shows are listed from the collector's code, and say why.

Renamed metrics lists the names that changed from the feed's exporters.

docs.title: The scrape's own
docs.text:
Every scrape ends with these, whatever collect[] selects: node_exporter's families of each collector that ran, and the exporter's version. While the exporter collector is selected, the scrape writes the instance's counters and each collector's samples too, after the exporter collector's own families, whether that collector ran or not: the deadline, a breaker or a crash cannot leave them out.

Family Type Labels Help Notes ucode_prometheus_exporter_scrapes_total counter — Scrapes the exporter answered since the service started. Written while the exporter collector is selected, in the service's scrapes, which keep the instance's ledger. Reset when the service restarts. ucode_prometheus_exporter_auth_failures_total counter — Requests basic auth refused since the service started. As scrapes_total: the requests basic auth refused (401). ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_failures_total counter collector, reason Scrapes in which a collector failed, by its error code, since the service started. As scrapes_total: a collector's failures by error code. ucode_prometheus_exporter_program_timeouts_total counter collector Programs of a collector killed at their timeout since the service started. As scrapes_total: programs killed at their timeout. ucode_prometheus_exporter_quarantines_total counter collector Times a collector's circuit breaker tripped since the service started. As scrapes_total: times a collector's circuit breaker tripped. ucode_prometheus_exporter_deadline_skips_total counter collector Scrapes whose deadline left a collector out, or killed its program, since the service started. As scrapes_total: times the deadline left a collector out or killed its program, this scrape's included. ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_samples gauge collector Samples a collector wrote in this scrape. Written while the exporter collector is selected: the samples each collector wrote in this scrape. Also in check and in the command line's scrape. node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds gauge collector node_exporter: Duration of a collector scrape. — node_scrape_collector_success gauge collector node_exporter: Whether a collector succeeded. — node_scrape_collector_observing gauge collector Whether a collector had something to observe: 0 when its hardware, kernel feature or service is not there. — ucode_prometheus_exporter_collector_quarantined gauge collector Whether a collector is quarantined: its circuit breaker tripped, and it is not run until its cool-down is over. — ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info gauge version A metric with a constant '1' value labeled by the version of ucode-prometheus-exporter. —

docs.title: agh
docs.text:
AdGuard Home. Collector.

Family Type Labels Help Notes adguard_up gauge — Whether AdGuard Home's HTTP API answered: 1 or 0. — adguard_build_info gauge version AdGuard Home's version: always 1. — adguard_running gauge — Whether AdGuard Home's DNS server runs: 1 or 0. — adguard_protection_enabled gauge — Whether AdGuard Home's protection, its filtering, is on: 1 or 0. — adguard_start_time_seconds gauge — When AdGuard Home started, in seconds since the epoch. — adguard_stats_window_seconds gauge — The statistics window of AdGuard Home, in seconds: its totals, adguard_stats_*, are of that much time up to now; 0 with its statistics off. — adguard_stats_dns_queries gauge — DNS queries AdGuard Home answered in its statistics window (adguard_stats_window_seconds): a total that drops as the window moves, not a counter. — adguard_stats_blocked_filtering gauge — Of them, the queries its filter lists and rules blocked, in the statistics window. — adguard_stats_replaced_safebrowsing gauge — Of them, the queries safe browsing blocked, in the statistics window. — adguard_stats_replaced_safesearch gauge — Of them, the queries safe search rewrote, in the statistics window. — adguard_stats_replaced_parental gauge — Of them, the queries parental control blocked, in the statistics window. — adguard_stats_avg_processing_time_seconds gauge — The mean time AdGuard Home took to answer a query in the statistics window, in seconds. —

in seconds — chrony_tracking_reference_timestamp_seconds gauge — Chrony tracking Reference timestamp — chrony_tracking_system_time_seconds gauge — Chrony tracking System time — if chronyd was not correcting it, in PPMs — chrony_tracking_residual_frequency_ppms gauge — For the currently selected reference source, the difference between the frequency it suggests and the one currently in use, in PPMs — chrony_tracking_skew_ppms gauge — The estimated error bound on the frequency, in PPMs — chrony_tracking_update_interval_seconds gauge — The time elapsed since the last measurement from the reference source was processed, in seconds — chrony_tracking_stratum gauge — Chrony tracking client stratum — chrony_sources_last_sample_age_seconds gauge source_address, chrony_sources_reachability_success gauge source_address, source_name Chrony sources last poll reachability success — chrony_sources_last_sample_offset_seconds gauge source_address, source_name Chrony sources last sample offset in seconds — chrony_sources_last_sample_error_margin_seconds gauge source_address, source_name Chrony sources last sample margin of error in seconds — chrony_sources_polling_interval_seconds gauge source_address, source_name Chrony sources polling interval in seconds — chrony_sources_state_info gauge source_address, source_name, source_state, source_mode Chrony sources state info — chrony_sources_stratum gauge source_address, source_name Chrony sources stratum — chrony_serverstats_ntp_packets_received_total counter — The number of valid docs.title: nat_traffic
docs.text:
Traffic per host. Collector.

Family Type Labels Help Notes node_nat_traffic_bytes gauge host, peer Bytes of the connections of a host on this side of the router, both directions. host is the end of a connection on this side of the router: one of the router's own addresses, or an address on-link to an interface without a default route (a LAN's subnet, a delegated IPv6 prefix). A connection with neither end there is written as host="other". Only the 2048 hosts with the most bytes get series of their own; the rest are written as host="other" too. peer, with the peers option only, is the other end. It makes a series per host and peer, which come and go with the connections. Only the 16384 pairs with the most bytes keep their peer; the rest are written as peer="other" of their host. host="other" always has peer="other".

docs.title: Migrate from prometheus-node-exporter-lua/-ucode
docs.text:
This page maps each package and each metric family of the packages feed's exporters to what this exporter has in its place. It also shows how to carry queries, recording rules and the configuration over.

make docs-gen writes the tables from two sources: the feed exporters' own sources, prometheus-node-exporter-lua 2026.06.05-r1 and prometheus-node-exporter-ucode 2024.02.07-r2, from openwrt/packages@705e1cc3beb7a0cb3ef53ba18a3ba1fed8f4342c (which make feed-inventory reads), and what this exporter's collectors write, as Metrics lists it. The generator refuses a family of the feed's exporters that has no row here.

The steps are in How to move from the feed's exporters. Why the names changed is in Renamed metrics and About metric names.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Each family of each exporter, by what it is here:

  • same: the same name and labels;
  • renamed: another name;
  • relabeled: the same name with other labels, or with other values of them (cpu="0" for cpu="cpu0");
  • missing: nothing here writes it.

A family of a collector whose name is computed (meminfo's node_memory_<Field>_bytes) counts once.

Change Lua exporter's families ucode exporter's families same 93 65 renamed 91 24 relabeled 23 8 missing 4 0 all 211 97

There is no option to write the old names. For a fleet that runs both exporters for a while, see A transition.

These packages have no counterpart in the feed:

  • ucode-prometheus-exporter-cli, the prometheus-exporter command. It prints a scrape on standard output, and checks the configuration and a collector module. The feed's exporters had their command in the base package (/usr/bin/prometheus-node-exporter-lua and -ucode, a scrape on standard output). Here the service needs none of it, and service prometheus-exporter check belongs to the base package. Install it for cron jobs that push a scrape: see How to push metrics.
  • The groups, ucode-prometheus-exporter-network, -wireless, -hardware and -full, which install several collectors: see How to choose collectors.
  • luci-app-prometheus-exporter, the LuCI app, and ucode-prometheus-exporter-devkit, which a collector of another package is written and tested with.
  • The collectors the feed had none of: ucode-prometheus-exporter-agh, ucode-prometheus-exporter-chrony, ucode-prometheus-exporter-dhcp_leases, ucode-prometheus-exporter-diskstats, ucode-prometheus-exporter-interrupts, ucode-prometheus-exporter-mmc, ucode-prometheus-exporter-pressure, ucode-prometheus-exporter-qdisc, ucode-prometheus-exporter-sockstat.

A query that selects collectors still works: collect[]= as the Lua exporter has it, and collect= as the ucode one does. Name a collector as here (nft-counters, ltq-dsl), or by its module (nft_counters). wifi_stations is refused: wifi writes the stations.

docs.title: PromQL
docs.text:
How the most common queries and recording rules on the old names read now. The values are the same unless the notes above say otherwise.

Wi-Fi. The wifi_ families are node_exporter's node_wifi_ families, with these labels:

  • radio: the wifi-device (the Lua exporter's device);
  • device: the interface (the Lua and ucode exporters' ifname);
  • mac_address: a station (was mac).

Only node_wifi_network_info has the network's SSID and BSSID:

# was: wifi_network_signal_dbm{ssid="home"}
node_wifi_network_signal_dbm * on (radio, device) group_left (ssid) node_wifi_network_info{ssid="home"}

# was: sum by (ifname) (wifi_stations)    (Lua's wifi_stations)
sum by (device) (node_wifi_stations)

# was: wifi_network_quality > 50          (a percentage)
node_wifi_network_quality_ratio > 0.5

# was: rate(wifi_station_receive_bytes_total{mac="..."}[5m])
rate(node_wifi_station_receive_bytes_total{mac_address="..."}[5m])

hostapd stations. The network's labels are on hostapd_station_info, one series per station:

# was: hostapd_station_signal_dbm{ssid="home"}
hostapd_station_signal_dbm * on (vif, station) group_left (ssid) hostapd_station_info{ssid="home"}

NAT traffic. There is a series per host on this side of the router, where there was one per pair of addresses:

# was: sum by (src) (node_nat_traffic)
node_nat_traffic_bytes

# was: topk(10, node_nat_traffic)         (pairs)
topk(10, node_nat_traffic_bytes)          # hosts; the pairs need the option peers

CPU. cpu is the CPU's number, and guest time is counted apart:

# was: sum by (cpu) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle",cpu="cpu0"}[5m]))
sum by (cpu) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle",cpu="0"}[5m]))

Gauges that ended in _total. node_procs_running, node_procs_blocked and dawn_ap_stations no longer end in _total. The counters nft_counter_packets_total and nft_counter_bytes_total now do. A rate() of one of the old gauges was a mistake, and still is.

Units. A family whose unit changed is a renamed family. The Lua exporter's wifi_network_bitrate, in kbit/s, is node_wifi_network_transmit_bits_per_second, * 1000. ModemManager's and bmx7's percentages are ratios, / 100. A recording rule keeps an old dashboard working until it is changed:

groups:
  - name: feed-exporter-names
    rules:
      - record: wifi_network_bitrate
        expr: label_replace(node_wifi_network_transmit_bits_per_second / 1000, "ifname", "$1", "device", "(.*)")
      - record: wifi_network_quality
        expr: label_replace(node_wifi_network_quality_ratio * 100, "ifname", "$1", "device", "(.*)")
      - record: node_nat_traffic
        expr: label_replace(node_nat_traffic_bytes, "src", "$1", "host", "(.*)")

unbound. Each counter is per thread, labeled thread, as letsencrypt/unbound_exporter writes them: sum without (thread) (unbound_queries_total) is the Lua exporter's unbound_num_queries_total.

Is the collector there? node_scrape_collector_success == 0 still finds a collector that failed. But a collector whose service or hardware is not there succeeds here, with node_scrape_collector_observing 0, where the Lua exporter failed it. See About nothing to observe.

docs.title: A transition
docs.text:
A fleet that moves router by router has both names for a while. Where only the name changed, and the labels and the value are the same, Prometheus can rename the old exporter's families at ingestion. Dashboards and alerts written on the new names then see every router. Put this metric_relabel_configs in the scrape job of the routers still on a feed exporter. It covers every such family of the tables above.

metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: bmx7_mem_usage
    target_label: __name__
    replacement: bmx7_memory_usage_bytes
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: bmx7_plugin
    target_label: __name__
    replacement: bmx7_plugin_info
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: bmx7_status
    target_label: __name__
    replacement: bmx7_info
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: bmx7_tunIn
