docs.title: The configuration
docs.text:
When the package is installed, its uci-defaults script takes over the settings of /etc/config/prometheus-node-exporter-ucode, or, without it, of /etc/config/prometheus-node-exporter-lua. It writes them into /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, once, and logs what it did (see Log messages).

  • It does so only while /etc/config/prometheus-exporter is as the package ships it.
  • It leaves the old file as it was.
  • apk keeps a feed exporter's config at removal only if it was changed, so what there is to take over is what someone set.
Old setting Taken over? listen_interface, listen_port, http_keepalive, cert, key, omit_zero_values of the main section Yes, each whose value this exporter accepts. A value it would refuse is left at its default, and logged. A port that is the old exporter's default (9101 for the ucode one, 9100 for the Lua one) becomes 9100. The ucode exporter's config collector sections (wifi's stations) Yes, each named section, with each option checked as the service checks it. An option the collector does not have is left out, and a value it refuses is left at its default; each is logged, so the configuration stays valid. The script runs as the base package is installed, before the packages installed with it. So a collector not installed yet is checked against the options the feed's ucode exporter had for it (wifi's stations), and the options every collector has (enabled, budget, max_samples). Both old configs Only the ucode exporter's. Which collectors were installed No: install the packages of Packages. Whether the old service was enabled No: the exporter is enabled when it is installed. The Lua exporter's textfile directory Nothing to take over: textfile reads /var/prometheus by default, as the Lua exporter did. WireGuard peer descriptions No: the old exporters always labeled peers with their description; here, only with wireguard's option peer_names.

docs.title: Service Commands
docs.text: The init script is /etc/init.d/prometheus-exporter (procd, START=60). Every action is also service prometheus-exporter <action>.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action What it does start Does nothing with option enabled '0'. Otherwise it checks the configuration (/usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc --config), sets up basic auth's file, and makes the state directory and the directories the collectors own. Then it hands procd the uhttpd instance, in its jail. It refuses an invalid configuration, and logs why at err. It waits for the listen interface: while the interface has no address, it logs deferring start until listen interface <interface> becomes ready, and starts once the interface comes up. stop Stops the instances. restart stop, then start. The new instance starts without state. reload Checks the configuration. If it is invalid, keeps the running instance and logs why. If it is valid, runs start again; procd restarts the instance only if its command line, mounts or watched files changed. enable, disable Adds or removes the boot link /etc/rc.d/S60prometheus-exporter. enabled Exits 0 when the boot link is there. running Exits 0 when procd runs the service. status procd's state of the service, then one line: disabled (option enabled in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter), or, while it runs, where it listens. See status. check Checks the configuration, lists every installed collector and runs a scrape, in the service's jail. See check.

option enabled in the main section and the boot link are separate: enabled '0' stops the service whether or not it is enabled at boot.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
While the service runs:

running
listening on http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 16 collectors
Part Shown when listening on <url>, ... One URL per address uhttpd listens on: http:// for HTTP, https:// for HTTPS, *:<port> for every address. nothing when it listens on none. , basic auth uhttpd has basic auth's file: a scrape logs in. , gzip when asked option compress is on. , serving <n> collectors The installed collectors that are enabled.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
service prometheus-exporter check runs the base package's /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/check.uc, which needs no command line. prometheus-exporter check (see The command) runs the same. It prints a line per finding, then every installed collector, then the jail's mounts:

ok   main: HTTP on every address, port 9100, keepalive 70s, exec_timeout 5s, scrape_timeout 10s, collector_budget 5s, max_samples 20000, memory_limit 64 MB (a quarter of the RAM, at most 64), gzip when asked
ok   collectors: 17 installed collectors, their options valid
ok   scrape, in the service's jail: 17 of 17 collectors succeeded, 1 with nothing to observe
ok   scrape: wifi has nothing to observe: no wireless radios

collectors: 17 installed, 17 enabled
  conntrack (Connection tracking): section 'conntrack', enabled
      budget   5s # the main section's collector_budget
      needs    fs
  ...
  textfile (Text files): section 'textfile', enabled
      option   directory="/var/prometheus" # The directory of the *.prom files.
      budget   5s # the main section's collector_budget
      needs    fs log
      paths    /var/prometheus
      makes    /var/prometheus
      mounts   /var/prometheus
  ...

jail mounts:
  /bin/sh
  /etc/config/prometheus-exporter
  /var/prometheus
  /var/run/prometheus-exporter/timesync

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Each finding starts with ok, warn or FAIL. Only a FAIL makes check exit 1. Otherwise it exits 0.

Finding Level main: <listen summary>, exec_timeout <n>s, scrape_timeout <n>s, collector_budget <n>s, max_samples <n>, memory_limit <n> MB[ (a quarter of the RAM, at most 64)], gzip when asked (or no compression (option compress)) ok main: <CODE (detail)>: an option of the main section the exporter does not take, or options that go together not set together FAIL main: cert and key go together; with only cert, it serves HTTP warn main: <file> is missing; it serves HTTP until it is there warn main: <file> is missing; basic auth takes HTTPS only, so the service does not start until it is there FAIL collectors: <n> installed collectors, their options valid ok collector <name>, section '<module>': <CODE (detail)>: an option of its section it does not take FAIL section '<name>' names no installed collector; it is ignored warn an unnamed collector section is ignored: name it after its collector's module warn cannot load collector '<module>': ..., skipping collector: COLLECTOR_INVALID (...) or skipping collector: COLLECTOR_IMPURE (...): a module the loader left out warn jail: <collector>: <problem>: a path or command the jail cannot give warn jail: <collector>: <path> is not there; the service mounts it once it is warn scrape, in the service's jail: <n> of <m> collectors succeeded[, <k> with nothing to observe] (or outside the jail, where ujail cannot run) ok, or warn when one failed scrape: <collector>: <CODE (detail)>: a collector that failed warn scrape: <collector> has nothing to observe: <reason> ok service: <collector> is quarantined: <CODE (detail)>; the service tries it again at the next scrape (or in <n> scrapes), or at once once restarted warn service: the scrape deadline left <collector> out in the last scrape (or <n> scrapes ago, within the last 10) warn

The listen summary is HTTP or HTTPS, on interface <name> or on every address, the port and the keepalive, and basic auth as user "<user>" when basic auth is on. The password's hash is never shown.

docs.title: Collectors
docs.text:
One block per installed collector, enabled or not:

Line Content <name> (<title>): section '<module>', enabled Its name, title, the section that configures it, and whether it is enabled. option Each of its own options: <name>=<value> # <help>. timeout For a collector that runs programs: its seconds, and where they come from: its section's option timeout, the collector's own (meta.timeout) or the main section's exec_timeout. budget The seconds it may take before its circuit breaker trips, and where they come from: its section's option budget, the main section's collector_budget or its timeout and a second more. needs, configs Its meta.needs and meta.configs. paths, makes The paths it reads outside procfs and sysfs, and those the service makes for it. commands Each program it runs, <name>=<path>, or (not found). mounts What the jail mounts for it, when it is enabled.

check runs its scrape as the service's scrapes run: in the service's own jail, with ujail; the collectors in a child process, each stopped at its budget, within scrape_timeout. It uses the committed configuration, and runs a collector the service quarantined all the same.

Where ujail cannot run (not root, or a kernel or container that refuses it a namespace), check runs the scrape outside the jail, as root, with the same guards, and says outside the jail. A collector that works there and fails under procd lacks something in the jail: see The jail.

The service: findings are what the service's own scrapes found, from its running instance's ledger: see The jail.

docs.title: procd
docs.text:
Instance Command When instance1 /usr/sbin/uhttpd -f -c <auth file or /dev/null> -h /dev/null -S -D -o /metrics -O /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/handler.uc [-r prometheus-exporter] -k <keepalive> -t 60 -n 3 -N 10 [-C <cert> -K <key>] -p\|-s <address>:<port> ... While the service is enabled. -s (HTTPS) with cert and key both set and both there, -p (HTTP) otherwise. One -p or -s per address of the listen interface, IPv4 and IPv6, or the port alone for *. -r only with basic auth. -t, -n and -N: see HTTP endpoint. watch /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/watch.uc <path>... While a path an enabled collector reads is not there. See The jail.

procd respawns both. The uhttpd instance runs in a jail: see The jail.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text: Trigger Action A change of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth (the ubus object's set_password sends its event itself), or of a config an enabled collector reads (meta.configs), applied by reload_config reload The listen interface going up or down, unless listen_interface is * reload The event prometheus-exporter.path, which the watch instance sends reload A change of a file procd watches for the instance: the configs it mounts, every collector module, basic auth's file, the TLS certificate and key procd restarts the instance on reload

docs.title: Package scripts
docs.text:
Package On install On removal ucode-prometheus-exporter OpenWrt's defaults (run the uci-defaults script, enable and start the service), then reload rpcd; on an upgrade, restart a running service. Reload rpcd. A collector package reload an enabled service, which restarts it with the collector. A failed reload fails no install. The same, without the collector. luci-app-prometheus-exporter Clear LuCI's index and module caches, reload rpcd. The same.

None of the scripts runs while building an image ($IPKG_INSTROOT set).

docs.text:

  • Log messages: what the service logs.

docs.title: ubus Object
docs.text:
The ubus object prometheus-exporter belongs to the base package. rpcd serves it whether or not the service runs. It serves it from the ucode plugin /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter.uc, which uses src/prometheus/exporter/rpc.uc and its modules rpc/describe.uc, rpc/validate.uc, rpc/sources.uc and rpc/plugin.uc. rpcd loads the plugin when it starts or reloads, and the package reloads rpcd when it is installed, upgraded or removed.

rpcd keeps the methods for the collectors loaded all the time, with rpc/sources.uc only. It compiles the other methods, with rpc.uc and all it imports, when one of them is called, and drops them 120 s after the last such call. The reason: after every call of a plugin's methods, rpcd collects the plugin's garbage, in a pass over everything the plugin holds, and the collectors call their methods at every scrape. See Performance on small routers.

The object reads with the exporter's own modules. The only thing it writes is the hash of basic auth's password, through set_password. Each call reads the committed configuration and the installed collectors afresh.

$ ubus -v list prometheus-exporter
'prometheus-exporter' @085bb3ca
    "collectors":{}
    "validate":{"main":"Table","collectors":"Table"}
    "status":{}
    "interfaces":{}
    "hash_password":{"password":"String"}
    "password":{}
    "set_password":{"password":"String"}
    "wireless":{}
    "wireguard_peers":{}
    "time_daemons":{}

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Arguments Reply collectors none { collectors: [ collector ], skipped: [ message ] } validate { main?, collectors? } { ok, errors: { main: { <option>: refusal }, collectors: { <module>: { <option>: refusal } } } } status none { service: { enabled, boot, running, error, auth, compress }, listen: [ url ], collectors: [ result ], jailed } interfaces none { interfaces: [ { name, proto } ] } hash_password { password } { hash } password none { saved } set_password { password } { saved } wireless none { radios: { <radio>: { disabled, config: { channel, country, htmode }, interfaces: [ { ifname, config: { ssid, mesh_id, encryption } } ] } } } wireguard_peers none { interfaces: { <interface>: { <public key>: <description> } } } time_daemons none { running: { sysntpd, chronyd } }

A call with malformed arguments, or one that fails, gets the reply { error, message }. See Errors.

Who calls which methods, and under which ACL:

flowchart LR
    L["LuCI app<br/>(its ACL, luci-app-prometheus-exporter)"] -- "collectors, interfaces, password,<br/>status, validate; set_password to write" --> O
    C["Collectors in the service's jail<br/>(the service's ubus ACL)"] -- "wireless, wireguard_peers,<br/>time_daemons" --> O
    Root["root, with ubus call"] -- "every method" --> O
    O["prometheus-exporter<br/>(rpcd's ucode plugin)"]
    O -- "status" --> S["rpc-status.uc<br/>a scrape in a process of its own"]
    F["The filesystem collector"] -- "mounts" --> FS["prometheus-exporter.filesystem<br/>(its package's plugin)"]

docs.title: collectors
docs.text:
Every installed collector, sorted by name, and the messages of the modules the loader left out (skipped).

Field of a collector Type Content name string Its name, as collect[] takes it. id string Its module: the name of its section. title, help string meta.title and meta.help. enabled boolean Whether its section enables it. package string or null The package that installed it, from apk's file lists; null when no package did. base boolean or null Whether that package is the base package. options array Its own options, in the order it declares them. For a collector that runs programs, the core's timeout follows them. needs, configs, commands array meta.needs, meta.configs, meta.commands. jail object What the jail gives it: paths, owned, commands ({ <name>: <path or null> }), mounts, problems, missing. See The jail. error string or null The first option of its section that the exporter does not accept, as CODE (detail). Field of an option Type Content name string The option's name. core boolean true for the core's timeout, false for the collector's own. title string Its label, as the collector declares it: Excluded devices. The core's timeout is Program timeout. type string bool, int or string: the type of its default. default any Its default. For timeout, the seconds it gets while unset. default_from string timeout only: where the default's seconds come from, meta.timeout or exec_timeout. help string or null What it does. datatype string or null See UCI configuration. value any Its value as the exporter reads it. When the exporter does not accept it, the value as uci holds it. set boolean Whether its section sets it. error string or null What the exporter expected, for a value it does not accept.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Checks values as the exporter would read them, without saving anything. main holds options of the main section. collectors holds options of collector sections, by module. Values are given as uci holds them: as strings.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter validate '{"main":{"listen_port":"0","auth_user":"p"}}'
{
    "ok": false,
    "errors": {
        "main": {
            "listen_port": {
                "code": "RANGE",
                "min": 1,
                "max": 65535,
                "value": 0,
                "message": "expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0"
            },
            "auth_password": {
                "code": "AUTH_NEEDS_PASSWORD",
                "message": "basic auth needs the hash of a password along with auth_user"
            },
            "auth_user": {
                "code": "AUTH_NEEDS_TLS",
                "message": "basic auth needs HTTPS: set cert and key, or the password crosses the network in the clear"
            }
        },
        "collectors": {

        }
    }
}

For each value it refuses, validate answers a refusal. A refusal says what is wrong with the value as a code, which a client can put in its own words, as LuCI does. It also carries the exporter's English message.

Field of a refusal Type Content code string What is wrong: one of the closed set in UCI configuration, such as RANGE or AUTH_NEEDS_TLS. min, max integer The arguments of the codes that take them: RANGE's bounds, CRYPT_ROUNDS' most rounds. value any What the exporter read: an integer for RANGE and UINTEGER, a list where it got one, a string otherwise. Absent from auth_password's refusal, and from the codes of options that go together. message string The exporter's English message, without the option's name, as check and the log say it.

A client that does not know a code shows message.

  • Each value is checked alone. An empty value is unset, and takes the default.
  • Options nobody declared, and collectors that are not installed, are ignored, as the exporter ignores them.
  • Some of the main section's options go together: basic auth's user, the hash, and the cert and key that basic auth needs. They are checked as if the values given were the whole section.
  • auth_password, the hash, is accepted among main's options, though it is saved apart (see set_password). When it is not given, a user given is checked against the saved hash. The saved hash is never answered.
  • A collector section accepts enabled, budget, the collector's own options, and timeout for a collector that runs programs.
  • No refusal holds the value of auth_password.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Runs one scrape of the enabled collectors, and replies when it is done. It runs them as the service's scrapes do: in the service's own jail, with ujail, where it can; the collectors in a child process, each stopped at its budget, within scrape_timeout. It runs a collector the service quarantined all the same.

rpcd runs the scrape in a process of its own, /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc, and answers other calls meanwhile. Among them are the collectors' calls to objects rpcd serves: wireguard, this object's own, and prometheus-exporter.filesystem. If that process is still running after 60 s, rpcd kills it, with all it started.

One scrape runs at a time. A call made while one runs waits for it, and gets its reply. So repeated calls, such as from a page being refreshed, never run more than one scrape at once.

rpcd answers status later, once the scrape is done: a ucode plugin's defer(), which rpcd has from its 2026 releases. 25.12.0's image has rpcd 2025.12.03, without it. Waiting for the scrape there would hold rpcd, and the scrape's collectors call rpcd's objects. So on that rpcd, status runs nothing, and answers STATUS_FAILED at once, saying to upgrade it:

apk update
apk upgrade rpcd rpcd-mod-ucode
Field Type Content service.enabled boolean or null option enabled of the main section; null when that section is not valid. service.boot boolean Whether the boot link /etc/rc.d/S*prometheus-exporter is there. service.running boolean or null Whether procd runs the uhttpd instance; null when procd cannot be asked. service.error string or null Why procd could not be asked. service.auth boolean or null Whether basic auth is configured. service.compress boolean or null option compress. listen array The URLs the running instance listens on, as http://*:9100/metrics. collectors array One result per installed collector, sorted by name. jailed boolean Whether the scrape ran in the service's jail; false where ujail cannot run, as for a process that is not root's. Field of a result Type Content name, id, title string As in collectors. enabled boolean Whether it ran: a disabled collector does not. success boolean or null Whether it succeeded; null when it did not run. observing boolean or null false for a collector with nothing to observe, true for any other that ran, null when it did not run. reason string or null Why it has nothing to observe, as dnsmasq is disabled. duration number or null Its seconds. error string or null Why it failed, as CODE (detail). mounts array What the jail mounts for it; empty when it is disabled. service object or null What the service's own scrapes found of it, from the ledger of its running instance (see The jail); null when the ledger has nothing of it. Field of service Type Content estimate number or null Its seconds, as the ledger averages them; null before it ran. quarantined boolean Whether its circuit breaker is open, or its trial is due. reason string or null What tripped its breaker, as CODE (detail). retry_in integer or null The scrapes until its trial: 1 for the next. late integer or null The scrapes since the deadline last left it out: 0 for the service's last scrape.

docs.title: interfaces
docs.text:
The logical interfaces netifd has, in its order, as network.interface dump gives them: name, and proto (null when it has none). It never reads /etc/config/network.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter interfaces
{
    "interfaces": [
        {
            "name": "lan",
            "proto": "static"
        },
        {
            "name": "loopback",
            "proto": "static"
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: hash_password
docs.text:
A SHA-512-crypt hash of password, with 1000 rounds and a fresh salt of 16 characters, for auth_password:

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter hash_password '{"password":"…"}'
{
    "hash": "$6$rounds=1000$…"
}

The password is 1 to 256 bytes, without control characters. rpcd runs the method unjailed, and logs neither the password nor the hash.

docs.title: password
docs.text: Whether a hash of basic auth's password is saved, in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth: { "saved": true }. It never answers the hash.

docs.title: set_password
docs.text:
Hashes password as hash_password does, and saves the hash in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth. It then commits that config, and sends procd the config's config.change event, which reloads the service as reload_config would. It replies { "saved": true }. An empty password removes the saved hash: { "saved": false }. The reply never holds the hash.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter set_password '{"password":"…"}'
{
    "saved": true
}

Basic auth is on while the main section's auth_user is set. A hash saved without a user is unused, and a user without a hash is refused. The change applies at once, apart from any change staged in uci: neither a rollback nor uci revert undoes it.

LuCI changes and removes the password this way, with its Change password… and Remove password buttons, apart from Save & Apply. LuCI's ACL grants this method to a login that may write, and grants nothing of /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth. See LuCI app.

docs.title: For the collectors
docs.text:
Three methods give collectors data that the service's user may not be allowed to read itself. Each asks its source as root, and answers only the part the collectors read. Each takes no arguments, and answers no key, password or command line. The service's ACL allows each method while a collector that calls it is enabled. LuCI's ACL grants none of them. See About the security model.

Method Asks, as root Answers of it For wireless uci's wireless config, which holds each network's key, and its network config's interfaces; sysfs's phys Each radio's disabled, its config's channel, country and htmode, and for each of its networks the config's ssid, mesh_id and encryption, with the interface netifd names it (ifname), where netifd sets it up; { radios: {} } without a wireless config wifi, hostapd_stations wireguard_peers uci's network config, whose peer sections hold the preshared keys and whose interfaces hold the private keys The description of each wireguard_<interface> section that has one, by interface and public_key wireguard, with peer_names time_daemons procd's service list of sysntpd and of chronyd, which holds each instance's command line and environment Whether an instance of each runs its daemon, /usr/sbin/ntpd and /usr/sbin/chronyd timesync 
$ ubus call prometheus-exporter wireless
{ "radios": { "radio0": { "disabled": false, "config": { "channel": "36", "country": "DE", "htmode": "HE80" }, "interfaces": [ { "ifname": "phy0-ap0", "config": { "ssid": "example", "encryption": "sae" } } ] } } }

wireless and wireguard_peers read uci's committed configs in rpcd's own process, and ask no daemon. wireless also reads sysfs.

wireless names each network's interface as netifd does, by mac80211.sh's rules. The name is the network's ifname. Without one, it is built from:

  • the radio's ifname_prefix, or else the phy's name, with the radio's index on a phy of several radios (phy0.1-);
  • the network's mode;
  • the network's index among the radio's networks of that mode (phy0-ap1).

The phy is the radio's as wifi-scripts find it: by its path (+N for the Nth of the device's phys), by its macaddr, or by its phy.

A network that netifd does not set up has no ifname. That is a network:

  • of a disabled radio, or of a radio without a phy;
  • whose logical interfaces are all disabled or auto '0';
  • that is an MLO network.

The collectors learn whether each interface is there from nl80211, and whether it is up from sysfs.

rpcd keeps the last reply of wireless. It gives the same reply again while the phys and the two configs' files (their inode, size and times) are unchanged. A scrape calls wireless twice, for wifi and for hostapd_stations, and the configs rarely change.

time_daemons asks procd over a connection of its own, without waiting on it, so rpcd answers other calls meanwhile. A procd that does not answer costs the call 3 s, and never blocks rpcd. An rpcd that cannot defer a reply, as 25.12.0's (see status), would be held while it waited for procd. So there time_daemons asks procd nothing: it reads /proc, and a daemon runs while a process's command line starts with its program, /usr/sbin/ntpd or /usr/sbin/chronyd.

A source that cannot be asked is answered { error, message }, such as { "error": "UBUS_CALL_FAILED", "message": "service list sysntpd: Request timed out" }. The collector then fails with SOURCE_INVALID.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
error message When ARGS_INVALID main and collectors must be objects, collectors.<module> must be an object validate was given something else. ARGS_INVALID password: expected a password, password: expected a password of at most 256 bytes, password: expected a password without control characters hash_password or set_password was given a password it does not take. FILE_UNWRITABLE FILE_UNWRITABLE (cannot write /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth: ...) set_password could not save the hash. STATUS_FAILED cannot run /usr/libexec/prometheus-exporter/rpc-status.uc, ... printed no reply status could not run its scrape, or the scrape printed no reply (or was killed at 60 s). STATUS_FAILED this rpcd cannot answer a call later, ...: upgrade it (apk upgrade rpcd rpcd-mod-ucode) status was called on an rpcd that cannot defer a reply, as 25.12.0's: see status. A code CODE (detail) interfaces could not ask netifd; hash_password or set_password had no random bytes.

ubus itself refuses arguments of the wrong type, such as a string for main, with Invalid argument.

docs.title: prometheus-exporter.filesystem
docs.text:
The filesystem collector has its own object. The base package has none: the collector's package serves it from the rpcd plugin /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/prometheus-exporter-filesystem.uc.

Its one method, mounts, takes no arguments. It answers { device, mount, fstype, ro, size, free, avail, files, ffree } for each mount of the host's /proc/mounts in which statvfs() finds blocks:

  • the device, mount point and filesystem type of its line;
  • whether its options have ro;
  • its sizes, in bytes and in inodes.

statvfs() comes from luci-base's luci.core. Without it, or without /proc/mounts, mounts answers { error }.

This is all the collector asks. It cannot read the mounts from the jail, whose own mounts are not the host's, and it does not use rpcd's file read, which reads any file as root (see About the security model). Where rpcd has not loaded the plugin, the collector fails, and says so.

$ ubus call prometheus-exporter.filesystem mounts
{ "result": [ { "device": "tmpfs", "mount": "/tmp", "fstype": "tmpfs", "ro": false, "size": 122658816, "free": 122286080, "avail": 122286080, "files": 29946, "ffree": 29890 }, ... ] }

Like getMountPoints, it runs statvfs() on every mount, including a network mount that hangs, in rpcd's process.

ucode's fs module has no statvfs() on 25.12, so the plugin uses luci-base's luci.core. It requires luci.core when mounts is called, not when rpcd loads the plugin. So a luci-base without it fails the call, and leaves rpcd and its other objects working.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Over HTTP, through uhttpd-mod-ubus, a session needs the methods in its ACL. The LuCI app's ACL, luci-app-prometheus-exporter, grants collectors, interfaces, password, status and validate to read, and set_password to write. See LuCI app.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• How to troubleshoot
  • Service commands: check, which shows the same on the command line.

docs.title: UCI Configuration
docs.text: The exporter's configuration is /etc/config/prometheus-exporter, and the hash of basic auth's password is apart, in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth (below). The files are optional: every option has a default, an unset option takes it, and an option the exporter does not know is ignored. Changes apply on reload_config or service prometheus-exporter reload.

docs.title: The main section
docs.text:
config prometheus-exporter 'main'. The init script reads the first options, to start uhttpd; the exporter reads the others in each scrape.

Option Type Default Datatype Description Read by enabled boolean 1 — Run the service; 0 stops it. init script listen_interface string loopback — The logical interface uhttpd listens on, or * for every address. init script listen_port integer 9100 range(1,65535) The port uhttpd listens on. init script http_keepalive integer 70 uinteger Seconds an idle connection is kept open; 0 for none. init script cert string unset tls_file The certificate to serve HTTPS with, along with key: a file of at most 64 KiB under /etc/ssl, /etc/acme or /etc/prometheus-exporter, or uhttpd's own /etc/uhttpd.crt. init script key string unset tls_file The private key of cert, where cert may be: uhttpd's own is /etc/uhttpd.key. init script auth_user string unset username The user a scrape logs in as (basic auth), with auth_password; HTTPS only. init script memory_limit integer 0 zero_or_min(8) MB of memory each of the exporter's processes may take (its data, RLIMIT_DATA), 8 or more: a collector that takes more fails alone. 0 for a quarter of the RAM, at most 64 MB. init script omit_zero_values boolean 0 — Leave out counters that are 0, most of which never move on a router. exporter compress boolean 1 — Send a scrape gzip-compressed when the scraper asks for it (Accept-Encoding: gzip); 0 never does. exporter exec_timeout integer 5 range(1,30) Seconds the programs a collector runs get in all in each scrape, unless the collector says otherwise; one still running then is killed. exporter scrape_timeout integer 10 range(1,60) Seconds a scrape has to answer when the scraper does not say (X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds); collectors left when they are nearly spent are skipped. exporter collector_budget integer 5 range(1,60) Seconds a collector may take in a scrape, unless it says otherwise; one still running then is stopped, and quarantined for a few scrapes. exporter max_samples integer 20000 range(1,100000) Samples a collector may write in a scrape, unless it says otherwise; one that writes more fails, and none of its samples are served. exporter max_scrape_samples integer 200000 range(1,1000000) Samples the collectors of a scrape may write in all; a collector whose samples would go past it fails, and none of its samples are served. exporter

Options that go together, checked wherever the configuration is checked (start, reload, check, the ubus object's validate and LuCI):

  • auth_user without auth_password: basic auth needs the hash of a password along with auth_user.
  • auth_user without cert and key: basic auth needs HTTPS: set cert and key, or the password crosses the network in the clear.
  • auth_password without auth_user is no basic auth: the hash stays saved, unused.

docs.title: Basic auth's hash
docs.text:
config auth 'main' in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth, which the package installs, mode 0600. It is apart so that LuCI's ACL, which grants reading the exporter's config, never grants the hash: the ubus object's set_password writes it, and password says whether one is saved. The init script reads it, and the jail does not mount it. A change reloads the service, as one of the main section does.

Option Type Default Datatype Description Read by auth_password string unset crypt The crypt hash of the password of auth_user: $1$ (uhttpd -m), $5$ or $6$, as the ubus object's hash_password makes it. init script

docs.title: Collector sections
docs.text:
config collector '<module>', one per collector, named after its module: the collector's name with _ for - (ltq_dsl for ltq-dsl), as a uci section name cannot hold -. A collector without a section runs with its defaults. A section that names no installed collector, and one without a name, is ignored (check warns of both). Besides its own options, listed in Collectors, every collector has these:

Option Title Type Default Datatype Description enabled Enabled boolean 1 — Serve this collector; 0 leaves it out, and naming it in a query is a 400. timeout Program timeout integer the collector's meta.timeout, else exec_timeout (5) range(1,30) Seconds the programs of this collector get in all in each scrape; one still running then is killed. budget Budget integer collector_budget (5), or the collector's timeout and a second more when that is longer range(1,60) Seconds this collector may take in a scrape; one still running then is stopped, and quarantined for a few scrapes. max_samples Sample limit integer the collector's meta.max_samples, else max_samples (20000) range(1,100000) Samples this collector may write in a scrape; one that writes more fails, and none of its samples are served.

timeout is only for a collector that runs programs (exec in its needs); the others ignore it. A collector still running at the end of its budget is stopped and quarantined, and one that writes more than its max_samples fails: see Collector contract and About deadlines and circuit breakers. No collector may declare an option named enabled, timeout, budget, max_samples.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
A boolean takes 1, yes, on, true, enabled for true and 0, no, off, false, disabled for false. An integer is decimal digits, with an optional -. A string is a single value, not a list. A datatype narrows what an option takes, by the name LuCI gives it; the exporter checks it itself:

Datatype Takes crypt a crypt hash: $1$ (uhttpd -m), $5$ or $6$ file an absolute path ipaddr an IPv4 or IPv6 address owned_directory a directory under /var, /tmp or /etc/prometheus-exporter, and not under /var/run or /tmp/run, which the service makes and mounts range(1,100000) an integer from 1 to 100000 range(1,1000000) an integer from 1 to 1000000 range(1,30) an integer from 1 to 30 range(1,60) an integer from 1 to 60 range(1,65535) an integer from 1 to 65535 regex a regular expression tls_file a file under /etc/ssl, /etc/acme or /etc/prometheus-exporter, or uhttpd's own, /etc/uhttpd.* uinteger an integer of 0 or more username a user of 1 to 64 characters, without ":", spaces or control characters zero_or_min(8) 0, or an integer of 8 or more

directory and file check the path's form, not that it exists. A value an option does not take is CONFIG_INVALID: in the main section it stops start and reload, and in a collector's section that collector fails in each scrape. See Error codes.

docs.title: What is wrong with a value
docs.text:
What the exporter finds wrong with a value, or with options that go together, has a code of its own, from src/prometheus/exporter/config/problems.uc, and arguments. The ubus object's validate answers the code and its arguments, for a client to say in its own words, as LuCI does, and the English below as message (see ubus object). The details of a CONFIG_INVALID, in the log, check and the command line, are that English after the option's name: listen_port: expected an integer from 1 to 65535, got 0. value is what the exporter read, but for a secret option's (auth_password).

Code Arguments English BOOLEAN value expected a boolean, got value INTEGER value expected an integer, got value SINGLE value expected a single value, got value RANGE min, max, value expected an integer from min to max, got value UINTEGER value expected an integer of 0 or more, got value ZERO_OR_MIN min, value expected 0, or an integer of min or more, got value ABSOLUTE_PATH value expected an absolute path, got value OWNED_DIRECTORY value expected a directory under /var, /tmp or /etc/prometheus-exporter, and not under /var/run or /tmp/run, which the service makes and mounts, got value TLS_PATH value expected a file under /etc/ssl, /etc/acme or /etc/prometheus-exporter, or uhttpd's own, /etc/uhttpd.*, got value TLS_FILE max, value expected a regular file of at most max bytes, which its links, if any, leave under /etc/ssl, /etc/acme, /etc/prometheus-exporter or /etc/uhttpd.*, got value REGEX value expected a regular expression, got value IPADDR value expected an IPv4 or IPv6 address, got value USERNAME value expected a user of 1 to 64 characters, without ":", spaces or control characters, got value CRYPT value expected a crypt hash: $1$ (uhttpd -m), $5$ or $6$, got value CRYPT_ROUNDS max, value expected a hash of at most max rounds, which a scrape computes to check the password (hash_password makes one of 1000; one without rounds= has 5000), got value INTERFACE value expected an interface name or *, got value AUTH_NEEDS_PASSWORD — basic auth needs the hash of a password along with auth_user AUTH_NEEDS_TLS — basic auth needs HTTPS: set cert and key, or the password crosses the network in the clear

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
config prometheus-exporter 'main'
    option enabled '1'
    option listen_interface 'loopback'
    option listen_port '9100'
    option http_keepalive '70'
    option memory_limit '0'
    option omit_zero_values '0'
    option compress '1'
    option exec_timeout '5'
    option scrape_timeout '10'
    option collector_budget '5'
    option max_samples '20000'
    option max_scrape_samples '200000'

config collector 'textfile'
    option enabled '1'
    option directory '/var/prometheus'

With basic auth, auth_user in the main section above, and in /etc/config/prometheus-exporter-auth:

config auth 'main'
    option auth_password '$6$rounds=1000$...'

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Lessons to follow from start to end, by doing. Each starts from nothing and ends with something working.

Tutorial For You will Monitor a router with Prometheus Operators Install the exporter on an OpenWrt router, open it to the LAN, scrape it with Prometheus and graph the router. Write your first collector Collector authors and maintainers Write, run, test and package a collector, and see it served by OpenWrt in the lab.

docs.title: Write Your First Collector
docs.text:
In this tutorial we will write a collector, tasks, that counts the kernel's tasks from /proc/loadavg. We will run it on the command line, test it, package it, and see OpenWrt serve it in the lab, in LuCI and at /metrics. Along the way we will meet the development environment: make shell, make test, the devkit's with_collector, make docs-gen and make lab.

It takes about half an hour, mostly waiting for builds. This collector is practice, so at the end we will remove what we made.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A checkout of the repository, and a terminal in it.
  • Docker, and make. Everything else runs in containers.
  • About 3 GB of disk for the images, the first time.

docs.title: 1. Run the tests
docs.text:
First, make sure everything works before we change anything:

make test

The first run builds the development image, based on OpenWrt's own, which takes a minute or two. Then the tests run, and the last lines say how they went:

Summary:

  1146 successes / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped / 0 ignored (49301 ms)

Your numbers will differ. What matters is 0 failures.

docs.title: 2. Look at the source
docs.text:
Our collector will read the fourth field of /proc/loadavg. Let's look at the file in the development image:

make shell

cat /proc/loadavg

0.72 0.61 0.97 2/3199 81234

The fourth field, 2/3199, gives the tasks that are runnable now and the tasks that exist. Leave the shell with exit.

docs.title: 3. Write the collector
docs.text:
Create src/prometheus/collectors/tasks.uc:

'use strict';

import { Result, errors, proc } from 'prometheus.exporter';

export const meta = {
    name: 'tasks',
    title: 'Scheduler tasks',
    help: 'Runnable and existing tasks, from /proc/loadavg.',
    needs: [ 'fs' ],
};

export function collect(deps, out) {
    let line = proc.first_line(deps.fs, '/proc/loadavg');

    if (line == null)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_UNREADABLE, '/proc/loadavg');

    let counts = split(proc.fields(line)[3] ?? '', '/');

    if (length(counts) != 2)
        return Result.err(errors.SOURCE_INVALID, `/proc/loadavg: ${line}`);

    out.gauge('node_tasks_runnable', 'Tasks that are runnable now.')(null, counts[0]);
    out.gauge('node_tasks', 'Tasks that exist now.')(null, counts[1]);

    return Result.ok();
};

Notice four things:

  • The collector imports one module, prometheus.exporter, the collector API. Everything it uses from the exporter comes from there.
  • meta.needs asks for fs, and collect reads the file through deps.fs, not by importing fs. A collector only gets what it asks for, and the exporter refuses a collector that imports anything else.
  • out.gauge declares a family, and returns a function that records a sample.
  • collect returns a Result: Result.ok() when it worked, or Result.err() with a code when it did not.

docs.title: 4. Run it
docs.text:
Back in the development image:

make shell

ucode -L /exporter/src files/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter scrape -d src/prometheus/collectors tasks

This runs the exporter's own command from the source tree. It loads the collectors from src/, and runs only ours. It prints a scrape:

# HELP node_tasks_runnable Tasks that are runnable now.
# TYPE node_tasks_runnable gauge
node_tasks_runnable 2
# HELP node_tasks Tasks that exist now.
# TYPE node_tasks gauge
node_tasks 3199
# HELP node_scrape_collector_duration_seconds node_exporter: Duration of a collector scrape.
...
node_scrape_collector_success{collector="tasks"} 1
...
ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="dev"} 1

Our two families come first. Then come the metrics every scrape writes about each collector that ran: ours succeeded. The version is dev, since it runs from a source tree.

Now let the exporter check our module against the rules it holds every collector to. This is the check you would run before anyone installs a collector:

ucode -L /exporter/src files/usr/bin/prometheus-exporter collector check src/prometheus/collectors/tasks.uc

ok   strict mode: 'use strict' first
ok   imports: prometheus.exporter alone
ok   top level: declarations alone
ok   load: 0.001 s, of at most 5 s
ok   meta: tasks (Scheduler tasks), needs fs, budget 5 s, max_samples 20000
ok   run: 0.000 s, 2 samples in 2 families
ok   families: node_tasks_runnable node_tasks
ok   exposition: valid text, each series once

Every line is ok. Our collector:

  • imports the API alone,
  • only declares at its top level,
  • loads quickly,
  • has a valid meta,
  • ran in its own process, well within its budget, and
  • wrote two families that no installed collector writes.

If it had looped, or written node_load1, a line would say FAIL, and why. Leave the shell with exit.

docs.title: 5. Test it
docs.text:
Tests run the collector the way a scrape does, with fakes in place of the system. The devkit's with_collector provides them. It is the same tool that tests a collector in another package. Create test/unit/prometheus/collectors/tasks_test.uc:

'use strict';

import { describe, it, assert } from 'utest';
import { with_collector } from 'prometheus.exporter.devkit.collector';
import * as tasks from 'prometheus.collectors.tasks';

describe('collectors.tasks', () => {
    it('counts the runnable and the existing tasks', () => {
        with_collector(tasks, { fs: { data: { '/proc/loadavg': '0.08 0.03 0.00 2/131 4567\n' } } }, (r) => {
            assert.match(true, r.result.ok);
            assert.match([
                '# HELP node_tasks_runnable Tasks that are runnable now.',
                '# TYPE node_tasks_runnable gauge',
                'node_tasks_runnable 2',
                '# HELP node_tasks Tasks that exist now.',
                '# TYPE node_tasks gauge',
                'node_tasks 131',
            ], r.lines);
        });
    });

    it('fails with SOURCE_UNREADABLE when /proc/loadavg cannot be read', () => {
        with_collector(tasks, { fs: { data: { '/proc/loadavg': null } } }, (r) => {
            assert.match('SOURCE_UNREADABLE', r.result.error);
            assert.match([ "collector 'tasks': SOURCE_UNREADABLE (/proc/loadavg)" ], r.logs);
        });
    });
});

with_collector hands the collector an fs that answers from data, and runs it. It gives us what the collector wrote: r.result, r.lines, and r.logs, which is what the scrape would log. The second test hands the collector a file that cannot be read.

with_collector also behaves as the exporter's jail would. If our collector read a file outside /proc and /sys without declaring it, the test would fail, and say so. Run only these tests:

make unit MODULES=test/unit/prometheus/collectors/tasks_test.uc

  2 successes / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped / 0 ignored (90 ms)

docs.title: 6. Package it
docs.text:
Now the whole suite:

make test

It fails, as it should. Among its output:

    ■ docs_gen.main.run > finds the notes and the code in agreement
        Expected 0 elements, got 1
...
    ■ collectors > tasks > is in the generated reference
        run make docs-gen: docs/reference/collectors.md has no tasks
    ■ collectors > tasks > is packaged once: in the base package or as its own, named after it
        tasks: base false, subpackage null

test/integration/collectors_test.uc checks that the repository gives every collector what it needs, such as a package and a reference entry. The documentation's generator also finds a collector in no package. Ours has no package yet. Open openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile, find the Collector lines, and add ours after sockstat's:

$(eval $(call Collector,tasks,tasks,scheduler tasks,))

That makes a package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-tasks. Then regenerate the reference pages, which are written from the code:

make docs-gen

wrote docs/reference/collectors.md
wrote docs/reference/error-codes.md
wrote docs/reference/metrics.md

Open docs/reference/metrics.md and find the tasks section. Our two families are there, with their type and help. The generator ran our collector on the captures of real routers in test/fixtures/, and wrote down what it produced. Now run the tests again:

make test

The summary says 0 failures again.

docs.title: 7. See it on OpenWrt
docs.text:
The lab is OpenWrt under procd, in a container, with every package installed. Start it:

make lab

It builds the packages with OpenWrt's SDK, which takes a few minutes the first time. Then it boots OpenWrt and installs them. It ends with:

The lab runs, as container ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab:
  LuCI      http://127.0.0.1:8080/  (root, no password)
  /metrics  http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics
  a shell   docker exec -it ucode-prometheus-exporter-lab ash
  stop it   make lab-down

Ask it for our collector:

curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics?collect[]=tasks' | grep '^node_tasks'

node_tasks_runnable 2
node_tasks 3255

Our collector counted these, in the exporter's jail, under procd. The numbers are your computer's: a container shares its host's kernel, and so its /proc/loadavg.

Now open http://127.0.0.1:8080/ and log in as root with no password. Go to Services → Prometheus exporter, tab Collectors. You see a row Scheduler tasks, with our help text and its package, ucode-prometheus-exporter-tasks. On Status → Prometheus exporter, it shows OK.

docs.title: 8. Clean up
docs.text:
Stop the lab:

make lab-down

Then remove what we made, since this collector was practice:

rm src/prometheus/collectors/tasks.uc test/unit/prometheus/collectors/tasks_test.uc
git checkout openwrt/ucode-prometheus-exporter/Makefile
make docs-gen

docs.title: What we did
docs.text: We wrote a collector that asks for one capability and writes two families. We ran it on the command line, checked that it keeps the collector contract, and tested it with the devkit's fakes. We gave it a package, generated its reference, and saw OpenWrt serve it in its jail and list it in LuCI.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Collector interface: every field of meta, every capability, out and the Results.
  • Collector contract: what the exporter enforces on a collector, and what breaking a rule costs.
  • About nothing to observe: when a collector should answer Result.none.
  • How to capture fixtures from a device: to test on what a real router answers.
  • How to package a collector and How to run the benchmark.
  • How to write a collector in your own package: the same, outside the exporter's tree.

docs.title: Monitor a Router with Prometheus
docs.text:
In this tutorial we will install the exporter on an OpenWrt router and look at its metrics on the router itself. Then we will open it to the LAN, and have a Prometheus on our computer scrape it and graph the router's load and traffic. Along the way we will meet the service's status and check commands, which tell us what the exporter is doing.

flowchart LR
    subgraph router [Router]
        C[collectors] --> E["exporter<br/>port 9100, /metrics"]
    end
    subgraph computer [Our computer]
        P[Prometheus] --> G[graphs]
    end
    E -- "scraped over the LAN" --> P

It takes about twenty minutes.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A router on OpenWrt 25.12, at 192.168.1.1 on its LAN, with internet access, and a shell on it: ssh root@192.168.1.1.
  • A computer on the router's LAN, with Docker.

If your router's address is not 192.168.1.1, use yours wherever it appears.

Where a step can be done in LuCI too, it shows two tabs: Browser (LuCI) and Terminal (SSH). Follow either. The LuCI steps need LuCI on the router, at http://192.168.1.1/.

docs.title: 1. Install the exporter
docs.text:
On the router, over SSH, add the exporter's feed and the key that signs its packages:

feed=https://m00qek.github.io/packages.ucode.dev/25.12
wget -qO /etc/apk/keys/packages.ucode.dev.pem "$feed/feed.pub.pem"
echo "$feed" > /etc/apk/repositories.d/ucode-dev.list

Now install the exporter, and its LuCI app. apk fetches their dependencies from that feed and from OpenWrt's own feeds:

Browser (LuCI)Terminal (SSH)
  1. Open System → Software and press Update lists….
  2. Type prometheus-exporter in Filter.
  3. On the Available tab, press Install… on the row of ucode-prometheus-exporter, then Install in the dialog.
  4. Do the same for luci-app-prometheus-exporter, then reload the browser page.
apk update
apk add ucode-prometheus-exporter luci-app-prometheus-exporter

apk lists what it installs, and ends with OK.

The service starts on its own. Let's ask it how it is doing:

Browser (LuCI)Terminal (SSH)

Open Status → Prometheus exporter. Under Service, State says Running, and Metrics says http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics (reachable from the router only).

service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 16 collectors

Notice where it listens: 127.0.0.1, the router's loopback. For now only the router itself can reach it.

docs.title: 2. Look at the metrics
docs.text:
Still on the router, over SSH, ask for a scrape, as Prometheus will:

wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep '^node_load'

node_load1 0.08
node_load5 0.03
node_load15 0

These are the router's load averages. Now the last lines of the scrape:

wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | tail -n 4

node_scrape_collector_observing{collector="vmstat"} 1
# HELP ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info A metric with a constant '1' value labeled by the version of ucode-prometheus-exporter.
# TYPE ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info gauge
ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{version="0.2.0-r1"} 1

Every scrape ends with metrics about the scrape itself: how long each collector took, whether it succeeded, and the exporter's version.

docs.title: 3. Open it to the LAN
docs.text:
Our computer is on the LAN, so we make the exporter listen there:

Browser (LuCI)Terminal (SSH)
  1. Open Services → Prometheus exporter, tab General.
  2. Pick lan in Listen on, and press Save & Apply.
  3. Open Status → Prometheus exporter. Metrics now says http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics.
uci set prometheus-exporter.main.listen_interface=lan
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload
service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 16 collectors

The address is now the router's LAN address. From the computer, check that the exporter answers:

curl -s http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics | grep '^node_load1'

node_load1 0.08

docs.title: 4. Scrape it with Prometheus
docs.text:
On the computer, make a directory for Prometheus, and in it a file prometheus.yml:

global:
  scrape_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: openwrt
    static_configs:
      - targets: [ '192.168.1.1:9100' ]

Start Prometheus in Docker, with that file:

docker run --rm -d --name prometheus -p 9090:9090 \
    -v "$PWD/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro" prom/prometheus

Open http://localhost:9090/targets. After a few seconds, the openwrt job's target, http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, shows UP. If it shows DOWN with connection refused, the exporter is still on loopback: go back to step 3.

docs.title: 5. Graph the router
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:9090/query, type this expression, and press Execute:

node_load1

You see one series: the router's one-minute load. Switch to the Graph tab to see it over time.

Now the traffic the router receives, in bytes per second, for each network device:

rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total[1m])

You see one series per device, labeled device. Give it a few minutes: rate needs several scrapes.

Last, ask which version runs there:

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info

ucode_prometheus_exporter_build_info{instance="192.168.1.1:9100", job="openwrt", version="0.2.0-r1"}  1

docs.title: 6. Ask the exporter how it is doing
docs.text:
Back on the router, over SSH:

service prometheus-exporter check

The first lines are its findings, something like this:

ok   main: HTTP on interface lan, port 9100, keepalive 70s, exec_timeout 5s, scrape_timeout 10s, collector_budget 5s, max_samples 20000, memory_limit 64 MB (a quarter of the RAM, at most 64), gzip when asked
ok   collectors: 16 installed collectors, their options valid
ok   scrape, in the service's jail: 16 of 16 collectors succeeded

Then comes one block per collector, with what the collector reads and what the service's jail gives it. Last comes everything the jail mounts. Each ok is a check that passed. A problem would show as a warn or FAIL line that says what is wrong.

In LuCI, Status → Prometheus exporter shows the same scrape as a table: one row per collector, each OK in Test run.

Now let's watch a collector go. Switch off softnet, the network softirq statistics:

Browser (LuCI)Terminal (SSH)
  1. Open Services → Prometheus exporter, tab Collectors.
  2. Untick Network softirq statistics in the Enabled column, and press Save & Apply.
  3. The tab now says 15 of 16 collectors enabled.
uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet=collector
uci set prometheus-exporter.softnet.enabled=0
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload
service prometheus-exporter status

running
listening on http://192.168.1.1:9100/metrics, gzip when asked, serving 15 collectors

It serves one collector fewer. In Prometheus, node_softnet_processed_total stops getting new samples. Switch it back on:

Browser (LuCI)Terminal (SSH)

Tick Network softirq statistics again, and press Save & Apply. The tab says 16 of 16 collectors enabled.

uci delete prometheus-exporter.softnet
uci commit prometheus-exporter
service prometheus-exporter reload

docs.title: 7. Clean up
docs.text:
Stop Prometheus on the computer:

docker stop prometheus

The exporter keeps running on the router, listening on the LAN.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text: We installed the exporter, read a scrape on the router, opened the exporter to the LAN, had Prometheus scrape it, and graphed the router's load and traffic. We asked the service for its status and its check, and saw it stop serving one collector and then serve it again.
